Both calculations concern an isotropic planar five-dimensional charged AdS background and its transverse shear fluctuation. Restrict this comparison to the zero-spatial-momentum, low-frequency prescription at a regular nonextremal horizon.

required_assumptions.statement: Impose the stated common-action coupling restrictions and retain only first order in the perturbative parameter χ.
Use r0>0 and x=q²/r0⁶<2, with 2−x held positive as χ tends to zero, so the comparison does not require an interchange of the extremal and low-frequency limits.

Compare the separately reported canonical-momentum horizon formulas in the same displayed quadratic-action basis. The right source supplies the conservation and infalling implementation; an independent derivation of these conditions for the left calculation is not asserted.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The common-action restrictions are explicit algebraic choices within the displayed actions. They produce the same Weyl-squared invariant without a field redefinition and contain no derivatives of curvature.
The supplied metric ansätze and zeroth-order temperature formulas support the selected planar nonextremal background sector.
The displayed quadratic actions have the same six monomial structures, and the two reported horizon formulas have matching kernels after the metric and gravitational-normalization substitutions.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left appendix also permits a Weyl–Maxwell interaction, whereas the right toy model excludes higher-derivative Maxwell terms. This interaction is set to zero in the asserted overlap.

The left appendix gives a leading-order calculation using the zeroth-order background. The right calculation retains curvature-cubed and quadratic four-derivative-coupling contributions and uses corrected metric data. Those higher-order applications are excluded.
The left main-text Riemann-squared action and its appendix Weyl-squared action are distinct. The asserted overlap uses the appendix action.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the displayed five-dimensional bulk theories in unit AdS-radius conventions and each source's unit-boundary-speed frame. No conversion of dimensionful transport coefficients between unnormalized time coordinates is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The left sets the AdS radius and boundary speed to one.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The right sets the uncorrected AdS radius to one and describes the time rescaling needed for unit boundary speed.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify κ_L²=8πG_R and choose −2Λ_R=12 in the common action. The gravitational constant κ_L² is distinct from the horizon kernels denoted κ2 and κ4.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The bulk action carries 1/(2κ_L²), with Einstein term R+12.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The bulk action carries 1/(16πG_R), with Einstein term R−2Λ_R.

conventionDictionary.concept: Common curvature invariant and coupling names
conventionDictionary.conversion: Set χ=c1_L, c2_L=0; b2_R=χ, b1_R=−5χ/6, b3_R=8χ/3, c1_R=c2_R=0. Then the right quadratic curvature correction is χ[Riemann²−(4/3)Ricci²+R²/6]=χ Weyl². Identically named c_i across papers are not identified.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Appendix c1_L multiplies Weyl²; c2_L multiplies a Weyl–Maxwell interaction.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The b_i multiply curvature-squared invariants, while c1_R and c2_R multiply curvature-cubed invariants.

conventionDictionary.concept: Radial metric and positive exterior root
conventionDictionary.conversion: With left c_metric(r)=r, set Ω_R=r²a² and σ_R=a/b. Then U≡sqrt(−g_rr/g_tt)=σ_R/Ω_R=1/(r²ab), taking the positive exterior root. Here Ω_R renames the right metric function ω(r), avoiding confusion with frequency.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: g_tt=−r²a², g_rr=1/(r²b²), and g_xx=c_metric².
conventionDictionary.right_definition: g_tt=−Ω_R, g_rr=σ_R²/Ω_R, and g_xx=r².

conventionDictionary.concept: Shear mode, Fourier convention and quadratic coefficients
conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the mixed-index shear field φ and use [dk]=d⁴k/(2π)⁴. A through F denote coefficients of the same displayed monomials, not higher-derivative couplings. Primes denote d/dr.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: h^y_x is expanded as φ_k(r)exp(−iωt+ikz); the quadratic action contains Aφ''φ, Bφ'φ', Cφ'φ, Dφφ, Eφ''φ'', Fφ''φ' and a boundary term.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The same mixed-index field and Fourier sign appear, with the same quadratic monomial basis and boundary terms.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both separately report η=lim Π/(iωφ). With K2=U(A−B+F'/2) and K4=(EU')', the left η=(K2+K4)/κ_L² and right η=(K2+K4)/(8πG_R) coincide under the dictionary. Image:2 resolves the left derivatives and prefactor in equations (32)–(33).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equations (29), (32) and (33) give the boundary momentum ratio and its horizon expression.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equations (3.9)–(3.13) report low-frequency momentum conservation, infalling conditions and the horizon expression.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the named Wald prescription and reported entropy densities. Their Einstein terms agree: 2πr0³/κ_L²=r0³/(4G_R). The right's explicit binormal normalization is recorded; an independently verified left binormal definition is not asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The appendix invokes Wald's formula and reports the density in (35) and (39), without an explicit binormal normalization in the supplied appendix text.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equations (3.16)–(3.18) use −2π times the horizon integral of ∂L/∂R contracted with two binormals, with ε_μν ε^μν=−2; entropy is divided by planar spatial volume. Image:5 confirms the sign and normalization.

conventionDictionary.concept: Charge parameters, horizon scheme and perturbative order
conventionDictionary.conversion: For the ratio check identify q_L²=q_R² and x=q²/r0⁶. The right's bar-x=bar-q² equals x+O(χ), so replacing bar-x by x in an already O(χ) correction changes only O(χ²). No signed gauge-potential identification is needed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The appendix uses q²/r0⁶ and retains first order in its higher-derivative couplings.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Tilde-q=q/r0³ uses the fixed horizon radius; bar-q=q/bar-r0³ uses the parameter introduced to compare at fixed physical temperature.

limitations: This is a comparison of supplied reported procedures and a restricted algebraic check, not a reproduction of either complete transport derivation. Earlier review conclusions and node certainty labels are not scientific premises.

endpoints.text: Evaluate the perturbative Repulsive Force Condition, including scalar attraction, for candidate charged string excitations. Separately count KK species using N∼k^n for n decompactifying dimensions and Λsp²=MPl²/Nsp to compare gravitational and string scales.

Evaluate the Repulsive Force Conjecture using the inverse gauge kinetic matrix and scalar metric, including gravitational and scalar-mediated attraction. The heterotic excitation mass includes both string tension and a charge-dependent Coulomb-branch shift.

records.exactAssertion: Right → left, analogy_only: the right's five-dimensional Type K3 RFC calculation is a procedural analogue of the left's four-dimensional RFC calculation and cutoff applicability assessment. Both compare gauge repulsion against gravitational and scalar attraction using their source-defined candidate masses, and assess when a particle description is gravitationally controlled. This assertion concerns the displayed procedures, including the left's explicitly hypothetical noncritical spectrum. It excludes equality of physical results across dimensions, a compactification or field-space identification, demonstrated use of the left paper's method by the right, transfer of the four-dimensional KK species formula, and universal existence of either candidate spectrum.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints evaluate self-repulsion by comparing gauge repulsion with gravitational and scalar-mediated attraction, using derivatives of the candidate particle mass.

The shared applicability criterion is controlled particle physics below the gravitational cutoff. This is a methodological intersection, not a demonstrated common compactification or spacetime regime.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare the displayed RFC tests in their respective dimensions and source-defined metric normalizations; do not identify their physical fields, charges or Planck masses.
Treat the left's critical-string-like spectrum for noncritical strings as an explicit hypothetical ansatz. Comparing that calculation does not establish the existence of those particles.
Restrict the right-hand algebraic check to the stated Type K3 asymptotics, candidate charges satisfying Q_i η^{ij} Q_j = −2n_L, and n_L ≫ a. Retain the Coulomb-branch mass contribution.
Interpret the left's KK species count as a KK-only estimate until competing towers have been assessed; do not transfer its four-dimensional species formula to five dimensions.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Images image:1 and image:4 explicitly display d = 4 and d = 5, respectively, and identify the scalar terms as attractive contributions.
The left explicitly labels the spectrum assumption and subsequently tests its particle interpretation. The comparison preserves that conditional status.
The right explicitly supplies the charge-level condition, large-level approximation, Coulomb contribution and asymptotic volume relation used in the restricted check.

Both sources discuss whether string excitations admit a particle interpretation relative to the gravitational cutoff; neither source's discussion is being substituted for a cutoff calculation in the other setting.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left concerns four-dimensional F-theory open-string gauge sectors; the right concerns five-dimensional M-theory compactifications. The gravitational coefficients are consequently 1/2 and 2/3.

The left's candidate mass ansatz is proportional to string tension and excitation level. The right includes an additional charge-dependent Coulomb-branch contribution; its scalar derivatives cannot be replaced by those of the tension term alone.

The left endpoint explicitly counts KK species. The supplied right endpoint uses the quantum-gravity cutoff and particle applicability but does not establish use of that particular KK-counting calculation.

conventionDictionary.concept: Dimension, Planck units and gauge normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: Write M_4 and M_5 for the respective Planck masses and μ_d = M_particle²/M_d². Define C_4 = g_YM,4² q_k² and C_5 = (M_5 g_5²) Q_α f^{αβ} Q_β. Both C_d/μ_d are dimensionless. The five-dimensional gauge coupling squared has inverse-mass dimension, whereas the four-dimensional one is dimensionless. No equality between M_4 and M_5 or compactification/frame conversion is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (3.7) uses g_YM² q_k²/M_k² and the four-dimensional Planck mass.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (3.3) uses (M_Pl g_5²)(Q_α f^{αβ} Q_β)/(M_k²/M_Pl²); f^{αβ} is the inverse dimensionless gauge kinetic matrix.

conventionDictionary.conversion: In each source's own coordinates, the normalized test is C_d/μ_d ≥ A_d + Y_d, where A_d = (d−3)/(d−2) and Y_d = G_d^{IJ}(∂_I μ_d)(∂_J μ_d)/(4μ_d²). Thus A_4 = 1/2 and A_5 = 2/3. G_4^{rs} and G_5^{AB} denote the respective inverse scalar metrics, not an identified metric. Images image:1 and image:4 resolve the plus sign and factor 1/4.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Scalar coordinates φ^r and inverse metric g^{rs}; gravity and Yukawa terms appear on the attractive side of (3.7).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Independent vector-multiplet scalars Φ^A and inverse metric g^{AB}; the same force signs occur in (3.3).

conventionDictionary.conversion: The right additionally rewrites its scalar term as (f^{αβ}−v̂^α v̂^β/3)(∂_α μ_5)(∂_β μ_5)/(2μ_5²), as displayed in (3.4). Image image:4 fixes the subtraction and coefficients. This is a right-specific coordinate representation; no corresponding special-geometry identity is imposed on the left.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The general inverse scalar metric enters the RFC; the primitive-string evaluation uses the tension's scalar dependence.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: v̂^α = v^α/V^(1/3), subject to the normalized cubic volume constraint; f^{αβ} enters the scalar-coordinate rewrite.

conventionDictionary.concept: Charges, excitation levels and the unrelated symbol q
conventionDictionary.conversion: Rename the left's geometric label q_top to distinguish it from particle charge q_k. Image image:3 confirms ξ = 1+q_top and the critical heterotic identification at q_top = 0. Image image:5 confirms the minus sign in n_L = −Q_i η^{ij}Q_j/2. The latter lattice quadratic form is not identified with q_k²; n_k and n_L are separate excitation labels.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: q_top ∈ {0,1,2} labels primitive string types; q_k² = 4m n_k, with m = C^0·S/2 > 0.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Q_i are lattice charges; the candidate subset satisfies Q_i η^{ij}Q_j = −2n_L.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both tensions have mass-squared units. On the right define Ω = 16π²(4π)^(−2/3), H = V̂_K3 and B = (Q_i v̂^i)²/(4n_L). For n_L ≫ a, μ_5 ≃ Ω n_L(H+B). The shift is Δ_CB/M_5² = Ω(Q_i v̂^i)²/4 and is independent of n_L at fixed charge. Image image:5 resolves the parentheses in (5.35). No equality of the two spectra is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The assumed spectrum is M_k² = 8π T_EFT(n_k−a). Its noncritical application is explicitly hypothetical.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M_nL,Q² = 8π(n_L−a)T_s + Δ_CB, with a = 1; the shift is fixed by matching the n_L = a modes to M2-brane masses.

conventionDictionary.concept: KK species estimate and effective weak coupling
conventionDictionary.conversion: The left gives Λ_sp,KK²/M_4² ∼ (M_KK²/M_4²)^[n/(n+2)], obtained from the four-dimensional species rule and KK counting. Image image:2 resolves the exponent n/(2+n). The right instead explicitly defines effective weak coupling through Λ_WGC²/Λ_QG² → 0. These provide comparable applicability checks, not an equality of cutoffs or a five-dimensional species formula.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: N_KK ∼ k^n for n decompactifying dimensions; Λ_sp² = M_4²/N_sp. Competing string towers must be checked before interpreting Λ_sp,KK as the actual cutoff.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Λ_QG is where gravity becomes strongly coupled; Λ_WGC² = g_YM² M_5³. The discussion relates sub-species-scale excitation masses to a particle description.

The leading right-hand cancellation was reconstructed, but the finite-vacuum-energy correction in (5.43) was only read as a source report, not independently derived (ad905cd2e07e4e024a5a:p0038s001).

No universal tower-existence result is certified. The right records qualifications concerning parent geometries, Type II/III degenerations and its treatment of Type T4 limits (ad905cd2e07e4e024a5a:p0036s001; ad905cd2e07e4e024a5a:p0044s001; image:6).

Image:6 reports an analogy with four-dimensional results cited as [27]. The supplied packet does not identify that bibliography entry, so the proposed edge is reconstructed from the endpoint equations rather than attributed to that numbered citation.
A stronger equivalence or dimensional-reduction claim would require an explicit map of compactifications, scalar metrics, charges, Planck normalizations and cutoffs. Such a claim is excluded here.

endpoints.text: Use the attractor mechanism and fake-superpotential gradient flows for static, spherically symmetric black holes. A nonnegative sum-of-squares rewriting bounds the ADM mass, assuming suitable horizon behavior, and identifies extremal flow solutions.

Complete squares in a radial functional whose on-shell value is the spherical black-hole ADM mass. A globally admissible mass function satisfying the force inequality gives a lower bound; associated first-order gradient flows characterize saturation limits.

records.exactAssertion: The left endpoint's displayed fake-superpotential radial mass-bound construction specializes the right endpoint's general radial square-completion construction: set d=5, use the stated normalization dictionary, and impose zero residual through the left PDE (3.5). The radial functionals, ADM masses, completed squares, boundary bounds and f=1 first-order flow equations then coincide. This is a conditional algebraic relation between methods, restricted to scalar domains containing all compared profiles, the stated smooth-horizon boundary conditions, and, for regular saturation, admissible flows ending at positive interior critical points. It does not assert existence of W in a new vacuum, equivalence of full EFT actions or string vacua, global uniqueness, treatment of singular limiting horizons or finite-distance transitions, or transfer of BPS, particle-spectrum or sublattice-WGC conclusions.

intersection.statement: The displayed radial methods overlap for static, spherically symmetric, purely electric configurations in five spacetime dimensions. This uses the right paper's general-dimension radial equations, independently of its bosonic-string theorem.

The comparison applies on a smooth scalar domain containing every exterior profile being compared, with a real sufficiently differentiable W satisfying the left PDE, positive kinetic metrics, and horizon conditions that remove the displayed boundary terms. The left PDE selects the equality case of the right residual inequality.

For saturation, the assertion is restricted to admissible f=1 flows approaching a positive interior critical point of W. Both sources describe this regular-horizon branch. Existence of such a W or attractor in a particular vacuum is not asserted.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare the displayed radial equations at d=5, identifying the radial metric fields and electric charge components through the dictionary below. Couplings are constant normalization parameters with positive gravitational and gauge kinetic signs.

W is real and sufficiently differentiable for the PDE and differentiated flow equations, and is defined throughout every scalar profile included in the bound. A bound on all black holes in a chosen family requires this coverage for every member of that family, rather than only its candidate saturating flow.
The scalar kinetic metric is positive definite and k_N>0, so the completed squares are nonnegative. The left equality Q_L²=g_L^{ij}W_,i W_,j+W²/3 holds throughout the comparison domain.

Use asymptotic normalization f(0)=1 and ψ(0)=0. Require smooth-horizon behavior and finite W at the horizon, with the on-shell total-derivative boundary term and f e^ψ W vanishing there. These are retained boundary hypotheses, not inferred merely from the PDE.

When invoking regular saturation, require an f=1 downward gradient flow that stays in the admissible domain and approaches an interior critical point with W>0. No claim is made that every PDE solution has this behavior.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The right radial construction is written with symbolic d, and its electric-charge caveat explicitly discusses D=5. Specializing these equations to d=5 does not require extending its D≥6 bosonic-string theorem.

The supplied formulae determine all normalization factors needed for the radial comparison. Images image:1, image:2 and image:4 resolve the radial normalization, the √2 factors, and the f² multiplying the scalar kinetic term.

Under the dictionary, the right residual is g_5² times the left PDE residual, and therefore vanishes identically for every W admitted by the left construction. This is a reconstructed algebraic check.

Both sources explicitly supply the smooth-horizon and positive-attractor hypotheses used in the restricted assertion. They are hypotheses of the compared conditional methods; their realization in a new physical model is not presumed.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left application concerns five-dimensional supersymmetric theories; the right paper's advertised string theorem concerns perturbative bosonic strings in D≥6. The relation concerns their radial methods, not a shared string vacuum or equivalence of their WGC conclusions.

The right construction permits a nonnegative residual and obtains bounds from self-repulsive particle masses. The left fake-superpotential PDE sets that residual to zero. Moreover, the right source distinguishes all massless scalars in the force from moduli in the radial action, so a vanishing full self-force cannot silently replace the equality hypothesis.

The left also discusses singular quasiextremal limits, finite-distance boundaries and hypermultiplet transitions; the right bosonic application has no regular electric extremal attractor and instead uses singular limiting flows. Those extensions are excluded from the asserted regular-branch specialization.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Set d=5 only in the right general radial construction. Compare displayed radial equations, mass functionals and regular saturation flows; do not identify the two underlying string theories.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Five-dimensional static spherical electric ansatz with angular S³.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: General d-dimensional electric ansatz with angular S^(d−2).

conventionDictionary.concept: Metric fields, frame and asymptotic normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify r, t, ψ and f, and identify scalar coordinates ϕ^i_R=φ^i_L. At d=5 the metric ansätze coincide. Use ψ∞=0 and f∞=1. No Weyl transformation or additional equality of full EFT actions is claimed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: ds²=−e^(2ψ)f dt²+e^(−ψ)[dr²/f+r²dΩ₃²].
conventionDictionary.right_definition: ds²=−e^(2ψ)f dt²+e^(−2ψ/(d−3))[dr²/f+r²dΩ_(d−2)²].

conventionDictionary.conversion: Define α=√2 κ_5 g_5. Then z_L=α z_R, z_h,L=α z_h,R, and d/dz_R=α d/dz_L. Thus f=1−z/z_h is unchanged. Image:1 fixes the left numerator as √2 times κ_5 g_5.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: z_L=√2 κ_5 g_5/(4π²r²); dots denote z_L derivatives.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: z_R=1/[(d−3)V_(d−2)r^(d−3)], hence z_R=1/(4π²r²) at d=5; dots denote z_R derivatives.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Define C=g_5/(√2 κ_5)>0 and choose k_N,R=α/(3C)=2κ_5²/3. Consequently α/k_N,R=3C. Retain these factors and their units; neither the radial coordinates nor the potential and ADM mass are set equal by a Planck-unit convention. Images image:1 and image:2 fix √2 as multiplying κ_5.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: M_ADM,L=3C[−ψ̇_L,∞+1/(2z_h,L)]; the W bound has mass normalization C.

conventionDictionary.conversion: With the same scalar coordinates, choose G_R,ij=(C/α)g_L,ij=g_L,ij/(2κ_5²), hence G_R^ij=(α/C)g_L^ij=2κ_5²g_L^ij. This is a constant metric rescaling, not a scalar-coordinate rescaling.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: g_L,ij and g_L^ij are the moduli metric and its inverse in the left radial equations.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: G_R,ij and G_R^ij are the moduli metric and its inverse in the right radial equations.

conventionDictionary.concept: Electric charges and gauge kinetic matrix
conventionDictionary.conversion: Choose Q_I^R=q_I^L and f_R^IJ=g_5²a_L^IJ, equivalently f_R,IJ=a_L,IJ/g_5². Thus f_R^IJ Q_IQ_J=g_5²Q_L². The electric field strengths also coincide at d=5. This identifies radial charge components, not full charge lattices.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Q_L²(φ)=a_L^IJ(φ)q_Iq_J; F_L^I=g_5²a_L^IJq_J e^(2ψ)dt∧dr/(2π²r³).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: f_R^ab is the inverse gauge kinetic matrix, distinct from the blackening function f; F_R^a=f_R^ab Q_b e^(2ψ)dt∧dr/(V_(d−2)r^(d−2)).

conventionDictionary.conversion: Set M_R(φ)=C W_L(φ). M_R is the auxiliary comparison mass function, not automatically a particle mass m. This supplies the correct ADM mass units and maps the boundary contribution −f e^ψM_R to −C f e^ψW_L.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: W solves Q_L²=g_L^ijW_,iW_,j+W²/3. The left reserves global fake superpotential for a globally defined solution whose flows are good.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M_R is any admissible function with Δ_R=f_R^abQ_aQ_b−k_N M_R²−G_R^ijM_R,iM_R,j≥0.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Δ_R=g_5²[Q_L²−W²/3−g_L^ijW_,iW_,j]=0 under the left PDE. This equality is stricter than the right Δ_R≥0 hypothesis. The right force convention takes a nonnegative outward self-force as self-repulsive; its scalar and gravitational terms are attractive.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The fake-superpotential equation has zero residual and uses derivatives along vector-multiplet moduli.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The radial residual uses moduli derivatives. The long-range force can additionally receive attractive contributions from massless scalars that are not moduli.

conventionDictionary.conversion: For the asserted saturation comparison, retain only f=1 flows approaching an interior positive critical point. Do not identify every left quasiextremal object with a regular extremal black hole in the right paper's terminology.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Quasiextremal means r_h=0 and can include singular limits; extremal means least mass at fixed charge. A positive critical endpoint of W gives a smooth horizon.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Regular saturation requires an interior critical endpoint with M_R>0; the bosonic electric example instead needs a singular limiting construction.

limitations: Only the supplied spans and attached images were inspected. No tools, code, external references or omitted paper pages were used.

The cross-paper normalization dictionary and specialization are reconstructed here; neither supplied source explicitly states this particular pairwise relation. The right source reports that its first-order equations reproduce the fake-superpotential method, but this does not establish attribution to the selected left paper (35fadaab7efe61ab3dcc:p0031s002, image:5, footnote 37).

Full action-level equivalence is excluded. Establishing it would additionally require the left action (2.1) and its complete field-normalization definitions, rather than only its reference in 0f921335106ad2c14e5a:p0022s002 and the supplied radial equations.

Global existence and uniqueness for arbitrary moduli spaces are excluded. The left source explicitly identifies unresolved finite-distance CFT-boundary flows and possible hypermultiplet interactions (0f921335106ad2c14e5a:p0026s002; 0f921335106ad2c14e5a:p0027s005; 0f921335106ad2c14e5a:p0028s001).

Singular saturation limits and the bosonic-string extremality formula are excluded from this regular-branch relation; their source statements involve additional limiting-horizon arguments (0f921335106ad2c14e5a:p0024s002; 35fadaab7efe61ab3dcc:p0032s001; 35fadaab7efe61ab3dcc:p0032s002).

No particular particle mass is identified with C W. Such an application would separately require the right source's charge proportionality, mass-function coverage and force hypotheses (35fadaab7efe61ab3dcc:p0030s001; 35fadaab7efe61ab3dcc:p0031s001).

endpoints.text: The separated test-scalar equation becomes a singular Sturm–Liouville problem. The substitution h=g/u with u=1−log(sinθ) produces coefficients satisfying the stated regularity conditions, allowing use of imported large-eigenvalue asymptotics.

Restrict to modes depending only on theta. Their equation is (p g')'+lambda q g=0, with p=exp[4(A+C)] sin(theta)/f and q=exp[4(A+C)] f sin(theta). The paper maps this singular problem using g_tilde=g/u, u=1-log(sin theta), to what it identifies as a regular Sturm-Liouville problem.

records.exactAssertion: The right endpoint uses the left endpoint's positive-function rescaling of the separated internal differential equation. On the same background, restricting the left scalar problem to M=0 and constant B4 mode mu=0, and identifying lambda_left=L²M_right,n², makes its p,q,u and transformed coefficients identical to right Eqs. (3.8)-(3.12). This assertion concerns the differential-expression transformation on (0,pi). It excludes equality of physical boundary-value spectra, endorsement of right boundary prescription (3.13), independent certification of endpoint regularity, and any low-lying mass or scale-separation bound.

intersection.statement: The common setting is the same smooth warped AdS4 × S²(B4) background, with the comparison restricted to its theta-dependent internal differential equation on I=(0,pi).
Set the left ten-dimensional scalar mass M to zero and choose constant chi on B4, so mu=0. Then r=0, and identify the left eigenvalue lambda_n with the right L² M_n².

required_assumptions.statement: Compare the same background functions A,C,f and radius L in the displayed string-frame convention; the assertion concerns differential expressions rather than arbitrary backgrounds or physical boundary domains.
Restrict the left problem to M=0 and mu=0; retain arbitrary spectral parameter lambda=L² M_n².
Use the substitution only where its coefficients are differentiable and u=1-log(sin theta)>0, namely inside I. Endpoint boundary conditions require a separate transformation.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Images image:1 and image:4 confirm identical p=e^{4(A+C)} sin(theta)/f and q=e^{4(A+C)} f sin(theta).

The displayed left potential vanishes at M=mu=0. The right paper's footnote 3 explicitly identifies its internal equation with left Eq. (5.3) at M=0 and lambda_n=L² M_n²; image:5 confirms this identification.
On I, 0<sin(theta)<=1 implies u>=1. The rescaling is therefore invertible there, and its coefficient transformation agrees in images image:2 and image:4.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left endpoint treats a scalar probe, including nonzero ten-dimensional mass and B4 eigenvalue; the right treats spin-2 perturbations in a theta-only sector. The common internal equation does not identify the physical fields.

The substitution alone does not identify endpoint domains. In particular, the right paper's claimed equivalence between finite original g and vanishing transformed flux fails the constant-mode check in reproduction step 5.

The left large-n asymptotic statement and the right numerical investigation of the first nonzero eigenvalue are different spectral claims. Neither is certified by the restricted method-reuse relation.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the same A(theta), C(theta), L and theta coordinate. Both displayed backgrounds use the string frame and ds10²=e^{2A}ds²(AdS4)+L²ds²(M6); no frame change is needed for this comparison. Image image:3 confirms the left metric convention.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Ten-dimensional warped geometry with four-dimensional AdS radius L and six-dimensional internal space; R(AdS4)=-12/L².
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The same displayed metric decomposition and AdS curvature normalization.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Choose chi constant, hence mu=0, and remove psi dependence. This produces the right theta-only sector. The zero base eigenvalue is independent of any numerical base-metric normalization.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: omega=chi(w)g(theta), independent of psi, with -Delta_B4 chi=mu chi. The base is normalized by Ric_B4=2g_B4.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: g depends only on theta; the base metric is described as canonically normalized.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Set M_left=0 and lambda_left=L² M_right,n². This does not set the right four-dimensional KK masses to zero. Lambda is dimensionless; L has length units and both mass symbols have inverse-length units.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: M is the ten-dimensional scalar mass; lambda_n is the internal eigenvalue and m_n²=lambda_n/L² is the four-dimensional scalar KK mass squared.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M_n is the four-dimensional Pauli-Fierz spin-2 mass; its internal eigenvalue is L² M_n².

conventionDictionary.conversion: At M_left=mu=0, r_left=0 and both equations are (p g')'+lambda q g=0, equivalently -(p g')'=lambda q g. Images image:1 and image:4 resolve the coefficient placement and signs.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: (p g')'+(lambda q-r)g=0, with p=e^{4(A+C)}sin(theta)/f, q=e^{4(A+C)}f sin(theta), r=e^{6A+2C}f sin(theta)(mu+L²M²e^{2C}). Primes denote theta derivatives.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The same p,q and derivative convention, with no original r term and lambda=L²M_n².

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify h_left with g_tilde_right. Setting r=0 in the left transformation gives exactly the right coefficients. Images image:2 and image:4 confirm the critical derivative placement: r_tilde=-u(pu')', not -(upu')'.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: h=g/u, u=1-log(sin theta); p_tilde=pu², q_tilde=qu², r_tilde=ru²-u(pu')'.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: g_tilde=g/u with the same u; p_tilde=pu², q_tilde=qu², r_tilde=-u(pu')'.

conventionDictionary.conversion: At M_left=0, multiplying the left internal equation by e^{4A} gives the right divergence-form equation with lambda=L²M_n². Thus the printed e^{-2A} and e^{2A} factors are compatible, not competing eigenvalue conventions; image:5 confirms the right factor.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: -(Delta6+4 grad A·grad-L²M²)omega=lambda e^{-2A}omega.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: -div6(e^{4A}grad g)=L²M_n² e^{2A}g.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The exact flux transformation is p_tilde h'=p(u g'-u'g). It does not preserve a zero-flux condition automatically. For the reported finite-g branch, h tends to zero, while its transformed flux can be nonzero; see reproduction step 5.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Appendix B permits separated or periodic conditions on the regularized variable; the supplied section 5 does not specify a physical endpoint domain.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Eq. (3.13) imposes p_tilde g_tilde'=0 at both endpoints and claims this is equivalent to finite original g.

limitations: The left coefficient-integrability argument invokes its pole expansion Eq. (2.16), which is not supplied. That regularity claim is reported rather than independently reproduced; it is excluded from the exact assertion (8dc194fae0fdf0bccb51:p0017s001; 8dc194fae0fdf0bccb51:p0017s002).

The right endpoint-domain claim has a local countercheck: its admitted constant zero mode transforms to a solution with nonzero endpoint flux, contrary to Eq. (3.13). This prevents using the algebraic reuse as certification of physical isospectrality; reproduction step 5 gives the calculation (0dd7757685993832204c:p0005s001; 0dd7757685993832204c:p0006s001).

The left paper explicitly cautions that its high-mode asymptotics do not settle low-mode scale separation. The right numerical first-mass bound is a separate claim and is not reproduced here (8dc194fae0fdf0bccb51:p0018s002; 0dd7757685993832204c:p0012s001; 0dd7757685993832204c:p0012s002).
Only the supplied spans and five attached images were assessed. Node labels, nomination and earlier review summaries were not treated as scientific authority.

endpoints.text: Dimensional reduction gives a three-dimensional scalar theory with real superpotential P. Supersymmetric equations Px=Py=Pa=0 are varied before imposing the shape ansatz (σ,σ,σ,ρ,τ,τ). Nonlinear algebraic equations are then solved numerically as functions of γ=q/f.

Dimensional reduction is matched to the real 3D superpotential potential V=GIJ PI PJ−4P². Supersymmetric vacua solve eight equations PI=0; Hessian eigenvalues with the inverse scalar metric give masses, and Δ=1+√(1+m²L²) gives the chosen scalar operator dimensions.

records.exactAssertion: Left-to-right uses_method, restricted to the shared real three-dimensional bulk scalar formalism: the left endpoint implements the right endpoint's superpotential-extremization stage by eliminating the redundant seventh shape scalar and setting all eight independent derivatives of P to zero, then imposing its particular shape ansatz and solving numerically. The constrained kinetic metrics and supplied scalar-mass normalization agree under the stated dictionary, K=2G. This is a reconstructed method-level relationship, not a historical dependency claim. It excludes equality of the flux-dependent superpotentials, equation systems, vacua, spectra, T-dual backgrounds or scale-separation regimes, and excludes attributing the right's conformal-dimension calculation to the left endpoint.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints describe a three-dimensional bulk scalar theory with two universal scalars and six independent unit-volume shape scalars, and find supersymmetric configurations by setting all eight derivatives of a real superpotential to zero.

The constrained shape metric and the normalization of the scalar Hessian agree as formal prescriptions: writing the kinetic term as -G_IJ ∂φ^I∂φ^J gives the canonical kinetic metric K=2G and the mass operator (2G)^(-1)V_IJ. This comparison does not identify the potentials or vacuum points.

required_assumptions.statement: Use the independent scalar coordinates of the displayed bulk truncations, eliminating the redundant seventh shape scalar. The metric comparison is on the nonsingular domain of positive cycle volumes.

Compare the full superpotential stationarity conditions before additional identifications among independent shape scalars. A nonzero real critical value of P is required only for the AdS specialization.

Compare Einstein-frame scalar equations and dimensionless mass normalizations, accounting for the kinetic convention. Absolute flux coefficients, superpotential values and three-dimensional Planck normalizations are not identified.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both sources explicitly impose s̃7=1/(product of s̃a, a=1,...,6), leaving six independent shape coordinates; images image:1 and image:4 confirm the constraint and kinetic conventions.
The left source explicitly differentiates before imposing its shape ansatz. The right source states the eight derivative equations in (5.21) before its later temporary field identifications.
The left reports V at a supersymmetric vacuum as -4P². The same identity follows directly from the right's (3.8) when all P_I vanish.
Images image:3, image:4 and image:5 establish that the apparent factor-of-two difference in the mass formulas is precisely K=2G.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left applies its particular massive-IIA flux ansatz and numerically solves an ansatz-reduced system parametrized by γ=q/f. The right's displayed application uses type-IIB/type-I flux and metric-flux data. Shared superpotential extremization does not equate these systems.

The common scalar formalism does not establish the same low-energy decoupling regime. The left explicitly distinguishes a three-dimensional truncation from an actual three-dimensional effective theory when the seventh KK tower becomes light.

The displayed spectra belong to different examples: the left includes a BF-allowed negative scalar mass, whereas the right's (5.35) includes massless scalars. Neither supersymmetric stationarity nor use of the same mass prescription implies equal spectra or complete stabilization.

conventionDictionary.concept: Independent scalar content and shape constraint
conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the formal six-coordinate unit-volume shape description, not numerical vacuum values: s̃7=(product_a s̃a)^(-1). The left's later ansatz implies s̃7=(σ³ρτ²)^(-1).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Independent fields are x, y and s̃a, a=1,...,6; s^i=Vol(X7)^(3/7)s̃i.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Independent fields are υ, ϕ and s̃a, a=1,...,6; s^i=vol(X)^(3/7)s̃i.

conventionDictionary.conversion: For variations of the defining volume and dilaton variables in a common reference convention, (δx,δy)^T=(1/8)[[-1,-3√7],[3√7,-1]](δυ,δϕ)^T. This matrix is orthogonal, so it preserves the universal kinetic block and the condition that both universal derivatives vanish. It is not a T-duality map between the displayed vacua.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (2.7) gives x=-3√7 ϕ/8+log Vol(X7)/(2√7), y=-3 log Vol(X7)/2-ϕ/8.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equations (3.2)-(3.3) give log vol(X)=7βυ with β=-1/(4√7); ϕ is the dilaton.

conventionDictionary.conversion: After eliminating s̃7, the coefficient metric in -G_IJ∂φ^I∂φ^J has shape block (1+δab)/(4s̃a s̃b) in both descriptions. The metric in the convention -K_IJ∂φ^I∂φ^J/2 is K=2G. Images image:1, image:3 and image:4 resolve the coefficients.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (2.11) has universal kinetic coefficients 1/4; (4.6) defines K=2 diag(1/4,1/4,Gab), Gab=(1+δab)/(4s̃a s̃b).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equations (3.6) and (3.9) use -G_IJ∂φ^I∂φ^J, with G=diag(1/4,1/4,G̃ab), G̃ab=(1+δab)/(4s̃a s̃b).

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the operation dP=0 on all eight independent fields and the critical identity V=-4P². No equality or constant proportionality between the two flux-dependent superpotentials is asserted; a full off-shell identification is unnecessary for this restricted method relation.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: A real P is supplied in (3.3); supersymmetry requires P_x=P_y=P_a=0, and the source reports V at the vacuum as -4P².
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (3.8) states V=G^{IJ}P_I P_J-4P², with P_I=∂_I P; (5.21) sets all eight derivatives to zero.

conventionDictionary.conversion: K^(-1)V_IJ=(1/2)G^(-1)V_IJ, so the two mass prescriptions have the same normalization. For AdS use positive L²=1/|V|. Image image:5 confirms both the overall 1/2 and |V| in (5.35); its preceding prose literally prints L²=⟨V⟩^(-1), a local sign inconsistency that is not adopted here.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (4.5) uses eigenvalues of K^(-1)V_IJ/|V|; (4.7) gives V=-1/L_AdS² at the vacuum.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (5.35) uses (1/2) times the eigenvalues of G^(-1)V_IJ/|V|.

conventionDictionary.concept: Units, flux normalization and overall action
conventionDictionary.conversion: Retain each source's units. The left's factors of 2π can be stripped to expose its integer flux labels, but those labels are not identified with fluxes in the right's type-I examples. A constant overall action factor does not affect the stationary equations or the normalized Hessian prescription.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: α′=1; h=(2π)²K, m=(2π)^(-1)M, f=(2π)³N, q=(2π)³Q; the three-dimensional Planck mass is set to one.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: (2π)²α′=1; (A.8) writes harmonic RR fluxes with integer coefficients in these units; (B.1) has an overall 4π multiplying the three-dimensional action. Image image:6 confirms these conventions.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The right's positive-root dimension formula is an additional endpoint operation. Its application to the left spectrum is excluded from the relation.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The supplied mass section reports canonically normalized scalar masses and checks the AdS3 BF bound.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (5.36) chooses Δ=1+√(1+m²L²), giving {8,4,4,4,4,2,2,2} for (5.35); image image:5 confirms the radical.

limitations: The relation is reconstructed from the supplied source passages and images. Node labels, nomination rationale and earlier review metadata are not independent scientific evidence.

No numerical root of left (3.11), Hessian spectrum or ten-dimensional field equation was independently reproduced. The left's switch to numerical methods is directly reported, not an established impossibility of analytic solution (147ef99e43b7e612b9ba:p0008s001; image:2).

The right's IIB superpotential/reduction matching explicitly requires tadpole cancellation for the source contributions. This comparison does not certify that matching or the existence of localized ten-dimensional solutions (0d8cdf3c0a345bbc3b2f:p0012s001; 0d8cdf3c0a345bbc3b2f:p0012s002).

An off-shell equality of the two flux-dependent potentials, a T-duality identification of these particular endpoint examples, or equality of spectra would require additional flux and normalization matching. Those stronger assertions are excluded, so they are not decisive gaps in the chosen method relation (147ef99e43b7e612b9ba:p0005s002; 0d8cdf3c0a345bbc3b2f:p0011s001; 0d8cdf3c0a345bbc3b2f:p0012s001; 0d8cdf3c0a345bbc3b2f:p0024s001).

No common decoupled three-dimensional effective regime is established. The left explicitly allows a light seventh KK tower, and its anisotropy is reported as nonparametric (147ef99e43b7e612b9ba:p0008s001; 147ef99e43b7e612b9ba:p0008s002; 147ef99e43b7e612b9ba:p0013s001).
Only the supplied physical pages and six attached images were assessed; no full-paper mathematical certification is claimed.

endpoints.text: Flux backtracking switches off f7 and f31,f32,f33, solves flat-sliced three-dimensional domain-wall BPS equations obtained by completing squares, and uplifts using explicit metric and dilaton formulae.
Flux backtracking removes the D4-sourced F4 terms. The residual flat-domain-wall BPS equations admit an analytic solution; restoring F4 requires numerical integration of the coupled BPS system.

records.exactAssertion: Within their displayed truncations, the right endpoint is a procedural analogue of the left endpoint: both remove designated brane-sourced RR terms, solve the residual flat-sliced three-dimensional BPS flow, and reconstruct the corresponding probe background. The right-to-left arrow uses left as the comparator; it does not assert historical borrowing or dependence on its particular IIB implementation. This restricted analogy excludes equivalence of actions or solutions, a duality or scalar-field dictionary, specialization, transfer of tadpole independence, and transfer of successful analytic brane reinstatement. The right source's numerical restoration is an exhibited construction, not a theorem excluding every analytic interpolation.

intersection.statement: The intersection is procedural: remove specified brane-sourced RR flux terms from a three-dimensional superpotential, solve a residual scalar BPS flow with flat Lorentzian two-dimensional slices, and interpret the resulting background as the geometry probed by those branes.
Both sources display analytic residual backgrounds. This does not establish an intersection of their physical solution spaces or identify their scalar fields, fluxes, or ten-dimensional theories.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare the procedures within their respective displayed truncations; do not assume a common compactification, duality map, or identical equations.
The removed coefficients must be the RR fluxes assigned by each source to the branes whose probe background is being reconstructed.
Restrict the right endpoint to its stated untwisted example, with h_i=(h,h,h,h,-h,-h,-h), initially e_i=-f, and s^{1,2,3,4}=a, s^{5,6,7}=b.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The source passages explicitly identify their own three-dimensional descriptions and flux-backtracking operations. These statements establish the comparison's source scope, without independently certifying the truncations.
Left removes f7 and f31,f32,f33 associated with D1/D5 branes; right removes all e_i associated with D4-sourced F4. Both explicitly introduce a residual flat domain-wall problem.
The right source supplies the stated flux pattern, symmetry reduction, residual superpotential, and reduced BPS equations.

scope_mismatches.statement: Left concerns type IIB with F(3), F(7), and metric fluxes; right concerns massive IIA and removes F4 while retaining the displayed m and H3 contributions. The packet establishes no physical field or flux identification.

The removed left fluxes do not enter its displayed tadpole conditions. On the right, restoring f changes a source contribution coupled to h, and the D4 charges are reported to be correlated by tadpoles and anomaly cancellation. Tadpole independence cannot be transferred.

Left reports power-law profiles on y∈(0,∞); right reports a non-scaling residual solution on a finite three-dimensional radial interval. These are distinct outputs of the shared procedure, not an established tension.

Left supplies harmonic-like functions for reinstating D1/D5 branes. Right explicitly reports failure of independent-stack factorised harmonic superposition and exhibits a numerical coupled flow. Analytic reinstatement is not a common guarantee.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match only the operation of deleting the designated brane-sourced RR coefficients. No equality of flux ranks, charges, signs, or numerical values is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: f7 multiplies η1234567 in F(7); f31,f32,f33 multiply η127,η347,η567 in F(3). Their corresponding probe branes are D1 and D5(1,2,3).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The seven coefficients e_i belong to the D4-sourced F4 sector; e_i=-f in the chosen full configuration and e_i=0 in the residual problem.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The displayed untwisted fields are φ and s^i, with 𝒱=(∏_{i=1}^7 s^i)^(1/3), reduced to a and b for this flow.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Retain the separate source normalizations. Matching their functional roles does not establish W=P or an action-level W=2P correspondence.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: V=K^{AB}∂_A W∂_B W-2W², with ϕ'^A=∓K^{AB}∂_B W and A'=±W. Images image:3 and image:1 confirm the kinetic convention and paired signs.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: P carries the explicit prefactor 1/8 in (5.1); P_res=M+4H_++3H_- and A'=2P_res in the displayed residual flow.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The established procedural correspondence is deletion of specified linear RR terms from each superpotential, retaining its other displayed terms.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Set f7=f31=f32=f33=0 in (2.13), retaining the f34,f35,f36,f37 and metric-flux terms. Image image:3 resolves the powers and overall 2g^{-1}W normalization.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: P_res=(1/8)[m e^{5φ/4}/𝒱+(e^{-φ/2}/𝒱)Σ_i h_i/s^i]. Image image:4 confirms both denominators and the removed e^{φ/4}Σ_i e_i s^i/𝒱² term.

conventionDictionary.concept: Radial gauge, signature, and frame scope
conventionDictionary.conversion: Both ansätze have unit positive radial coefficient and flat slices of signature (-,+). No global coordinate identification or ten-dimensional frame transformation is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: ds3²=dy²+e^{2A(y)}(-dt²+dx²), with derivatives in y, in the three-dimensional theory defined by (2.10).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: ds3,E²=dr²+e^{2A(r)}(-dt²+dx²), with derivatives in r; the reconstructed ten-dimensional metric is explicitly labelled string frame in (5.22).

conventionDictionary.conversion: No numerical flux or length comparison is made, so a common unit conversion is unnecessary for this procedural assertion.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The source sets g=1 and restores it through f→gf and ω→gω.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The displayed P uses its own 1/8 normalization; the supplied comparison passages do not establish a common normalization with left g.

limitations: No decisive context is missing for the restricted procedural analogy. Direct attribution of the right construction to the particular left implementation would require identifying the right paper's cited references; that stronger uses_method claim is excluded.

The residual solutions and ten-dimensional consistency are reported by the sources. The comparison does not independently reproduce their complete scalar equations, uplift equations, or numerical integration.

The right source reports failure of independent-stack harmonic superposition and a numerical branch approaching AdS3; this does not establish nonexistence of other analytic constructions (9efe4bcb4ae2505fd97a:p0038s001; image:5).

The supplied physical-page-44 image concerns Appendix B exceptional-modulus corrections and is not a kinetic-action dictionary for the main Section 5 flow (9efe4bcb4ae2505fd97a:p0044s001; image:6). No claim is made about extending that flow to all resolved-sector fields.
Inherited node labels, earlier review summaries, and source-wide coverage metadata were not treated as independent scientific proof. Only the supplied excerpts and images were assessed.

endpoints.text: Obtain temperature from horizon regularity, entropy from Wald’s formula, energy from the boundary stress tensor and grand potential from the on-shell action. Impose T=0 together with the horizon equation to extract extremal mass/charge ratios.

Extract conserved charge through the corrected Noether flux and mass through the holographically renormalized boundary stress tensor; compute entropy using Wald's formula, including the correction to horizon area at fixed physical mass and charge.

records.exactAssertion: Within first-order static, spherical, singly charged AdS black holes in five bulk dimensions, the right endpoint implements two subprocedures explicitly contained in the left endpoint: extraction of black-hole energy from the holographically renormalized boundary stress tensor, with Casimir subtraction and boundary-time normalization, and evaluation of the Wald entropy functional on the corrected horizon. This establishes a restricted right_to_left uses_method relation by comparing implemented prescriptions. It does not establish historical borrowing or identify citation [20]; it does not assert use of the entire left pipeline, equality of higher-derivative theories or results, a coefficient dictionary, equality of grand-canonical and canonical actions, or derivation of the right fixed-M,Q entropy shift from the left extremal mass/charge calculation.

intersection.statement: Restrict the comparison to static, singly electrically charged, spherical AdS black holes in five bulk dimensions, with higher-derivative corrections treated to first order.
Use a regular nonextremal horizon for the entropy-variation comparison. This avoids the double-root obstruction to an ordinary linear horizon-radius shift at exact leading-order extremality.
Both constructions extract energy from a renormalized boundary stress tensor, remove the Casimir contribution, and account for boundary-time normalization.

required_assumptions.statement: Remain within the first-order, static single-charge regime; higher-order corrections and additional charges or angular momenta are excluded.
Compare the mass-extraction prescriptions after specifying the boundary-time frame and the zero-Casimir subtraction convention.

Wald entropy is evaluated on the relevant corrected solution. For the right endpoint's derivative at fixed physical M and Q, the horizon area must vary; the linear derivative is taken away from exact leading-order extremality.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The displayed solutions and stated perturbative orders admit the selected five-dimensional, spherical, static single-charge subdomain.
The sources explicitly state Casimir subtraction and boundary-time rescaling. The right mass formula already includes its redshift factor.

The left entropy is expressed using the horizon constrained by the corrected solution. The right explicitly uses the corrected horizon area, includes its fixed-M,Q variation, and explains why the ordinary linear variation fails at an exactly extremal leading-order horizon.

scope_mismatches.statement: The operator content is not identified coefficient by coefficient. The left starts with curvature-squared corrections; the right corrected electric flux contains c2,c3,c4 interactions. Field redefinitions in a charged background can generate mixed curvature-Maxwell terms, so matching names or setting coefficients equal is insufficient.

The left on-shell potential is grand canonical. The right canonical action discussed on physical page 19 includes the Hawking-Ross term for fixed charge. Their untransformed on-shell actions are not interchangeable.

The left's horizon parametrization and extremal mass/charge extraction do not themselves specify the right's entropy derivative at fixed physical M,Q. Likewise, the left's asymptotically flat equation (66) is outside the selected AdS comparison.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Write D=d_left=d_right+1. Select D=5, hence d_left=5 and d_right=4, with k=1 and a three-dimensional spherical horizon of unit volume omega_3.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The bulk has dimension d; the transverse horizon has dimension d-2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The bulk integration measure has dimension d+1; the transverse horizon has dimension d-1.

conventionDictionary.concept: Leading action, length scale, and gravitational normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: For the leading-order normalization check choose g_left=1/l_right and 2*kappa_5^2=16*pi. Both displayed Maxwell terms are -F^2/4; their five-dimensional cosmological terms then coincide. This is a chosen units dictionary, not a matching of higher-derivative theories.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The displayed bulk action has overall factor -1/(2*kappa_d^2); g is the inverse uncorrected AdS radius. Equation (10), checked in image:3, fixes the Maxwell and curvature-squared terms.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: G=1 gives the 1/(16*pi) normalization; equation (4.12), checked in image:6, displays the Euclidean two-derivative bulk action and radius l.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match geometric roles: f1_left corresponds to bar_f_right and f2_left to g_right; r_plus corresponds to r_h as an areal horizon radius. This does not identify the corrected functions numerically. The left constant g is not the right radial function g(r).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The Euclidean radial-time metric is f1*d_tau^2+dr^2/f2, with both functions vanishing at r_plus.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The normalized Lorentzian metric is -bar_f*d_bar_t^2+dr^2/g(r)+r^2*dOmega^2, where bar_f=lambda^(-2)*(1+gamma(r))*g(r).

conventionDictionary.conversion: In D=5 and the chosen gravitational units, equal physical charges imply Q_parameter_left=sqrt(3)*q_right. This normalization also matches the leading metric terms Q_parameter_left^2/(12*r^4) and q_right^2/(4*r^4). No equality of corrected electric profiles is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Distinguish Q_parameter_left from physical charge mathcal_Q_left=omega_(d-2)*Q_parameter_left/(2*kappa_d^2), which the source says is unmodified by the higher-derivative terms.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Physical Q_right=(1/(16*pi))*integral star(mathcal_F), where mathcal_F is the corrected electric field. Equation (2.21) gives Q_right=sqrt((d-2)*(d-1)/2)*omega_(d-1)*q_right/(16*pi). Image:4 resolves the square root and distinguishes mathcal_F from F.

conventionDictionary.concept: Mass, boundary time, and vacuum subtraction
conventionDictionary.conversion: At zero higher-derivative coupling, the selected units and equal mass imply mu_left=m_right. At nonzero coupling compare the prescriptions, not these parameters: E_left must be divided by lambda_left for its CFT frame, whereas M_right already includes division by lambda_right. Both sources exclude Casimir energy. Equality of the two numerical lambda factors is not assumed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: E is the boundary-stress-tensor energy. With lambda_left=g_eff/g, t_prime=lambda_left*t and E_CFT=E/lambda_left. Finite counterterms remove the stated Casimir term.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: bar_t=lambda_right*t, with lambda_right^2=1+2*c1*(d-3)/(d-1). M is the zero-Casimir stress-tensor mass in bar_t time, including the factor 1/lambda_right.

conventionDictionary.concept: Wald functional, area, and perturbation parameter
conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the displayed -2*pi Wald prescription with each source's own action-density measure. Under the chosen leading gravitational normalization both give S0=A/4. In D=5 the right area variation gives dot_A/A=3*dot_r_h/r_h. A dot here denotes differentiation in the scalar perturbation parameter at zero coupling and fixed physical M,Q; it is unrelated to the horizon binormal. No componentwise Riemann-sign dictionary is needed for the procedural assertion.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equations (49)-(50) use the curvature variation of S_bulk at fixed metric and a horizon binormal; the leading entropy is 2*pi*A/kappa_d^2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (3.14) uses the curvature variation of the Lagrangian. endpoints.text: Scherk–Schwarz reduction and a flux-to-embedding-tensor dictionary encode the scalar potential and consistency constraints. The authors report matching embedding-tensor quadratic constraints to the required flux Bianchi identities and tadpoles.

Embedding-tensor matching translates flux consistency into quadratic constraints. Singular solves the constrained extremisation problem; scalar masses test BF stability, while gravitini with m3/2 L=1 determine preserved supersymmetry.

records.exactAssertion: The right endpoint uses the embedding-tensor/QC construction and Singular constrained-extremisation workflow described by the left endpoint's type IIB O5/D5 branch: flux couplings specify Θ, Θ generates the scalar potential, and its quadratic constraint supplies flux consistency identities imposed during extremisation. The right applies this construction to SO(8,8+N_extra) with dynamical open strings, using N_extra=3 in its RSTU search. Its reported direct-reduction matching is restricted to the axion-free, zero-current sector specified in (3.20)–(3.22). Both sources expressly leave the permitted O5/D5 charge outside the restrictions generated by QC. This is a reconstructed methodological-use relation, without a claim of bibliographic priority, equal component dictionaries, equal potentials or constraint ideals, a proved truncation between complete theories, equal vacuum sets, or transferred stability results. The left's type IIA branch is excluded.

intersection.statement: Type IIB reductions on a seven-dimensional twisted internal space with one type of smeared, spacetime-filling O5/D5 source, described by half-maximal D=3 supergravity. The left neglects source dynamics; the right includes open-string dynamics.

Both apply embedding-tensor consistency constraints and Singular to an RSTU constrained-extremisation problem. The right search includes three additional matter multiplets and restricts background fluxes to H(3)=F(5)=0; the supplied left method is not asserted to have this entire search restriction.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare the abstract embedding-tensor construction and its operational use, with each theory's own invariant metric and flux dictionary. Do not identify individual tensor or flux components across different index spaces.

An allowed O5/D5 source charge is not required to vanish by the quadratic constraint. Its physical charge/tadpole equation must be distinguished from the constraints imposed by half-maximal supergravity.

The right paper's reported matching to its direct reduction is restricted to vanishing closed-string axions and the independent zero-current condition (3.20), with its stated flux and dilaton dictionaries.

Constrained extremisation means imposing the flux consistency identities alongside the scalar extremisation equations; the relation concerns the reported procedure, not an independently reproduced solution of those equations.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both explicitly encode flux couplings in Θ, give the same abstract tensor decomposition and quadratic-constraint form, and construct a scalar potential quadratic in Θ. The right changes the duality group to SO(8,8+N).

(26) leaves the η^1357 component of dF(3) unrestricted by the quadratic constraint; right excludes its permitted-source equation (2.95) from the identities generated by that constraint. Images image:2 and image:4 confirm these qualifications.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left scalar theory has 64 scalars and SO(8,8) duality; the right has 64+8N scalars and SO(8,8+N) duality. Identical abstract constraint notation does not establish identical component constraint ideals.

The left ignores source dynamics. The right includes source-induced RR field-strength corrections and modified Bianchi identities through O(λ²); its tilded field strengths cannot generally be identified with the left background fluxes.

The right also diagnoses supersymmetry and BF stability, including extra scalar fluctuations even at zero open-string VEVs. These diagnostics are not consequences transferred from the left method by this relation.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Half-maximal N=8, D=3 theory with SO(8,8+N_extra) duality and 64+8N_extra scalars.

endpoints.text: Hodge decomposition reduces the localized G2 Bianchi identity to a Calabi–Yau Laplace equation for a three-form current K. Its decomposition into a scalar ϕ and primitive (2,1) component k guides the warp-factor and geometric corrections; stable-three-form reconstruction determines the complementary part of Ω.

Construct localization corrections through Calabi–Yau Laplace equations for a three-form current and warp/dilaton profiles; adjust harmonic, co-exact and exact flux components to satisfy Bianchi identities and equations of motion at the retained order.

records.exactAssertion: The right endpoint uses the Laplace/Hodge-current component of the left endpoint's localization method: it solves a CY Laplace equation for K, decomposes K into ϕ and primitive k, and constructs the retained co-exact RR two-form as d†CYK. Its supersymmetric geometric formulas match the left first-order construction; its non-supersymmetric branch retains this solver while adjusting other flux pieces. The numerical K equations coincide for matching CY/source inputs at right N=0 and 5μ̂=mg_s. This is an equation-level method-use relation at the displayed perturbative order in the reliable bulk. It excludes equivalence of complete backgrounds, general-N source equality, an independently repeated stable-three-form derivation, derivation of non-supersymmetric equations of motion from left supersymmetry, and identification of numbered bibliography entries.

intersection.statement: Both constructions organize localized type-IIA AdS4 backgrounds around a Calabi–Yau reference metric on X6, using a three-form current K and its scalar and primitive components. The comparison concerns this shared procedure, not identification of arbitrary backgrounds.

The geometric comparison applies at the displayed perturbative order in the weak-coupling, large-volume bulk. The right source explicitly restricts reliability to g_s|ϕ| ≪ 1; the near-O6 region is excluded.

required_assumptions.statement: The Laplacian and adjoint are those of the compact CY reference geometry. The left primitive-decomposition argument uses its stated SU(3)-holonomy setting and absence of harmonic five-forms; no extension of that argument to every manifold admitting a CY metric is asserted.

A physical solution requires cancellation of the cohomological source obstruction. For the coefficient comparison, use the left tadpole-compatible source data and set N=0 in the right displayed equation, obtaining the same −4δ(ΠO6) term. This is a restricted input comparison, not an existence claim for arbitrary flux choices.

Use the left c=0 choice in K=ϕ Re ΩCY+c Im ΩCY+Re k and the stated zero-mean scalar convention. Harmonic freedom must be distinguished from the co-exact flux solver; equality of harmonic moduli between backgrounds is not required or asserted.
Compare only retained perturbative terms where g_s|ϕ| ≪ 1. The authors' displayed order symbols are not interpreted as uniform error bounds at localized source cores.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both supplied equations explicitly use ΔCY=d†CY d+dd†CY and the decomposition K=ϕ Re ΩCY+Re k, with k primitive of type (2,1), after the left c=0 choice.
The supplied formulas establish the shared first-order pattern J=JCY+O(g_s²), Ω=ΩCY+g_s k+O(g_s²), and the same linear warp correction after taking the fourth root of the left warp equation.

The left constructs a supersymmetric background and reconstructs Ω from its imaginary part. The right also constructs a non-supersymmetric branch by adjusting fluxes and reports an equations-of-motion check. The left supersymmetry argument does not establish that additional check.

endpoints.text: For F₄B=0, γ=1, f,h,m>0, and f^i=(−f,−f,−f,−f,−f,−f,6f), the authors exhibit a supersymmetric AdS₃ critical point with six equal shape moduli σ≈1.32691. The previously flat y direction is stabilized, and all eight retained Hessian directions are positive.

For the simple flux vector with B=0, the source reviews a supersymmetric stationary point where the six independent shapes coincide. It gives three numerical constants and two equations fixing the dilaton and volume. The eight retained real scalars are stabilized; the twisted sector is not included.

records.exactAssertion: The left stationary-point result is the same result reviewed at the right endpoint within the shared constrained eight-scalar 3D system: identical positive flux choice, real superpotential, six-equal-shape supersymmetric critical point, constants (a,b,sigma)=(0.515696...,3.43111...,1.32691...), negative potential and reported positive quadratic form. The formerly no-scale y direction has no remaining flat direction in this retained system. This equivalence uses the unit-product shape variables explicitly appearing in both superpotentials. It excludes the conflicting literal geometric conversion in right (2.19), numerical identification of coordinate-Hessian eigenvalues with canonical masses, absolute AdS-radius normalization, finite F4B corrections, and stabilization of D2-position or twisted fields.

F4B=0, gamma=1, positive f,h,m, flux vector f^i=f(-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,6), positive unit-product shape variables, and six equal independent shapes.

endpoints.text: The reviewed emergence proposal generates kinetic terms by integrating out a charged tower up to a species cutoff. For a linear tower, both induced kinetic terms depend on the same mass gap, giving parametric charge–mass proportionality. Exact force/extremality matching remains undetermined.

Use the imported quasi-Jacobi decomposition of the four-dimensional elliptic genus and theta expansions to identify charged towers. Apply the scalar-inclusive repulsive-force condition and a one-loop mass ansatz to infer the mass correction required for that tower to remain repulsive.

records.exactAssertion: The left emergence estimate provides a qualitative analogy for the right method: both organize weak-coupling charged-tower physics around linked gauge, scalar, and mass data. Their operations differ: the left induces kinetic terms from an assumed spectrum, whereas the right uses an indexed sublattice and imposes repulsive-force matching to constrain a mass ansatz. This directed comparison asserts no method inheritance, common spectrum, species-cutoff identification, numerical equivalence, derived mass renormalization, or one-loop equality of extremality and repulsion.

intersection.statement: Both displayed methods concern charged particle towers becoming light near four-dimensional weak gauge coupling and relate their masses to gauge and scalar data. This is an intersection of physical questions, without an established identification of compactifications or spectra.
Both discuss quantum effects relevant to charge-to-mass and scalar-force relations. The left supplies a parametric motivation; the right imposes a perturbative repulsive-force matching condition.

required_assumptions.statement: The left estimate is read under its proposed emergence boundary condition, linear charged spectrum, species prescription, and leading one-loop approximation. Its continuum reconstruction additionally assumes large N.

For the right's unshifted indexed sublattice, retain its stated nonzero derivative contribution and reported absence of cancellation on that sublattice. This is restricted to the corresponding generic-flux argument.

The right mass-matching calculation uses its ansatz and linear expansion in small mass and threshold corrections. Equating a sufficient lower bound to the force threshold is an imposed matching prescription, rather than a first-principles mass calculation.

The comparison must preserve both sources' qualifications: the left does not determine exact force coefficients, and the right's one-loop black-hole interpretation is conditional on continued agreement between extremality and the repulsive-force condition.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left explicitly states the emergence proposal and displays the assumed spectrum and cutoff equations. These establish the inputs of its toy estimate, not their universal physical validity.
The right explicitly states the quasi-Jacobi decomposition, the generic-flux restriction, and the sublattice survival argument. Only their reported use is needed for this method comparison.

The right explicitly identifies its mass correction as an ansatz constrained by demanding repulsion. Image:4 confirms the scalar-metric derivative term and the negative sign of the threshold correction in equation (5.21).
The qualifications limiting numerical and extremality conclusions are present in the sources themselves; no missing cross-paper normalization premise is used to assert the restricted analogy.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left assumes q_k=k and m_k=kΔm. The right identifies charges q_k=2m_J k and an inequality involving excitation levels. This does not establish the left's exact linear mass spectrum.

The left's N counts species below a cutoff. The right's elliptic-genus coefficients are signed indices of a subsector; they do not supply a full positive species count or the degeneracies needed to transplant the species estimate.

The left proposes generating kinetic terms from integrated particles with nondynamical UV fields. The right constrains string-loop mass renormalization alongside corrections to an existing leading gauge coupling. These are different calculations despite their common quantum-correction language.

The left leaves exact force matching undetermined. The right's corrected extremality interpretation remains conditional, and its fluxed U(1) force description is evaluated at the tower scale, where the source reports the Stückelberg mass to be lower. Neither establishes an unrestricted long-distance, exactly massless shared gauge sector.

endpoints.text: The authors propose connecting adjacent F4 flux vacua using spacetime-filling D4-branes wrapping contractible one-cycles that sweep the dual two-cycles and annihilate. Their position moduli supply scalar interpolation directions. This is distinct from a spontaneous decay: supersymmetric D4 domain-wall transitions are marginal and do not dynamically expand.

A space-filling probe D4 wrapping a contractible two-cycle inside Φ7 is proposed to connect flux vacua non-dynamically. Sweeping the three-cycle shifts F4,q by one quantum (2π)³; the brane pinches off at vacuum endpoints. DBI energy relative to |Vflux| scales as N^{-1/2} at S=0 and N^0 at S=−1/7.

records.exactAssertion: Within the sources' stated smeared/probe descriptions, the right construction uses the left endpoint's proposed F4-interpolation method: introduce a spacetime-filling D4 wrapping a contractible cycle, use its internal position as an open-string scalar, and sweep the dual internal cycle so that the brane disappears at the endpoints while the relevant F4 integer changes by one per elementary sweep. The right adapts the AdS4/one-cycle/two-cycle construction to AdS3/two-cycle/three-cycle geometry and its own flux ansatz. This is a reconstructed identification of the explicit procedure. It excludes equivalence of vacuum families, actions, kinetic metrics, energy powers or distances; spontaneous decay; a proven fully localized interpolation; and verified bibliographic identification of the right paper's reference [62].

intersection.statement: The intersection is a flux-interpolation procedure in massive IIA orientifold AdS constructions, rather than a common vacuum family: a spacetime-filling D4 wraps a contractible internal cycle and sweeps the cycle dual to the relevant F4 component.
Within the displayed transverse-four-cycle smearing or suppressed-backreaction description, the sourced F4 Bianchi identity gives a step across the internal D4 location.

Both descriptions use a brane-position scalar and disappearing branes at vacuum endpoints to propose a field-space interpolation. This intersection concerns the proposed construction; it does not establish spontaneous decay or a continuous family of vacuum solutions.

The right states its fixed-moduli probe prescription and its choice of B2 with zero pullback on the brane. These are source assumptions adopted for identifying the reported method.

The left discusses three D4 position moduli to change all three DGKT F4 components. The right varies the selected F4,q component. Their flux parameters and vacuum families are not identified.

The left paper's AdS3 extension includes induced D2 charge from worldvolume flux. The right explicitly chooses a different H3/B2 configuration with no induced net D2 charge. Reusing the interpolation procedure does not identify these charge sectors.

The left displayed DBI calculation is in string frame and four external dimensions; the right uses Einstein frame and three external dimensions. The right's energy-ratio powers are model-specific and supply no common numerical energy law for the two endpoints.

In both cases the D4 worldvolume has dimension five and is codimension one inside the swept internal cycle. This is a procedural correspondence, not a dimensional reduction identifying the two vacua.
