The left output is a normalized large-distance response coefficient and its worldline matching. The right output is a local near-horizon exponent determined by an indicial or enhanced-isometry calculation. These are different data of a perturbation equation.

Left horizon regularity is imposed in the neutral-hole response calculation. Right branch selection uses regular non-extremal solutions before taking the extremal limit; the resulting extremal deformations can be singular. These prescriptions are not interchangeable.

endpoints.text: For the discussed N=4 supergravity multiplets, reviewed flux and geometry couplings produce a vanishing total heat kernel. N=2 theories can retain logarithmic corrections even with nonminimal couplings; supersymmetric cancellation is therefore sensitive to the complete theory.

Applying previously computed N=2 multiplet heat-kernel results, the author finds c=0 for every complete multiplet because supersymmetry-required nonminimal couplings produce exact boson–fermion cancellation. Only E4 is renormalized, preserving Δ=0 at one loop. The stated protection also covers nonsupersymmetric Einstein–Maxwell backgrounds in the embedding.

records.exactAssertion: Right-to-left support is restricted to the left endpoint's qualitative conclusion that supersymmetric loop cancellation depends on complete multiplets and their flux couplings. In the right paper's specified four-dimensional ungauged Einstein-Maxwell embedding, the supersymmetry-fixed nonminimal terms cancel c for every complete massless N=2 multiplet, while the Euler contribution to a4 generally survives and depends on multiplet counts. This explicitly supports coupling- and field-content-sensitive cancellation. The right result c=0, Delta=0 therefore does not by itself contradict the left report of surviving N=2 entropy logarithms. Excluded are a derivation of the left K_(N=4)(s)=0 statement, identification of its charged massive multiplets with the right massless multiplets, equality of entropy-log coefficients, and protection beyond the right one-loop four-derivative embedding.

The right coefficients refer to complete massless N=2 multiplets with the required nonminimal couplings and appropriate gauge fixing and ghosts. They cannot be replaced by coefficients for minimally coupled fields or incomplete multiplets.

The extremality conclusion uses the on-shell four-derivative basis and its classical restriction c1=c3=c4=0, as well as its preservation at one loop. Interpreting this truncation as a black-hole extremality result requires the stated large-black-hole EFT regime.

endpoints.text: Combining positivity with an imported leading extremality correction, the authors obtain √2m_Pl|Q|/M > 1 for extremal black holes within EFT control, approaching unity from above as mass increases. They claim a proof of the mild WGC through self-repulsion and kinematically allowed fragmentation; the same coefficient combination gives a positive Wald entropy shift.

The manuscript imports the effective-theory result that the leading large-black-hole shift Q_ext/M−1 is proportional to c_ext/M² with positive normalization, so the sign of c_ext determines the side from which Einstein–Maxwell extremality is approached.

records.exactAssertion: Restricted to electromagnetic quartic four-derivative corrections, alpha3=0 and c1=...=c6=0, the extremality component of the left claim specializes the right imported large-black-hole formula to c_ext=alpha1>0. At fixed coefficients this approaches zero from above as M increases. Positivity is taken as the left paper's reported conditional premise. This relation excludes alpha3!=0, equivalence of the positivity proofs, and certification of the entropy, self-repulsion or fragmentation conclusions.

M5 twists on negatively curved surfaces yield smooth eleven-dimensional warped AdS5 solutions preserving N=2 or N=1 supersymmetry. The N=2 solution includes an explicit AdS7-to-AdS5×Σ flow at C₁=0; reported holographic central charges scale as N³(g−1).

Their stated constructions are Hopf T-duality followed by a lift on the left, and an R-symmetry twist solved in seven-dimensional gauged supergravity followed by an uplift on the right. The assertion excludes equality, specialization, methodological dependence, dynamical support, matched charges or central charges, a common CFT, and shared global regularity.

endpoints.text: Higher-derivative corrections can make finite-size black holes superextremal relative to the asymptotic bound. Such a result could satisfy the mild WGC without light charged particles; it does not establish the stronger tower/sublattice requirements at smaller charges.

ModMax coupled to Einstein gravity has mass-independent extremal Z̄. It therefore lacks any strictly decreasing discrete subset and fails the necessary decay condition, leading to conditional incompatibility with the black-hole WGC despite its shifted charge-to-mass normalization.

endpoints.text: The controlled highly charged limit yields d₀>0. The extremality calculation gives Δz=2d₀/(5m²)>0, so extremal charge-to-mass ratios approach unity from above with increasing mass. The authors infer superextremal smaller black-hole states and kinematically allowed decays satisfying the WGC under their assumptions.

Conjecture 2, the Minimal WGC, states that towers of (super-)extremal particles below the black-hole threshold exist if and only if dimensional-reduction consistency requires them. The proposed cases are emergent-string limits, reductions with KK gauge bosons, and strongly coupled limits with exactly extremal states; the exhaustive converse remains conjectural.

This is a source-scoped no_relation assessment; it excludes claims of logical independence of the full theories, extrapolation through the black-hole threshold, and independent certification of either endpoint.

They reach D7-brane branch cuts at finite ξ, rather than falling into the Poincaré horizon, and transform their charges on crossing. The supersymmetric segments form loops along the boundary of Σ without reaching the AdS conformal boundary.

endpoints.text: In the RN numerical examples, negative ε lowers the extremal mass and increases entropy, reducing M/Q; positive ε reverses these trends. Larger l makes reaching M<Q easier in the illustrated family. The authors describe these results as WGC-like, using an imported positive-entropy criterion.

At leading positive β, the paper finds increased entropy at fixed (M,Q) and decreased extremal mass, Mext=Q−β/(20Q)+O(β²). These satisfy the imported entropy/mass criteria used to motivate EBI as a WGC toy model.

records.exactAssertion: Left→right analogy only: the left source's interpretation of entropy increase accompanying reduced extremal mass and M/Q for negative ε is analogous to the right source's leading-positive-β interpretation of increased fixed-(M,Q) entropy and reduced extremal mass. This edge compares the reported WGC diagnostic practice. It does not identify the entropy ensembles, deformation parameters, undeformed extremality curves or theories. It excludes equivalence, specialization, cross-model evidential support, a transferred WGC proof, any instability or decay conclusion, and any right-hand counterpart of the left l-dependent numerical trend.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints concern four-dimensional, static, spherically symmetric, electrically charged black holes and interpret deformation-induced entropy and extremal-mass shifts using an imported WGC criterion. The intersection is this diagnostic practice, rather than a common deformed theory.

The comparison retains separate applicability domains: the left illustrated extremal family has a=1, Q=1, ωq=-2/3 and l=0.1, 0.2, 0.3; the right entropy calculation is a small-β expansion at fixed (M,Q), while its extremal-mass expansion is at fixed Q.

required_assumptions.statement: Define each mass shift relative to that theory's zero-deformation extremal solution at fixed positive electric charge. Hold a, l and ωq fixed on the left. Do not identify the two undeformed extremality curves.

Retain the entropy comparison specified by each source. In particular, the left Fig. 3 entropy is labeled Sext, whereas the right Eq. (8) entropy shift holds (M,Q) fixed. They are not interchangeable entropy variations.

Restrict the local algebra checks to small deformations on the displayed black-hole branches: ε<0 near zero on the left, and β>0 with β/Q² small on the right. For the right fixed-(M,Q) entropy expansion, take μ=M/Q>1 fixed away from the singular μ=1 endpoint.
Treat the WGC interpretation as an attribution to the papers. The analogy does not assume that either imported entropy criterion has been proved applicable to the other model.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly supplies the illustrated fixed-parameter family, labels its extremal quantities, and describes negative ε as increasing entropy and lowering extremal mass and M/Q.
The right source explicitly distinguishes its fixed-(M,Q) entropy expansion from its T=0 extremal-mass calculation and states the leading positive-β sign pair.

The supplied equations permit local mass-sign checks within each theory without a cross-theory parameter map: the left reported extremal derivative is positive with respect to ε, and the right leading derivative is negative with respect to β.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left deformation rescales a negative cosmological constant in Einstein-Maxwell theory with quintessence. The right deformation changes the electromagnetic Lagrangian through a Born-Infeld coupling in an asymptotically Minkowski solution.

The entropy ensembles differ. Indeed, the right Eqs. (7) and (10) imply Sext=π(Q²-β/2), which decreases for positive β at fixed Q, despite the positive fixed-(M,Q) entropy correction. This prevents identifying the two endpoints as the same extremal-entropy statement.
The left numerical dependence on the AdS radius l has no corresponding parameter or established conclusion in the assigned right endpoint.

endpoints.text: In A2-S1±, D8- and D6-branes with suitable non-diluted flux and orientation yield Q > T in the constructions analysed. The authors interpret the resulting independent membrane charge sectors as satisfying the sharpened WGC and indicating non-perturbative instability, subject to existence and control conditions.

The proposed general type II mechanism relates magnetic Fn flux to a wrapped D(8−n)-brane particle, with L⁻¹∼|fn|e^((5−n)φ/4)/Vol[Σn] and T_eff∼e^((5−n)φ/4)/Vol[Σn]. Its stated scope includes model-dependent curvature coefficients and the exceptional D3 diagnostic.

records.exactAssertion: Analogy only, left to right: the A2-S1± fluxed D8/D6 construction is a structural analogue of the right mechanism in using internally wrapped type II D-branes as external codimension-one defects associated with flux sectors. The edge asserts no quantitative charge/tension dictionary, derivation or support of the AdS2 no-go from Q>T, historical method dependence, common vacuum, or tension between the scale-separation conclusions. The direction only presents the left construction as an analogue of the right mechanism.

intersection.statement: The intersection is structural: type II flux compactifications contain internally wrapped D-branes that appear as codimension-one defects in the external theory. This establishes no common lower-dimensional vacuum.

Both descriptions connect the lower-dimensional defects to background flux sectors: the left discusses induced flux-quantum shifts, while the right identifies the electric source dual to a magnetic flux.

required_assumptions.statement: Retain the left statement as conditional on existence of admissible quantized bound states, appropriate flux and orientation, and the source's approximation. The analogy does not assume that such states have been constructed in every A2-S1± vacuum.

Retain the right mechanism's hypotheses: the stated flux-supported curvature scaling, flux quantization, the internal metric split assumed in (4.42), and transverse internal smearing. Its curvature-based mass diagnostic excludes n=5.

Any accompanying right-hand no-scale-separation conclusion remains conditional on the stated supersymmetric setting and fundamental BPS domain walls whose tension bounds the cutoff. These conditions are not transferred to the left endpoint.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The source descriptions establish the wrapped-brane dimensions needed for the structural comparison: D8 on X6 and D6 on a divisor give membranes in four dimensions; D(8−n) wrapping its internal spatial directions gives a particle in two dimensions.

The qualifications used in this comparison are explicit source qualifications: left-hand existence is conditional, the right D3 curvature diagnostic is exceptional, and the right no-go relies on fundamental BPS walls. This checks faithful scope, not realization of all physical hypotheses.

scope_mismatches.statement: The assigned left claim concerns non-supersymmetric A2-S1± AdS4 vacua; the right no-go concerns AdS2 with at least two preserved supercharges. The right source explicitly describes its argument as specific to two dimensions.

Left worldvolume flux creates bound states and induced lower-brane charges. Right Fn is a bulk magnetic field strength. Their appearances of flux do not identify the fields, cycles, or charge normalizations.

The left compares membrane charge with tension to diagnose superextremality. The right compares a curvature scale with a particle mass parameter and, conditionally, an EFT cutoff. These are different inequalities and physical conclusions.
The left's reported geometric scale separation and the right's obstruction to a two-dimensional cutoff hierarchy do not constitute a shared-regime tension.

limitations: This is a comparison of the supplied spans and six images, not an independent reproduction of either full physical argument. Node metadata and earlier review assertions are not used as scientific premises.

Universal existence of the left A2 bound states is excluded: physical page 23 explicitly makes existence conditional and identifies dependence on stabilized Kähler moduli (acb6ae44fd1d1fd1d353:p0023s002; image:1).

A quantitative inter-paper map would require the left membrane definitions in section 4.1, equations (4.2), (4.3), and (4.12), and a specified dimensional reduction relating the backgrounds. The supplied footnote already distinguishes ten-dimensional and four-dimensional charges; this additional work is needed only for the excluded stronger identification (acb6ae44fd1d1fd1d353:p0017s002; image:3).

The left DBI expansions and numerical extrema on physical pages 24–25 were not independently verified from page images or recomputed. Their qualitative Q>T conclusion is corroborated by the supplied conclusion image (acb6ae44fd1d1fd1d353:p0024s001; acb6ae44fd1d1fd1d353:p0025s001; acb6ae44fd1d1fd1d353:p0027s001; image:2).

The right scaling argument is not certified for arbitrary flux backgrounds: its curvature coefficient depends on the model, its reduction assumes an internal metric split, and its D3 curvature diagnostic fails at n=5 (b01d405e4a24b057dbbf:p0021s001; b01d405e4a24b057dbbf:p0021s002; b01d405e4a24b057dbbf:p0022s001; images:4–5).

No extension of the right no-go to the left non-supersymmetric AdS4 vacua is asserted. The right source expressly restricts its argument to two dimensions and invokes fundamental BPS walls and a cutoff bound (b01d405e4a24b057dbbf:p0022s002; image:5).

endpoints.text: The authors propose that LWGC violation entails fractionally charged monopoles confined by flux tubes. Across the studied examples, the dual of their magnetic superlattice is populated everywhere by superextremal electric states. This is a guaranteed sublattice, not a claim that every superextremal state lies within it.

In the second orbifold, the Wilson-line-free SU(9) monopoles are unstable. An alternative Wilson line yields (SU(7) × U(1)²)/Z14 and a genuine topologically stable monopole with Dirac pairing 4/3 against one specified LWGC-violating charge in the original Wilson-line vacuum. Assumed wall transport therefore supplies a confined fractional monopole for that charge.

records.exactAssertion: Defer a directed scientific-support edge. The right source reports its specified monopole as an example supporting the left proposal, and the supplied vectors independently reproduce the fractional pairing 4/3. However, establishing a confined object in the original vacuum requires the asserted transport between the particular e₂ and e₁ heterotic Wilson-line vacua. The supplied explicit transport construction does not establish that extension. Thus the packet establishes an algebraically consistent candidate and a reported conditional connection, but supplies insufficient evidence for physical right-to-left support. This assessment excludes a universal proof, full dual-sublattice population or equality, and splitting–tension bounds.

intersection.statement: The shared content is the association between LWGC violation, a surviving superextremal sublattice, and magnetic charges with fractional Dirac pairing. The right paper formulates the nonabelian charge-lattice comparison using a Cartan subgroup.

The selected example concerns one charge in the original Wilson-line vacuum and one monopole in an alternative Wilson-line vacuum. The physical confinement conclusion requires transport between those vacua; the fractional pairing alone does not construct a monopole in the original vacuum.

missing_assumptions: For physical support of the existential confinement claim, the supplied material does not establish an admissible domain wall between the specific e₂ and e₁ heterotic vacua that transports the stated monopole while retaining its fractional pairing. The right paper asserts this application of the earlier argument, but the supplied explicit construction concerns a different, discrete-gauge-theory setting.

required_assumptions.statement: The lightest state of charge q in Eq. (82) is subextremal in the regime under consideration, as reported by the right source.

The vector q_mag in Eq. (83) represents an actual genuine, topologically stable monopole of the alternative vacuum with the specified global gauge-group quotient, rather than merely an allowed Lie-algebra charge.

The wall-transport construction must extend to this particular pair of heterotic Wilson lines and produce a physical confined endpoint with the nonintegral pairing of Eq. (84). This extension is asserted, but not established by the supplied construction.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The two explicit vectors and their relative normalization are available: image:4 fixes q = (−2,−2,1,−1,−1,−1,0,0)/3, and image:5 fixes q_mag = (−3,5,5,−1,−3,−3,−3,3)/2. Their displayed dot product is reproducible.

The source distinguishes Dirac-allowed charges, topological stability, and confined fractional charges. It explicitly reports genuineness and stability in the donor vacuum; these properties have not been independently certified here.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left endpoint includes a guarantee of superextremal occupation throughout a dual sublattice. The selected right calculation concerns one electric–magnetic pair and cannot establish that lattice-wide guarantee.

The supplied explicit transport recipe connects Wilson-line-off and Wilson-line-on phases of compactified Z_p gauge theory. The selected example instead requires transport between two different nonzero Wilson lines in a heterotic orbifold. Its applicability needs justification.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Fractional monopole charges lie outside Γ̃ and have physical Dirac strings; Eq. (84) diagnoses fractionality by q·q_mag = 4/3.

endpoints.text: Adding supersymmetry to either duality gives vanishing extremality shifts for black holes carrying only gravity-multiplet photon charge, as expected for BPS states. In the heterotic O(d,d) example β=−2α; the gravity-multiplet embedding cancels the shift, while the vector-multiplet embedding gives a positive shift.

For minimally coupled massless matter of spin ≤1, the one-loop contribution to the stress-tensor-squared coefficient has the sign that increases extremal charge-to-mass ratios in the deep IR. N=1 supergravity also gives positive running; extended-supergravity graviphoton running instead cancels. Consequently logarithmic running alone does not establish a strictly positive shift in every supersymmetric theory.

records.exactAssertion: Right to left: the extended-supergravity cancellation of the local one-loop four-graviphoton UV/running coefficient is structurally analogous to the left paper's vanishing leading four-derivative extremality shift for gravity-multiplet charge after imposing the specified duality and supersymmetry. The explicit comparison is the right N=2 complete-multiplet sums against the left heterotic O(d,d) gravity-multiplet branch. This asserts neither equality of actions, charges or operators nor an implication from zero running to zero finite or full extremality correction. N=1, matter-photon charged sectors and all-loop claims are excluded.

intersection.statement: Both calculations concern four-dimensional gravitational EFTs with extended supersymmetry and a protected sector involving photons in gravity multiplets. This establishes common sector descriptors, not an identical action or black-hole solution.

The comparison concerns cancellations involving positive and negative contributions in supersymmetric gravity-photon sectors: contributions to an extremality shift on the left and to a local one-loop UV coefficient on the right.

required_assumptions.statement: The left cancellation is restricted to supersymmetry added to the specified duality-preserving higher-derivative action and to the gravity-multiplet embedding.
The explicit left algebra uses the regular, sufficiently large dyonic solutions with a controlled derivative expansion, at leading order in the higher-derivative coefficients.
The right cancellation includes complete extended-supergravity multiplets and their required nonminimal interactions; the minimally coupled spin-at-most-one contributions cannot be used alone.
The comparison preserves the distinction between a vanishing local one-loop running coefficient and a vanishing leading extremality correction. It does not infer the latter from the former.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Section 4.4 explicitly selects the heterotic O(d,d) gravity-multiplet embedding, and the discussion limits the analysis to dominant higher-derivative terms respecting the chosen duality.

The left source supplies regular dyonic backgrounds and states the large-charge condition controlling the derivative expansion. The explicit cancellation below does not require a singular single-charge limit.

The right N=2 table includes the gravity, Maxwell and hypermultiplet contributions separately and identifies the nonminimal couplings responsible for negative matter contributions; image:5 confirms the table signs.
Equations (7) and (23) distinguish logarithmic running from finite UV matching contributions, allowing the analogy to be stated without equating their observables.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left result concerns the extremality shift from a correlated four-derivative action; the right protected quantity is a one-loop local UV/logarithmic coefficient. Zero running leaves finite matching contributions undetermined.

The explicit left heterotic cancellation uses an N=4 gravity-multiplet embedding; the right cancellation table is N=2. The left also discusses an N=2 SL(2,R) setup, but no common truncation is established here.

Negative higher-derivative contributions to the left extremality functional are not identified with the right gravitino or dimension-five nonminimal loop interactions. Their cancellation roles are analogous, without an operator dictionary.

The displayed left solution has electric and magnetic charges in different U(1) fields; the right RN formula uses electric and magnetic charges of a Maxwell field. A common charged background is not established.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify only the multiplet role. No numerical field normalization or charge-lattice identification is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The heterotic top-sign embedding places the gauge fields in the N=4 gravity multiplet; in the SL(2,R) discussion A1 belongs to the N=2 gravity multiplet.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Fg denotes the graviphoton field strength; the external photons in the protected four-graviphoton amplitude belong to the supergravity sector.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the vanishing of the respective quantities structurally. A zero one-loop UV coefficient is not an equation for the left extremality shift.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Delta z_L denotes z_ext minus its two-derivative value 1, evaluated at leading order in the higher-derivative Wilson coefficients.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: C_R is an auxiliary notation introduced here for the summed local one-loop UV coefficient. Equation (7) gives the corresponding common large-log term as minus C_R times log(s/mu^2).

conventionDictionary.conversion: There is no supplied numerical map between alpha or beta and a. Equality of their symbols, magnitudes or renormalization properties is not assumed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Alpha and beta parameterize the O(d,d)-invariant four-derivative action. The SL(2,R) discussion instead uses alpha_abcd, alpha_ab, alpha_1 and alpha_2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: a multiplies the photon stress-tensor square in Eq. (4); a_1 and a_2 multiply the two quartic photon invariants. The N=2 table labels contributions to the UV coefficient by a.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Image:1 resolves the minus sign in the protected top branch of Eq. (4.45). Image:4 fixes the minus sign preceding the common logarithm, and image:5 fixes the alternating signs in the N=2 table.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (4.45) is z_ext = 1 + 4 alpha (1 ∓ 1)/[5p(p+q)]. The gravity-multiplet branch takes 1 minus 1.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: For a positive summed UV coefficient, minus C_R log(s/mu^2) is positive in the deep IR. In extended supergravity the summed coefficient instead vanishes.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Only the source-normalized baseline value 1 is used. Raw Q, P, q, p and mass parameters are not identified between papers.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Q = 4 pi q and P = 4 pi p; the displayed solution assigns electric charge to A1 and magnetic charge to A2. Equation (4.45) normalizes the uncorrected extremal ratio to 1.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Q and P in Eq. (5) are RN electric and magnetic charges, with the extremal ratio normalized to 1 at two derivatives.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The Einstein-term normalization can be aligned by setting kappa^2 = 8 pi G_N = 1. No Weyl transformation or dimensional conversion of Wilson coefficients is performed for the analogy.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Four spacetime dimensions with reduced Planck units 8 pi G_N = 1. The displayed action used for the black-hole calculation has Einstein term R/2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell normalization R/(2 kappa^2) minus F^2/4; higher-derivative couplings are rescaled with appropriate powers of kappa^2 to be dimensionless, and Eq. (5) sets kappa^2 = 1.

limitations: The checks reproduce substitution and coefficient sums, not the black-hole thermodynamic calculation or the unitarity-cut derivation. The relevant methods are reported in 97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0008s001, 97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0008s002 and b8581b5e3a6a76cfd8eb:p0008s001.

Those identifications are excluded from the exact assertion; zero local running alone does not provide them (97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0016s002; b8581b5e3a6a76cfd8eb:p0008s001; b8581b5e3a6a76cfd8eb:p0014s001).

This comparison uses the detailed gravity-photon result and does not resolve the abstract's broader wording (b8581b5e3a6a76cfd8eb:p0001s001; b8581b5e3a6a76cfd8eb:p0010s001).

The left SL(2,R) gravity-charge conclusion is retained as a reported source assertion. No independent regular single-charge black-hole limit is reconstructed from its displayed two-charge solution (97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0007s001; 97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0016s001; 97cfc8141e4436433f7b:p0016s002).
Node labels, inherited reviews and provenance metadata were not treated as independent scientific validation. Coverage is limited to the supplied spans and checked images.

endpoints.text: Applying the area prescription to this stretched surface gives A ≃ 4πm0C/g and SBH ≃ (2πC/g)√(m² − QL²/(8g²)), rather than the zero entropy obtained directly from the classical horizon area.

The reviewed cubic-prepotential attractor solution in the p0=0 sector gives the macroscopic area entropy S=2π√(Dq̂0), with q̂0=q0+(1/12)D^{AB}qAqB and horizon moduli determined by charges rather than their asymptotic values.

records.exactAssertion: Left-to-right analogy only: the left stretched-horizon prescription is analogous to the right cubic-attractor entropy in assigning macroscopic entropy through an area prescription for charged extremal four-dimensional black holes. The left uses a proposed string-scale stretched surface despite zero classical horizon area; the right uses the classical horizon in its stated semiclassical p^0=0 sector. This is a comparison of source prescriptions within their separate scopes. It asserts no numerical equality, shared charge dictionary, specialization, dependence on the other endpoint's method, or evidential support for the other endpoint. It excludes applying the right cubic formula to the left string-scale surface and excludes inferring the right attractor mechanism from the left cutoff argument.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints assign macroscopic entropy through an area prescription for charged extremal black holes in four dimensions. This establishes a source-level analogy; the supplied evidence does not establish a common solution or controlled physical regime.

required_assumptions.statement: Read the left endpoint as a proposed stretched-surface prescription, retaining its near-horizon approximation and string-tree-level setting. Its strong-field cutoff is a worldsheet/target-space criterion, not a claim that the spacetime string coupling becomes large. At the chosen surface, the near-horizon approximation requires C/g much smaller than m0.

Read the right endpoint as the leading classical cubic-prepotential result with p^0=0 and an invertible D_AB. Its controlled M-theory interpretation requires large R and V_M in eleven-dimensional Planck units, large horizon two-cycles, P inside the Kahler cone, qhat_0^3 much greater than D, and D much greater than V_M.

The comparison retains each paper's own surface, charges, constants and units. It assumes no identification of the two symbols C, no charge dictionary, and no continuation of either formula outside its stated approximation.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly distinguishes the zero-area classical event horizon from the proposed stretched surface, specifies the canonical Einstein metric, and defines the displayed entropy from the stretched area. Images image:1 and image:2 confirm the surface distinction and entropy formula.

The right source explicitly identifies a four-dimensional N=2 extremal horizon, charge-determined horizon moduli, the p^0=0 cubic sector, and its leading-action validity conditions. Images image:4 and image:5 confirm the physical setting, positive square-root entropy and stated hierarchies. These are source-stated conditions, not a verification of a particular numerical solution.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left formula concerns toroidally compactified heterotic theory and a stretched surface placed where string-scale effects become important. The right formula concerns M-theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold times S^1 and a classical horizon in a long-wavelength, weak-curvature regime. The zero classical area on the left and nonzero area in the right's controlled sector therefore do not establish a tension.

In the displayed frames, the left solutions are electrically charged, whereas the right controlled sector includes magnetic p^A encoded by a nonzero Kahler class P. Setting all p^A to zero on the right gives D=0 and D_AB=0, invalidating the inverse-matrix solution and the stated large-D regime. This excludes a naive same-frame purely electric specialization, without excluding an unprovided duality.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both effective black holes are four-dimensional. No compactification or duality identification is made.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Four-dimensional theory obtained by toroidal compactification of heterotic string theory; image:3 confirms this scope.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M-theory on M times S^1, with M a Calabi-Yau threefold and precisely N=2 spacetime supersymmetry; image:4 confirms this scope.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare only the use of an area prescription. Do not equate the two areas or identify their surfaces.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: A is the stretched-sphere area calculated with canonical Einstein metric g_mu_nu=exp(-Phi)G_mu_nu; G_mu_nu is the string metric. The classical event-horizon area vanishes.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Area is the black-hole horizon area entering the leading four-dimensional supergravity entropy in section 2.1. No metric transformation identifying it with the left geometry is supplied.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The common formal normalization is S=A/(4G_N), retaining a separate Newton constant and length unit for each theory. No numerical cross-paper unit conversion is needed for the analogy.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Image:2 resolves equation (37) as S=A/(4G_N)=pi*m0*C/(2g). Together with equation (36), this implies numerical G_N=2 in the source's units at the displayed order.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (2.4) writes S=Area/4, absorbing the four-dimensional Newton constant into the area units. Image:5 confirms S=2*pi*sqrt(D*qhat_0). Internal volumes and R are separately discussed in eleven-dimensional Planck units.

conventionDictionary.left_definition: c_* is a pure numerical cutoff constant in rhobar=c_* and rho=c_*/g, as confirmed by image:2. The microscopic comparison later selects c_*=4; the cutoff argument itself does not fix that value.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: C_att is the complex quantity appearing in p^Lambda=Re(C_att*X^Lambda) and q_Lambda=Re(C_att*F_Lambda), with the section convention stated below equation (2.8).

The inverse-index placement is reconstructed from the extracted inverse relation, not checked against an attached image of physical page 3.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: F=D_ABC*X^A*X^B*X^C/X^0; 6D_ABC=integral_M alpha_A wedge alpha_B wedge alpha_C; D=D_ABC*p^A*p^B*p^C; qhat_0=q_0+(1/12)D^{AB}q_A*q_B. The plus sign is the paper's convention, not a positivity claim about the quadratic form. q_0 is S^1 momentum, p^A specify the wrapped four-cycle, and q_A arise from the fivebrane tensor field.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Leading entropy is expressed using charge-determined horizon moduli and cubic intersection data.

endpoints.text: For the assumed single critical string and modular/quasi-modular flux, the authors give a tree-level proof of an infinite super-extremal tower becoming light at weak coupling. The charge–mass inequality matches the relevant dilatonic black-hole threshold, including scalar effects.

The illustrative heterotic T⁶ spectrum has q=gn and m²=g²(n²−1) for positive integers n, producing a superextremal tower approaching extremality. The stronger tower WGC is conjectural generally; the review reports proofs for U(1)s arising from perturbative string physics, with general nonperturbative cases still open.

records.exactAssertion: The left paper's reported conditional result supplies a restricted example supporting the right review's general infinite-superextremal-tower phenomenon: for its nonzero charged-seed orbits, assumed single critical string, compatible (quasi-)modular flux, and tree-level weak-coupling regime, the reported physical tower satisfies the scalar-corrected dilatonic threshold. This support uses the left paper's asymptotic effectively massless gauge interpretation and each theory's own normalized extremality ratio. It does not derive the right T^6 spectrum, identify the compactifications or charge lattices, prove the review's universal perturbative statement, establish a large-charge black-hole crossover, settle general nonperturbative cases, or assert an exact infinite-size black-hole limit at fixed nonzero Stückelberg mass. The relation compares reported conditional results; it does not independently certify the left geometric hypotheses or their full derivation.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints concern an infinite tower charged under a selected four-dimensional U(1), with superextremality assessed relative to a black-hole threshold. The intersection is this tower property, rather than an identified compactification or spectrum.

The comparison uses each theory's own scalar-dependent extremality threshold. The left dilatonic threshold is compatible with the review's definition, which expressly allows massless scalars to modify extremality.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the left result to its stipulated single critical-string geometry, compatible (quasi-)modular flux, and a nonzero charged seed orbit. The curve conditions referenced as (3.27) and (6.17) remain hypotheses of the reported result; their existence in arbitrary geometries is not asserted.
Use the critical-string mass relation and the authors' interpretation of the charged left-moving orbits as physical, level-matched states only at tree level and weak coupling.

Use the left paper's asymptotic effectively massless gauge interpretation, justified by the suppressed Stückelberg mass. Do not replace it with an exact massless-photon statement at finite coupling or an infinite-size black-hole limit at fixed nonzero Stückelberg mass.

Interpret support as an additional restricted realization of the review's tower-WGC phenomenon. A restricted example does not establish the review's reported theorem for all perturbative U(1)s or settle general nonperturbative cases.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The source explicitly states the single-curve and (quasi-)modularity hypotheses, reports D-term compatibility for these fluxes, and describes nonzero seed charges ±1 and ±2 in its example. Image:1 confirms the conditional scope. This establishes the scope of the reported example, not an independent geometric existence proof.

Equation (6.30) supplies the weak-coupling mass relation. The conclusion explicitly explains physical level matching despite massive-level cancellations in the parity-odd partition function and restricts its protection and WGC proof to tree level; checked in image:2.

Image:3 confirms M_St ~ t^(-s) M_KK with s=3 or 3/2 for modular or quasi-modular flux, respectively, and the stated energy interval M_St ≤ E ≤ M_KK. Thus the source supplies an asymptotic gauge regime for its comparison.

The review distinguishes its general tower conjecture from examples and reported perturbative proofs, permits scalar-dependent thresholds and equality, and leaves nonperturbative cases open in full generality. Images:5 and :6 confirm these qualifications.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left setting is chiral four-dimensional N=1 F-theory with an emergent heterotic string; the right illustrative spectrum is SO(32) heterotic theory on T^6 with a selected U(1) inside U(1)^16. No identification of these compactifications is supplied.

The left construction supplies shifted charge orbits and index gaps; the right example reports a state for every positive integer charge label. Index gaps on the left do not establish absence of physical states in other sectors.

The left gauge interpretation is asymptotic because the photon generally has a Stückelberg mass. The review defines its threshold using infinitely large black holes. The proposed support concerns the limiting effectively massless comparator, without equating these limits at finite coupling.
A restricted construction involving nonperturbative heterotic ingredients and a tree-level weak-coupling spectrum does not settle the general nonperturbative problem left open by the review.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Write the left charge as r and its coupling-included magnitude as e_L=g_YM|r|. Write the right illustrative charge as e_R=gN. Compare charge-to-mass ratios normalized by their respective extremality thresholds; do not identify g with g_YM across compactifications.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The review's example includes the coupling in q=g n; its general WGC definition uses physical charge-to-mass ratios.

conventionDictionary.concept: Mass, excitation level, and Jacobi index
conventionDictionary.conversion: Rename left m as I, left excitation number as n_L, right mass as μ_R, and right integer label as N. There is no established map n_L=N or n_L=N^2. In units with c=ℏ=1, T has mass dimension two and M_L and M_Pl have mass dimension one; the review writes its spectrum in its chosen natural units.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: m is the Jacobi index, n labels excitation level, and M_n^2=8πT(n−1), with T=2π vol(C_0).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: m is particle mass, while n is a positive integer charge label in m^2=g^2(n^2−1). Image:4 confirms the minus-one shift and the square on n.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Define R_L=g_YM|r|M_Pl/M_L using the reported d=4 threshold, and R_R=(e_R/μ_R)/γ_R using the review's threshold. The common predicate is R≥1. This removes the need to equate Planck conventions or raw charge normalizations between vacua.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The Einstein-frame dilatonic comparator has g_YM^2 Q_BH^2/M_ADM^2=1/M_Pl^(d−2), equation (6.41), hence 1/M_Pl^2 in four dimensions. This includes the scalar contribution.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: γ_R=lim_(M→∞)(Q/M)_ext may depend on massless scalars. The T^6 illustration uses a normalization with threshold Q=M. Image:6 confirms the general scalar qualification.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use absolute charges and nonnegative masses. A positive excess above the squared threshold gives strict superextremality for massive states; the general tower property also allows saturation. Treat massless charged seeds without dividing by zero.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The seed charges are ±ℓ, with ℓ≠0, and the orbit identity has positive offset ℓ^2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The example takes N>0. The review explicitly includes extremal states in its term 'superextremal' and chooses positive charge representatives.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use the left result only as an asymptotic effectively gauged realization. Image:3 resolves the inverse power M_St~t^(−s)M_KK and specifies s=3 or 3/2. No exact finite-coupling massless-photon identification is made.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The U(1) generally acquires a Stückelberg mass, parametrically suppressed for (quasi-)modular flux in the weak-coupling limit.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The general WGC definition compares a U(1)-charged particle with a large extremal black hole.

An independent geometric derivation is explicitly excluded. It would require 1901.08065 equations (3.14), (3.27), and (6.17), including their definitions and hypotheses; here the reported inequality (6.31) is used as a conditional source result [7e45443491d5a09b0d16:p0037s002; 7e45443491d5a09b0d16:p0039s002].

The light-tower statement means that each fixed excitation level becomes light as T→0; it does not mean every member of an infinite tower lies below a fixed cutoff simultaneously [7e45443491d5a09b0d16:p0039s002].

endpoints.text: For the exponential Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton setting, an extremal charged black hole obeys a charge-to-ADM-mass relation with μ = (d−3)/(d−2) + α·α/4. The reviewed Sublattice WGC requires physical states on at least a finite-index charge sublattice to meet or exceed that bound. The source states that this condition implies the Convex Hull Condition and is stable under dimensional reduction.

In two-derivative Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton gravity, subextremal black holes are self-attractive and extremal black holes have zero long-range self-force. The scalar charge is the mass derivative at fixed quantized charge and entropy.

records.exactAssertion: The right black-hole calculation supports the extremality coefficient used by the left, restricted to their common classical, two-derivative, asymptotically flat, single-electric-U(1), single-massless-dilaton sector in d=D≥4 with nonzero dilaton coupling. Matching actions by χ_L−χ_L0=−(ϕ_R−ϕ_R0)/√2, a_L=√2 a_R, M_Pl^(D−2)=κ_D^−2 and f_L(χ_L0)^−1=e₀², the right's fixed-(q,S) scalar charge and extremal vanishing leading self-force recover Q²/f_L=μ_L M_ADM²/M_Pl^(D−2), with μ_L=(D−3)/(D−2)+a_L²/4. This supports only the left endpoint's black-hole benchmark. It excludes sublattice population, the Convex Hull Condition and dimensional-reduction claims, generic particle self-repulsion, and equivalence of the WGC and RFC.

intersection.statement: The common domain is classical, two-derivative, asymptotically flat Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton gravity in d=D≥4, restricted to one electric U(1) and one active massless dilaton with an exponential gauge kinetic term.

Compare the extremal limit of the displayed charged black-hole family at the same asymptotic scalar background. The relevant mass is the black-hole ADM mass, and the scalar response is evaluated at fixed quantized charge and entropy.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the left theory to one photon and one scalar χ with gχχ=1, and compare it with the right action (5.1). Take a nonzero dilaton coupling for the manipulations involving division by that coupling.
Identify the gauge potential and electric charge unit, match the Einstein terms, and evaluate the gauge coupling at the same asymptotic scalar value.

Use the right source's displayed black-hole family and its fixed-(q,S) scalar response, taking extremality as r+=r−. Do not substitute an arbitrary particle mass function for this black-hole response.
Interpret self-force as the leading large-separation force between two identical objects, with only the displayed massless gauge, gravitational and scalar exchanges retained.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The selected single-field member of the left action and right equation (5.1) match under the explicit scalar and gravitational normalization dictionary below. This is a restriction of the comparison, not a claim about arbitrary multi-field models.
The left fixes its extremality formula at the asymptotic scalar value; the right explicitly varies the asymptotic coupling while holding quantized charge and horizon area, hence entropy, fixed.
Equations (5.4), (5.8)–(5.11) supply the black-hole mass, scalar charge, force criterion and extremal specialization needed for the restricted reconstruction.

Both sources provide leading-force conventions with the same positive sphere-volume denominator. Image:5 confirms that vanishing of this coefficient is distinct from vanishing of the complete finite-distance force.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left additionally postulates physical states on a charge sublattice and reports consequences for the Convex Hull Condition and dimensional reduction. The right black-hole calculation does not establish those population statements.
A generic particle's scalar dependence is separate input. The right explicitly warns that zero long-range force between extremal black holes does not imply equivalence of the WGC and RFC.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Set d=D≥4 and M_Pl^(D−2)=κ_D^−2 by matching the constant Einstein–Hilbert coefficients. The calculation uses κ_D directly and does not require an inferred definition of the right source's separate symbol M_D.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (2.1) has Einstein coefficient M_Pl^(d−2)/2 and scalar coefficient −M_Pl^(d−2)gχχ/2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (5.1) has Einstein coefficient 1/(2κ_D²) and scalar coefficient −1/(4κ_D²).

conventionDictionary.concept: Dilaton coordinate, exponent sign and normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: Choose χ−χ₀=−(ϕ−ϕ₀)/√2 and a_L=√2 a_R. Both kinetic terms and exponential gauge terms then match. Consequently a_L²/4=a_R²/2. Reversing the scalar coordinate explains the exponent sign; it does not change the squared coupling.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: In the selected gχχ=1 sector, f_L=f₀ exp[a_L(χ−χ₀)] and μ_scalar=a_L²/4. Image:1 confirms the factor 1/4 in (2.5).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Write the right scalar as ϕ and its coupling as a_R to distinguish them from left symbols: f_R∝exp(−a_Rϕ), with kinetic term −(∂ϕ)²/(4κ_D²).

conventionDictionary.concept: Gauge kinetic coefficient and electric charge
conventionDictionary.conversion: Use the same A and electric charge unit, Q_L=q_R. Absorb the reference scalar value into e₀ so f₀=e₀^−2 and Q_L²/f₀=e₀²q_R². The form term −f F∧*F/2 corresponds to the component term −f FμνF^μν/4.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: f^{ab} is the inverse gauge kinetic matrix; in one U(1), the charge norm is Q²/f. Particle charges appear in ∂+iqA.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The component gauge coefficient is e^−2 exp(−a_Rϕ); q is the quantized charge held fixed during scalar variation.

conventionDictionary.concept: Mass, extremality coefficient and symbol collisions
conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify M_ADM,L=m_BH,R and μ_L=γ_R^−1 after the action dictionary. Do not identify the left particle mass in (2.7) with a specified scalar-dependent black-hole mass function.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: μ_L=(D−3)/(D−2)+a_L²/4 multiplies M_ADM²/M_Pl^(D−2).

endpoints.text: Expand metric and four-form perturbations in internal harmonics, decompose forms into primitive transverse pieces and lower-rank derivatives, fix diffeomorphism and three-form gauge freedom, and diagonalize the linearized Einstein-Maxwell equations. This determines the bosonic KK spectrum in terms of internal operator eigenvalues.

Explicit modes are generated from scalar harmonics using differential operators and Sp1 projectors. Diagonalisation, divergences, scalar products and vanishing norms determine transverse spectra and exceptional low-label irreps; two-form construction requires symmetrised second derivatives.

records.exactAssertion: The left method has a procedural analogue in the right method, restricted to organizing internal form sectors, imposing their respective transverse constraints, and forming linear combinations that resolve spectral mixing. The left then diagonalizes coupled spacetime perturbation equations; the right explicitly constructs and diagonalizes internal scalar-generated form modes and checks their existence. This is analogy_only. It excludes equality of spectra, geometric specialization, transfer of Kähler identities, demonstrated use of one endpoint's method by the other, and any transfer of stability conclusions. The arrow records the comparison from left to right, without asserting historical influence or logical implication.

The left diagonalization resolves coupled spacetime perturbation equations and physical AdS5 masses. The selected right construction diagonalizes internal form operators and determines their representation content. These are different stages of a KK calculation.

endpoints.text: The authors speculate that a black hole allowed to grow without bound in the proposed theory eventually has negative entropy because its decreasing quantum correction defeats the growing area term. They interpret negative entropy as fewer than one microscopic state and suggest that the scalar theory is secretly nonunitary.

Classical Dominance proposes that, outside large extremal black holes in semiclassical theories consistent with quantum gravity, nonlocal corrections are much smaller than local corrections at the same order in black-hole mass. Its amplitude formulation also requires local coefficients to dominate logarithmic running coefficients.

records.exactAssertion: Left → right is analogy_only: the left's explicitly speculative interpretation of a scalar entropy correction overtaking area entropy during unbounded black-hole growth is a conceptual analogue of the right's conjectured exclusion of nonlocal/running quantum corrections overwhelming UV-sensitive local corrections outside large extremal black holes. The shared feature is a consistency motivation involving quantum dominance. This assertion excludes implication, equivalence, method use, a counterexample or tension between the conjectures, and any identification of entropy-versus-area dominance with the right's same-mass-order equation-of-motion hierarchy. Neither nonunitarity nor Classical Dominance is established.

intersection.statement: The nominal common setting is large charged extremal black holes, restricted here to four dimensions. This establishes a setting for comparison, not a common quantum-corrected solution.
Both passages connect a proposed hierarchy involving quantum corrections to a gravitational consistency concern. The quantities entering those hierarchies differ.

required_assumptions.statement: For the selected textual analogy, preserve the endpoints' declared epistemic status: the left is speculation and the right is a conjecture. Neither must be physically correct for this comparison of their reported motivations.

Retain the distinct meanings of dominance: scalar entropy correction versus leading area entropy on the left; nonlocal/running corrections versus local gravitational corrections at the same mass order on the right.
Do not assume the left's allegedly nonunitary candidate theory satisfies the right's hypothesis of a semiclassical theory consistent with quantum gravity.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The supplied passages explicitly identify speculation and conjecture respectively; image:1 and image:4 confirm those qualifications.
The source definitions establish the two different hierarchies. The proposed relation compares their consistency motivations without identifying their observables.
The scope restriction is retained: no quantum-gravity completion or unitary evolution is established for the left theory, so it is not placed inside the right conjecture's domain.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left concerns macroscopic black-hole entropy and its state-counting interpretation. The right concerns exterior expectation values determined by effective gravitational equations of motion.

The left compares a quantum contribution with the increasing Bekenstein–Hawking term. The right compares local and nonlocal corrections at the same order in black-hole mass; its local terms are not identified with the leading area term.

The left proposes an inconsistency of a WGC-violating scalar theory. The right is conjectured for theories consistent with quantum gravity and defines semiclassical quantum-field evolution as unitary. Their domains are not demonstrated to coincide.

The left extrapolates to unbounded growth, whereas its supplied backreaction estimate uses a small-perturbation expansion and defers a full semiclassical Einstein-equation analysis. The right's coefficient hierarchy does not supply that missing control of the entropy extrapolation.

limitations: This is a comparison of reported argument structures. It does not validate either conjecture or establish a controlled shared physical regime.

The node's explicit quartic-log entropy formula and earlier reviewers' technical criticisms were not promoted to verified source equations or findings. No charged-scalar determinant, counterterm calculation or asymptotic entropy coefficient was reproduced.

The left's required extrapolation of renormalized entropy, its microscopic state-counting interpretation and uniform control during unbounded growth remain unproved here. The supplied source limits its backreaction estimate to a small-perturbation expansion and defers a full semiclassical Einstein-equation analysis (ee2e32fdade8c327655e:p0020s001; ee2e32fdade8c327655e:p0020s002; ee2e32fdade8c327655e:p0022s001; ee2e32fdade8c327655e:p0022s002). These are limitations of excluded stronger physical claims, not premises needed for the textual analogy.

A stronger support or tension claim would require an operator-level decomposition of the scalar effective action, matched renormalized local coefficients and nonlocal terms, and a demonstrated connection between entropy and exterior gravitational response. None is assumed by this assertion (ee2e32fdade8c327655e:p0008s001; 1a46bf6ca59fc2cb9017:p0004s001; 1a46bf6ca59fc2cb9017:p0005s001).

Visual inspection covered only the five supplied images. Image:2 was inspected as context for the left's instanton discussion; its transition formulas were not used as a unitarity test. All other coverage is limited to the supplied spans.

endpoints.text: The paper tabulates nonzero non-extremal light-scalar cubic couplings and their conversion to CFT three-point coefficients. Most parity-allowed couplings are nonzero; in the supersymmetric discussion, c′_(φ₀φ_iφ_j)=0 is attributed tentatively to a possible supersymmetric Ward identity.

Recalling their companion CFT construction, the authors identify the universal multiplet with the isospin-singlet product of three short field-strength superfields. Its E=6 breathing component is represented by an N=3 supersymmetric completion of a cubic gauge-field-strength operator, together with auxiliary-field and derivative contributions.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied source scope, classify the two assigned claims as no_relation: the DGKT table and bulk-to-boundary conversion concern scalar interaction coefficients and three-point correlators, whereas the N=3 shadow construction identifies the constituent expression of one breathing-mode operator. Neither supplied endpoint provides a result or method used to establish the other. Shared AdS4/CFT3 language, dimension 6, and cubic expressions do not supply that connection. This assertion excludes operator identification, numerical coupling matching, a shared Ward/non-renormalization theorem, application of the left extremal-coupling criterion to the right compactification, and any claim that no connection could exist beyond this packet.

endpoints.text: For a nonnegative linear combination, at least one modulus increases exponentially in a shifted proper distance. A corresponding KK scale with the assumed decreasing power law has an exponentially bounded mass ratio. Rough geometric exponent estimates are given, without a universal lower-bound proof.

The paper illustrates the availability of many tower families using KK states on S1×S1. Along a fixed rational radius ratio, choosing integer momentum labels proportional to fixed integers produces a tower scaling as 1/R. This is an example of dense rational labels, not a derivation that all canonical gradient directions are independently populated.

This comparison excludes a specialization or derivation of the left distance bound, identification of the two compactifications or frames, equality of canonical decay exponents, identification of the printed Delta phi prime with reconstructed delta_M, and any inference of dense canonical gradient directions.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied derivations, no directed mathematical or methodological relation is established between these two assigned methods. The left rewrites localized-source contributions and estimates a regulated three-dimensional effective potential; the right uses a local Calabi-Yau blow-up metric and special Lagrangian conditions to track an O6 three-cycle. Their shared O6 subject matter does not identify a transferable calculation. In particular, the right geometric smoothing does not establish the string-theoretic source-core resolution assumed by the left. This packet-scoped assessment excludes claims of equivalence, specialization, method use, dynamical support or tension, and does not assert that the complete papers have no other relationship.

endpoints.text: Protected N=4 operators are matched to previously computed Type IIB KK harmonics. One family has Δ=k and m²=k(k−4), k≥2, in symmetric traceless SO(6) representations; the absence of k=1 is interpreted as supporting SU(N), rather than U(N), boundary gauge theory.

Under the short-multiplet assumption, the (2,0) high-harmonic spectrum is ⊕_m[(m,m±2)_S+(nT+1)(m,m)_S]. Low-mode corrections give nT degree-(1,1) primaries and nT+1 diagonal generators at higher degree. For nT=21, their multiparticle Fock construction, supplemented by boundary current modes, matches the symmetric-product K3 chiral-primary spectrum in the large-N comparison.

records.exactAssertion: Right → left, analogy_only: within the sources' reported protected-sector comparisons, the right endpoint's conditional (2,0), nT=21, large-N matching supplements its propagating KK spectrum with boundary current multiplets. The right source explicitly compares this mechanism with the AdS5 U(1) singleton sector, agreeing with the boundary qualification accompanying the left endpoint's protected Δ=k, m²=k(k−4) family. This is a structural analogy between short-multiplet matching and the distinction between bulk and boundary content. It excludes equality of spectra or masses, identification of AdS3 current multiplets as singletons, derivation of the right Fock spectrum from the left scalar family, finite-N completeness, historical dependence on the left paper, and completeness of the non-chiral spectrum.

intersection.statement: The common scope is a comparison strategy: organize supergravity KK states into short multiplets and compare their chiral boundary content. The intersection is methodological, not a shared compactification or spectrum.

Both reported comparisons distinguish propagating bulk content from boundary content. The left discusses an explicit U(1) singleton for a U(N) boundary theory; the right restores two missing chiral-primary generators using boundary current multiplets.

required_assumptions.statement: Read the right endpoint as a reported calculation conditional on its all-KK-states-short ansatz, with nT=21 for the K3 comparison and the stable large-N chiral-primary Fock construction. The analogy does not require treating the shortness ansatz as proven.
Retain the sources' distinction between the AdS5 U(1) singleton and the AdS3 boundary current multiplets, which the right source explicitly says are not singleton representations.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The supplied right-source text explicitly states the shortness assumption, defines the large-N limit, performs the nT=21 comparison, and acknowledges the absence of a rigorous shortness argument. These establish the scope of the reported calculation, not the truth of its ansatz.
The left singleton qualification and the right boundary-current completion are explicit. The right source itself introduces the latter by comparison with the four-dimensional example.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left concerns Type IIB on AdS5×S5 and four-dimensional N=4 SU(N) Yang–Mills with SO(6) R-symmetry. The right concerns six-dimensional (2,0) supergravity on S3×AdS3 and a two-dimensional symmetric-product K3 comparison. No map between their representation towers is supplied.

The left's absent k=1 family member diagnoses the omission of a decoupled U(1) sector from the propagating bulk description. The right's missing degree-(2,0) and degree-(0,2) states are current descendants of the identity. Their boundary roles are analogous, but their representations and physical contents differ.

The left endpoint identifies a protected single-trace family. The right additionally constructs multiparticle chiral primaries. Its discussion explicitly prevents extending chiral-primary agreement to a claim that all states are chiral primaries or their descendants.

endpoints.text: Apply Israel–Lanczos–Sen junction conditions to the shell, expand around extremal tension, and combine the two Friedmann equations to obtain an effective continuity equation.

Shell motion is rewritten as a one-dimensional potential problem with an initial-value constraint. Axial exterior perturbations use Reissner–Nordström master potentials and tortoise coordinates; the interior gravitational potential is l(l+1)/R².

records.exactAssertion: The left method is a methodological analogue of the background radial-motion component of the right method: both use spherical inside/outside junction conditions to constrain one proper-time radius, and the left leading near-extremal Friedmann model with fixed bulk masses can be rewritten in the same auxiliary form ½(radius velocity)²+potential=−½ used on the right. This restricted analogy excludes equality of potential functions, physical parameters, conservation laws across dimensions, stability conclusions, axial perturbation spectra, and any claim that either endpoint uses or supports the other's complete method.

intersection.statement: Both methods apply spherical thin-shell junction conditions to a radius evolving in shell proper time. Their common scope is the background radial constraint, rather than a shared physical spacetime.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the left calculation to its displayed inside/outside branch and the near-extremal, leading-order Friedmann model. Hold k±, σ and the bulk mass parameters m± fixed; retain only the orders used in Eq. (5).

endpoints.text: For the stated generalized assumptions, the authors estimate Γ ≈ Ms³w^(2ν+3)/Mp², where ν = νb+νh and meff² = k²(ν²−4). Requiring decay before BBN or electroweak baryogenesis then bounds effective mass against warp factor; these are conditional phenomenological bounds for other backgrounds.

For finite weighted volume, the higher-eigenvalue bound reduces to mk² < (2816/5)k²m1² whenever m1² > (441/440)𝒦. Thus along a family with m1 → 0 satisfying this inequality, each fixed existing discrete higher KK mass also tends to zero. This requires the curvature/warp scale to tend to zero as well and is consistent with the scale-separated regime motivating the spin-two conjecture.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied source scope, no directed scientific relation is established between these selected results. The left result conditionally bounds the lifetime of a charged form-field scalar through a generalized mixing-induced decay estimate; the right result bounds higher spin-two spectral masses in terms of the first spin-two mass under a curvature/warping threshold. Their shared warped-KK setting supplies no identification of observables or derivation connecting the two results. This verdict excludes any claim about all possible relations between the papers or about a future application to a separately verified common compactification.

endpoints.text: For the specified class of rescalable scalar potentials, the authors conjecture that consistent quantum gravity requires (λ/μ²)^α≳G, with α determined by the interaction potential. Their α=1 kink examples give λ/μ²≳G. Applicability in higher dimensions, including four dimensions, is proposed through dimensional reduction.

At each scalar-field point, the proposed generalization requires at least one particle satisfying Q²≥m²+g^{ij}µ_iµ_j, with µ_i=∂m/∂t^i. Gauge repulsion then compensates gravity and scalar attraction between identical particles. The qualifying particle may change with field position. For N Abelian fields, a minimal spanning set of N qualifying charge vectors is proposed; a general stronger convex-hull analogue is not established.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied source scopes, no directed scientific relation is established between the left scalar-potential conjecture (λ/μ²)^α≳G and the right pointwise charged-particle conjecture Q²≥m²+g^ij∂_i m∂_j m. Their quantities, quantifiers and spectral motivations differ, and no common action or qualifying-state dictionary connects them. This source-scoped no_relation excludes claims of equivalence, implication, specialization, method dependence and tension; it does not prove logical independence in every possible model. The separate scalar-force proposal in the right paper's Section 4 is excluded.

intersection.statement: Both propose quantum-gravity consistency criteria involving scalar fields, gravity and particle spectra. This establishes a shared subject, but no common action, identified state or matched application of the two bounds.

required_assumptions.statement: The left conjecture concerns the specified two-parameter potentials with μ²>0 and the stated rescaling form; λ is normalized so that the dimensionless potential has coefficients of order one.

The left authors assume that loss of the relevant soliton scattering states obstructs a consistent quantum theory. This is a reported conjectural premise, not a demonstrated consequence of the classical solutions.
The proposed higher-dimensional left bound uses the authors' dimensional-reduction consistency argument; it is not a supplied reduction of the right theory.
The established domain of the right force formulation uses massless gauge and scalar mediators and a positive scalar metric. Its massive-mediator extension is expressly inconclusive.

The right nonsupersymmetric proposal assumes a prohibition on the relevant stable bound-state towers and adopts pointwise existence throughout field space. The source does not derive these requirements from black-hole decay alone.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The supplied text and images directly specify the left potential rescaling, parametric inequality and classical evidential scope. Their presence suffices to compare the reported conjecture without accepting its quantum-consistency premise as true.

The supplied right pages explicitly specify the scalar-force sign, mass derivative, existential quantifier and proposed charge-space spanning requirement. These are source statements, not independently validated consistency conditions.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left inequality constrains parameters of a scalar self-potential. The right constrains the gauge charge, mass and scalar couplings of a qualifying particle. No supplied equation identifies these quantities.

The left kink evidence uses two-dimensional dilaton gravity, a scalar potential and a selected C=0 solution branch. The right force proposal uses an Einstein-normalized gauge theory with massless scalar mediators. A common dimensional reduction or frame transformation is not supplied.

The left motivation is preservation of soliton scattering states; the right motivation is exclusion of stable bound-state towers through sufficient gauge repulsion. These are distinct spectral requirements.

The right inequality places attractive scalar exchange alongside gravitational attraction and requires gauge repulsion to compensate both. It does not itself require scalar attraction to exceed gravity, so the selected endpoints do not furnish an apparent sign tension.

endpoints.text: In the EH and DBI examples examined, the authors report WGC-expected monotonic corrections to extremal mass-to-charge ratios for flat, dS and AdS backgrounds. Full nonlinear corrections are milder than four-derivative truncations. These examples provide evidence beyond leading corrections, rather than a general WGC proof.

Imposing nonnegative γ for like charges gives q̂≥q̂0[L_eff²/(L_eff²−2α̃)](M_ext/Q_ext), identified by the authors as the Gauss-Bonnet WGC bound. They report agreement with the charged-AdS limit at α→0 and an increased threshold for positive α in the examined expansions.

records.exactAssertion: Only a qualitative analogy from left to right is established: in their AdS discussions, both endpoints organize corrections using WGC-motivated charge-to-mass criteria. The left reports downward, charge-dependent corrections to extremal black-hole M/Q in EH/DBI; the right reports a positive first-order shift of the minimum probe q/m with the Gauss-Bonnet coupling in its examined d=5 expansion, conditional on nonnegative like-charge anomalous dimensions. Inverting a positive left-hand M/Q makes their verbal charge-to-mass directions comparable, but the charged objects, varied parameters and theories differ. This assertion excludes equality, implication, a shared controlled solution regime, all-coupling monotonicity, and transfer of the left's milder-than-truncation result to the right.
