limitations: This is a comparison of source-reported statements plus elementary conditional algebra. No numerical extremality calculation, orbit calculation or full-paper derivation was reproduced.

The nonlinear-versus-four-derivative ordering is explicitly supported in the supplied flat EH/DBI and dS EH passages. It is not transferred to the Gauss-Bonnet probe threshold or independently certified throughout AdS parameter space.

A stronger quantitative identification would require the left paper's charge-normalization definitions and model details, and the right paper's Section 2.1 Gauss-Bonnet action, solution and parameter definitions. Such an identification is expressly excluded.

Independent validation would additionally require the left paper's actual AdS Figures 17-18 and numerical Appendix A, and the right paper's orbit expansion and hierarchy around equations (2.15)-(2.19). Those are not needed to establish the restricted comparison of reported trends.

The right paper's comparisons with other self-repulsive-particle calculations do not identify those calculations with the assigned left endpoint. Its reported series mismatches are therefore not evidence of tension between these two nodes; see d20efa048aac1f977349:p0009s002 and d20efa048aac1f977349:p0016s002, also checked in image:6.
Earlier reviewer assertions and node review labels were not used as mathematical certification.

endpoints.text: Reorganize the corrected radial potential around its two physical horizons. Retain their singular terms and a constant to obtain a confluent-Heun approximation; keeping numerical horizon roots improves that approximation, while expanding the roots permits analytic first-order EFT frequencies.

Flux backtracking identifies asymptotic moduli trajectories and potential steepness. The asymptotic radial wave equation defines an effective transverse dimension and phase-space factor. Formal sphere reduction is used to identify generalized Freund–Rubin potentials.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied passages, no directed scientific relation is established between the left two-horizon confluent-Heun approximation and the right asymptotic-trajectory/steepness, effective-dimension and formal sphere-reduction method. The documented inputs, approximation operations and outputs differ; sharing a radial scalar-wave problem supplies no specific method transfer. This is a packet-local no_relation verdict. It excludes claims of universal mathematical inequivalence, impossibility of a limiting correspondence, or a general relation between QNM poles and absorption amplitudes.

intersection.statement: Both treatments simplify radial scalar-wave propagation in a limiting regime. This common subject does not establish a shared background, parameter family, approximation procedure or observable.

required_assumptions.statement: Interpret the left method within its stated small-coupling, nearly extremal EFT regime. Its additional expansion of horizon positions requires the smallness condition in Eq. (4.9) and excludes M=Q.

Interpret the right absorption calculation within its one-modulus scalar-probe setup and low-frequency matching regime. The quoted exponential-regime formulas require d>2 and 2/sqrt(d−2)<λ<2sqrt((d−1)/(d−2)).

Treat the right sphere reduction as the specified gravity-plus-n-form model with an internal breathing mode in lower-dimensional Einstein frame; it is not automatically a reduction of the left Einstein–Maxwell EFT.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left regime restrictions are explicit in the supplied source and are retained in this comparison. This records the authors' domain, rather than independently proving approximation accuracy.
The right matching and steepness conditions are supplied. Its DGKT example has d=4 and λ²=54/13, which lies between the squared exponential-regime bounds 2 and 6.
Appendix A supplies the sphere ansatz, flux convention, volume kinetic term and breathing-mode potential needed to identify the right reduction operation.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left selects poles at two nearly coincident horizons and a constant to obtain a confluent-Heun approximation. The right extracts an effective dimension from a far-region Bessel equation. These are different specified operations.

The left output is a slowly damped QNM frequency obtained through a quantization condition. The right output is a ratio of absorbing throat flux to incident asymptotic flux. The supplied passages establish no conversion between these observables.

The right flux/curvature breathing-mode reduction has no demonstrated counterpart in the left horizon-pole construction. The supplied left action and method do not identify their Wilson coefficients with the right flux, volume or sphere dimension.

conventionDictionary.conversion: d_R=4 in DGKT matches the left spacetime dimension numerically, but does not identify the backgrounds or actions. No cross-theory frame transformation is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Four-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell theory with four-derivative operators; the source uses Planck units with κ=2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: d denotes the AdS spacetime dimension; DGKT has d=4. Appendix A reduces a (d+n)-dimensional gravity-plus-n-form theory to d-dimensional Einstein frame.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Do not identify Q_W with the moduli potential V. Internally to the right DGKT equation, writing ψ''+Q_Rψ=0 gives Q_R=−V_DGKT. This sign rewrite does not supply a cross-paper operator map.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Q_W^Heun is the radial wave-potential approximation A/(r−R_+)²+B/(r−R_+)+C/(r−R_−)²+D/(r−R_−)+E; image:2 confirms the pole orders.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: V(s,u) is a moduli scalar potential. V_DGKT is instead a radial wave potential defined by [−d²/dr²+V_DGKT]ψ=0.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No identification of left R_± or r_± with right r, ρ or R is established. Right u in the DGKT moduli trajectory is also distinct by context from the common radial coordinate u introduced for matching in Eq. (3.13).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: R_± are corrected horizon roots obtained numerically from the truncated background; r_±=M±sqrt(M²−Q²) are uncorrected RN horizons. Numerical root exactness is relative to that truncated background.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: r and ρ are radial coordinates in the respective examples; R is a constant in the DGKT harmonic function. The moduli s,u obey the adopted asymptotic trajectory s=u³.

conventionDictionary.conversion: There is no supplied conversion from the horizon separation or Wilson coefficients to the asymptotic steepness λ or flux N.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: g4 multiplies (F_μνF^μν)² and h4 multiplies R^μνρσF_μνF_ρσ. Horizon separation controls the reported pole-coefficient scaling; Eq. (4.9) restricts the expanded-root branch.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: λ is the slope in V_asym∼−V0 exp(−λΦ), using the source's canonically normalized modulus. In the exponential regime q=4/[(d−2)λ²]. N labels internal n-form flux.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Shared notation ω supplies no numerical or analytic-continuation dictionary. Frequencies refer to their respective time coordinates; the right normalization factor must not be silently dropped.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: ω is a complex QNM frequency; the source expresses its damping rate as −Im ω.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: P_abs=F_near/F_far^in is a dimensionless flux ratio. The source defines c_∞=t/t_∞ and ω_∞=c_∞ω. The specific Appendix B.3 scalar ansatz is exp(+iωt), confirmed in image:6.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The right definition can be reconstructed from the coefficient of ϕ'/ξ in Eq. (3.10). It is not an identification of the left spacetime dimension or horizon sphere.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The RN background has four spacetime dimensions; the selected method organizes its two horizon singularities.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: d_eff is a wave-equation-defined effective transverse dimension, without the literal geometric interpretation of an ordinary transverse space in these non-flat asymptotics. In the exponential regime d_eff=1+4(d−2)/[(d−2)λ²−4], confirmed in image:4.

conventionDictionary.concept: Overloaded n, scalar fields and Δ
conventionDictionary.conversion: Use n_QNM and n_sphere as distinct labels, and distinguish Δ_abs from Δ_CFT. The right breathing mode and scalar wave probe are different fields; neither is identified with the left probe.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: n labels the QNM family alongside angular index ℓ.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Appendix A uses n for sphere dimension and a breathing mode varphi=sqrt[(d+n−2)/(n(d−2))] ln(volume), as confirmed in image:5. Δ in the absorption section is a frequency exponent, whereas Appendix A's Δ=2(d−1) is a conformal dimension.

limitations: This is a comparison of supplied source passages, not an exhaustive search of either paper or a proof that no broader relation exists. Upstream node labels and review summaries were not treated as scientific authority.

The reported accuracy of the left potential approximation and the physical validity of the right one-modulus truncations were not independently certified. Keeping numerical roots of an EFT-truncated background does not establish an all-orders EFT solution.

The complete flux-backtracking construction is not reproduced here. Questions about global operator equivalence or QNM/scattering continuation are explicitly excluded; they would require, among other material, left Section 2.3 and Sections 3.2–3.4, and right Section 2 and Sections 3.1–3.2.2. Those stronger questions are not necessary premises of the packet-local verdict.

endpoints.text: The authors find large-k bubble approximations and numerical smeared bounces supporting a nonperturbative instability for the physical odd k>3 family, despite the absence of large-coupling tachyons. Their numerical continuation supports solutions for real k>3 and becomes singular as k approaches 3; this is numerical evidence rather than a general existence theorem.

Deformation-dependent KK spectra establish broad regions of nonsupersymmetric perturbative stability in the analyzed (ω,χ1,β1) family. For the Wilson-loop families, the authors find spectra bounded below by those of the round backgrounds and assert perturbative stability throughout the family.

records.exactAssertion: The left endpoint supplies only an illustrative analogy for interpreting the right endpoint: its reported nonperturbative decay despite a positive tree-level twisted-string mass demonstrates the distinction between passing a perturbative test and excluding tunnelling. The right endpoint's reported KK perturbative stability consequently does not determine its nonperturbative fate on the supplied evidence. This comparison excludes any prediction of a right-hand bubble, any proof of right-hand nonperturbative stability, any transfer of the left saddle or its flux/spin conditions, and any equivalence, specialization or contradiction between the two results.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints concern compact AdS backgrounds with nonsupersymmetric regimes in which the sources report absence of the perturbative instability being tested. This is a comparison of stability diagnostics, without an identification of backgrounds or spectra.

required_assumptions.statement: For the left endpoint, restrict physical backgrounds to odd integer k>3 and sufficiently large λ. Treat continuation to real k>3 as a numerical construction, not an additional physical orbifold family or an existence theorem.

For the right endpoint, retain the supergravity approximation and the stated perturbative scope: the sufficient stability regions of the (ω,χ1,β1) family and the reported Wilson-loop spectral bounds. Use nonsupersymmetric points when making the analogy.
Compare the sources' reported tests and conclusions; do not interpret a perturbative spectral bound as a calculation of tunnelling or transfer a bounce between the backgrounds.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The supplied left pages explicitly separate positive tree-level twisted-string mass at sufficiently large λ from the reported nonperturbative bounce instability.
The right stability passages explicitly call their conclusions perturbative and derive them from deformation-dependent KK spectra.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left geometry is AdS5×S5/Zk; the right geometries are deformations of AdS3×S3×T4 or AdS3×S3×S3×S1. Their AdS dimensions and internal spaces differ.

The left smeared cap requires D3-brane sources for its RR five-form flux. The right deformations are described as purely NSNS. The left flux/source construction is therefore not an established construction for the right backgrounds.

The left endpoint combines a twisted-string mass test with a topology-changing Euclidean saddle. The right endpoint reports KK fluctuation stability. These are different diagnostics and do not constitute contradictory answers to one shared stability problem.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Preserve the distinction between perturbative fluctuations and semiclassical tunnelling. No equality of mass thresholds or decay criteria is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (2.5) tests a twisted-string ground-state mass; the bounce tests a separate nonperturbative decay channel.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The endpoint tests perturbative stability through KK spectra. The supplied discussion of another deformation family identifies instability boundaries with BF-bound saturation.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Rename these k_orb and k_WZW when comparing papers. Their integer character supplies no physical identification.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: k is the orbifold order. The intended type-IIB construction requires odd integer k; numerical differential equations are also continued to real k.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: In equations (6.2)–(6.4), k and k̃ are sphere WZW levels, while k0 is the SL(2,R) level; 1/k0=1/k+1/k̃.

conventionDictionary.concept: Radii, α′, α, units and frames
conventionDictionary.conversion: Keep the source normalizations separate. No cross-paper radius, string-unit or metric-frame conversion is needed for this qualitative relation.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: R=λ^(1/4)√α′, hence R²/α′=√λ and α′M² is dimensionless.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (6.4) uses k0=4π²ℓAdS², k=4π²ℓS3² and k̃=4π²α^(-2)ℓS3², with the stated supergravity normalization ℓS3=1. Here α is a radius-ratio parameter, not α′. The worldsheet E tensor is expressed using the string-frame metric and B field.

conventionDictionary.concept: Circle coordinate versus deformation parameters χ
conventionDictionary.conversion: Do not identify χ on the left with χi on the right, or infer that the right circle admits the left cap and spin structure.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: χ is the Hopf-fibre coordinate, with period 2π/k and asymptotic circle radius R/k.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: y7 is the circle coordinate; χi and χ̃i are Wilson-loop deformation parameters entering the shifts (5.32)–(5.33). Their identifications are given in (5.34), including χi→χi+4πqi.

conventionDictionary.conversion: These β parameters have different definitions and are not mapped.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: βk is a numerical shooting correction in bk=√k/2+βk.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: β1 is a deformation modulus participating in TsT transformations; it is not a shooting correction.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use the right paper's momentum shifts exactly; no conversion to the left twisted-string mass is established. Image:5 resolves the last term of (5.33) as −2πp6χ̃2 outside the half-weighted charge bracket.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: qL and qR are integer-normalized Cartan charges; p7 labels the circle tower. Wilson-loop deformations replace 2πp7 by the charge-dependent expressions (5.32)–(5.33).

limitations: This is a source-scoped analogy, not independent certification of either endpoint. Node descriptions, nominations and earlier review metadata were not used as scientific premises.

The left numerical integration, complete boundary-value analysis and fluctuation analysis around the bounce were not reproduced. The supplied numerical conclusion is retained as a reported result, not a general existence theorem (2ede9f6b7dfe0ccfe530:p0015s001; 2ede9f6b7dfe0ccfe530:p0015s002).

The right full round-background spectra referenced as (4.32)–(4.41) are not supplied here. Consequently the Wilson-loop lower-bound conclusion is reported, not independently derived; this does not prevent comparing its explicitly perturbative scope (b3fa3069164d7a8be745:p0037s001).

A stronger claim transferring the left decay to the right would require a right-background cap construction, compatible global fermion conditions, flux/source constraints and a valid tunnelling saddle. No such transfer is asserted; the supplied backgrounds already differ in their RR versus NSNS content (2ede9f6b7dfe0ccfe530:p0004s001; 2ede9f6b7dfe0ccfe530:p0007s001; b3fa3069164d7a8be745:p0041s002).

Image:6 discusses BF saturation for the separate Ξ deformation family. It is used to check terminology and radius/level conventions, not to extend the assigned right endpoint's stability region (b3fa3069164d7a8be745:p0042s001).

endpoints.text: The proposed stretched N-flation model admits parametric enhancement while controlling both continuum and smallest-charge contributions. Suppressing its n=N harmonic requires β≳N^−1/2, leading to the stated field-range ceiling |ē|≲√N Mpl. Thus the LWGC alone does not exclude every non-monodromic large-field effective theory.

The five-dimensional scalar model generates mixing between its gauge photon and graviphoton when a Wilson line splits opposite-charge KK masses. Increasing the compactification radius can suppress mixing by lowering the KK coupling until the species cutoff excludes bi-charged towers.

records.exactAssertion: Within the supplied passages, no directed relation is established between the stretched-N-flation harmonic/field-range result and the 5D Wilson-line kinetic-mixing result. Their shared LWGC framework supplies no derivation, specialization or demonstrated method dependency between these particular claims. This source-scoped verdict excludes a universal claim of physical independence, any compactification or duality equivalence, and any conversion of |ē| ≲ √N Mpl into a constraint on χ.

intersection.statement: Both models assume gravity-coupled effective theories with LWGC-organized charge lattices. The supplied passages establish this common framework, without identifying their spectra, parameters or observables.

required_assumptions.statement: The local left-hand checks use the source's preserved axion identifications, flat kinetic metric and stated harmonic estimates. The large-N continuum approximation is restricted to its displayed condition; the smallest-charge estimate is checked separately.

The local right-hand checks use complex scalars saturating the displayed zero-dilaton mass bound, circle compactification, and the stated charge basis. Radius dependence is interpreted at fixed gravitational units and fixed e4D; the species-cutoff explanation is retained as a reported result.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly adopts the field identifications and flat metric, states the continuum validity condition, and supplements that calculation with the smallest-charge contribution.
The right source specifies the scalar spectrum and compactification, fixes e4D = 10^−3 for Figure 5, explains its gauge-basis convention, and reports the species-cutoff suppression.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left calculation concerns instanton/topological-sector contributions to a scalar potential. The right calculation concerns particle-loop contributions to a gauge kinetic operator. Their exponential action weights and signed charge-weighted logarithms are different quantities.

The left enhancement varies an N-axion lattice shape and compares harmonic orders. The right example has two U(1) factors after 5D-to-4D compactification and varies a circle radius and Wilson line. No shared parameter family is supplied.

The left field-range ceiling follows from comparing harmonic estimates. The right suppression is attributed to a species cutoff excluding bi-charged states. The supplied left derivation does not identify that cutoff as its bound's mechanism.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No identification of the left axions or instantons with the right complex scalars or KK particles is established.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: φ denotes canonically normalized axions; θ_L denotes their dimensionless lattice coordinates. Q = f^−1ℓ labels instanton/topological sectors in the lattice dual to the period lattice.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: φ_i denotes charged complex matter scalars in 5D. After circle reduction, their particle states carry integer charges (q,n) under U(1)F × U(1)KK. θ_R denotes the Wilson line.

conventionDictionary.conversion: A common 2π angular identification does not determine a canonical-field or decay-constant map. Gauge-basis changes in the right example are kept distinct from scalar-coordinate changes on the left.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The canonical scalar kinetic term has coefficient −1/2; φ = fθ_L and φ is identified modulo 2πΓ*. Image image:3 confirms the single-field normalization and period.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The 5D gauge normalization is −F²/(4e5D²). The displayed canonical 4D convention is −F_a²/4 − F_b²/4 + χF_aF_b/2. θ_R has 2π periodicity; the authors change gauge basis when comparing certain Wilson-line values.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Neither α_L = α_R nor β = eKK/e4D is established. The source-defined diagonal scale |ē| is used exactly with its displayed normalization, without inserting an additional 2π.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: α_L = μ_L/f2 ≃ Mpl/f2, β = f2/f1 and α̂ = α_L/√N. The source gives |ē| ≃ Mpl/(α̂β). Images image:1 and image:2 resolve these ratios and square roots.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The dilaton coupling called α in Eq. (2.1) is set to zero in §4.1. Radius dependence instead enters through eKK²R² = 16πG and the KK mass term.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Rename the indices n_harmonic and n_KK before comparison; no equality between them, or between N and a species count, is used.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: N is the number of axions, hence the field-space lattice rank; n labels the harmonics being compared, including n = 1 and n = N.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: n ∈ Z is KK momentum and the U(1)KK charge. The spacetime reduction is 5D to 4D, with a rank-two charge lattice.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No conversion between σ_n², |ē| and χ is supplied. A harmonic variance cannot be equated to a signed kinetic-mixing coefficient.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: V = Σ_Q Z_Q exp(iQ·φ), with Z_−Q = Z_Q*. The displayed harmonic variances contain exponentially action-weighted lattice contributions.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: A scalar contributes χ/(g_ag_b) = −Q_aQ_b ln(m²/μ_ren²)/(48π²), in the displayed kinetic-term convention. Opposite charge products can cancel for equal masses.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Dimensional bookkeeping uses natural units. No exact conversion of Mpl to M4D, or identification of μ_L with μ_ren, is needed or asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The displayed equations give f1, f2, μ_L, Mpl and |ē| mass units; Q has inverse-field units, while α_L, β and instanton actions are dimensionless.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: R has inverse-mass units; m5D, m4D, M4D and μ_ren are mass scales. The 4D couplings, integer charges, θ_R and χ are dimensionless. Image image:4 resolves m4D² = m5D² + R^−2(n − qθ_R/(2π))².

limitations: The verdict concerns the two assigned claims and supplied passages; it does not establish that no larger theory could realize both effects.

The statistical definition and full resummation underlying the left harmonic variances were not independently reconstructed. The local checks below do not certify suppression of every contribution to every harmonic; the source itself distinguishes continuum and smallest-charge estimates (07c23f2e3433c03c5e9e:p0029s001, 07c23f2e3433c03c5e9e:p0029s002).

The right species-counting prescription and numerical cutoff thresholds were not reproduced. Its radius-dependent exclusion mechanism is reported by the source and Figure 5, rather than independently verified here (e34a763882d4a6ea6c41:p0011s001, e34a763882d4a6ea6c41:p0012s001).
UV completion of the left model is explicitly left open by its source (07c23f2e3433c03c5e9e:p0030s002). No UV realization or universal kinetic-mixing bound is inferred.

Image image:6 concerns the separate Type IIB/CY example in §4.3. Its symplectic-frame discussion does not establish a bridge involving the assigned §4.1 scalar/KK calculation (e34a763882d4a6ea6c41:p0015s001, e34a763882d4a6ea6c41:p0015s002).
No decisive omitted premise is needed for this restricted source-comparison verdict. A stronger physical relation would require additional evidence and is excluded from the assertion.

endpoints.text: Uses discrete projections, BPS charge vectors and chiral-ring information to compute protected-sector indices. Tests a possible obstruction to convexity by seeking non-BPS small-charge operators collinear with higher-charge BPS operators.

Uses the imported Shapere–Tachikawa central-charge sum rule relating 2a−c to S(r)=Σ_i Δ_i and rank, together with the Hofman–Maldacena bound 1/2≤a/c≤5/4. The unspecified additional Coulomb-branch data in the separate central-charge formulae are unnecessary for the argument.

records.exactAssertion: The left method provides only a methodological analogy to the right: both extract constraints from protected charged-operator data. The left constructs BPS charge sublattices and tests a conditional obstruction involving non-BPS charge-sector minima; the right converts a sum of protected Coulomb-branch generator dimensions into a central-charge combination and combines it with the Hofman-Maldacena bound. The left_to_right direction presents this analogy and carries no implication. Equivalence, specialization, method reuse, a numerical relation between the invariants, transfer through discrete gauging, complete-spectrum convexity, and a derived scale-separation result are explicitly excluded.

intersection.statement: Both methods extract constraints from protected charged operators in supersymmetric CFTs. This is an intersection of ingredients; the supplied examples do not establish a common theory on which both constructions operate.

required_assumptions.statement: Retain the left method's distinction between lowest dimensions at specified full charge vectors and dimensions inferred from BPS saturation. Its obstruction test is conditional on strict nonsaturation at smaller collinear charges and saturation at their sum.

Retain the right method's stated setting: unitary, local, interacting four-dimensional N=2 SCFTs, with scalar Coulomb-branch generators and the assumed freely generated Coulomb branch. Use the imported central-charge formulae within that stated scope.
The comparison concerns the use of protected data, without identifying the left charge sublattice with the right collection of Coulomb-branch generators.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly describes the protected-sector calculation and states the obstruction test conditionally. It reports that its examples do not realize the proposed obstruction; the comparison does not assume otherwise.

The right source explicitly stipulates its theory class and free-generation assumption. These are satisfied as restrictions on the reported method, not independently verified properties of every N=2 SCFT.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left examples are the three-dimensional N=2 XYZ model and four-dimensional N=1 SQCD. The right method requires four-dimensional N=2 supersymmetry. The left examples therefore cannot directly instantiate the right argument.

The left method concerns a charge lattice and lowest dimensions along charge rays. The right sum is over selected Coulomb-branch chiral-ring generators, not all charged operators or charge-sector minima.

Discrete gauging is part of the left construction. The right source specifically warns that discrete gaugings can violate free generation. It does not establish applicability of its sum-rule argument after the left projections.

conventionDictionary.concept: Conformal dimensions and the selected operators
conventionDictionary.conversion: The symbol denotes the same type of CFT quantity, but there is no identification of spectra or equality between these dimensions.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Delta(q) is the lowest conformal dimension at full charge vector q.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Delta_i is the conformal dimension of the i-th Coulomb-branch generator O_i.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No numerical conversion between the left U(1)_R conventions and the right U(1)_r convention is asserted. Shared proportionality of protected dimension and charge does not supply such a conversion.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The method uses full Abelian charge vectors. XYZ R-charges are rescaled to integers; the SQCD discussion notes that multiplying charges by N_f makes them integral without changing the index.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Coulomb-branch generators have vanishing SU(2)_R charge and U(1)_r charge r_i=Delta_i.

conventionDictionary.concept: Convexity sign and the conditional obstruction
conventionDictionary.conversion: On a common ray, write b(nq) for the linear BPS saturation value, without asserting existence of a BPS operator at every smaller charge. If both smaller minima exceed b and the summed-charge minimum saturates b, their dimension sum exceeds Delta((n_1+n_2)q), violating the left inequality. The strict greater-than sign is checked in image:1, physical page 18.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: A convex vector obeys Delta((n_1+n_2)q) >= Delta(n_1q)+Delta(n_2q) for positive integers n_1,n_2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The selected right method provides a sum rule for generator dimensions and an anomaly ratio bound; neither is a charge-ray convexity definition.

conventionDictionary.conversion: There is no conversion between a lattice index and a sum of generator dimensions. In particular, the left matrix S in Eq. (4.6) is unrelated to the right scalar function S(r).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The BPS index measures the sublattice generated by BPS charge directions relative to the full operator charge lattice. It is not a supersymmetric graded-trace index.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: S(r)=sum_{i=1}^r Delta_i is a dimension sum over Coulomb-branch generators.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Do not identify Coulomb-branch rank r with charge-space dimension, gauge-group parameter N_c, projection order, or an individual charge r_i.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: M counts Abelian symmetries; N controls a discrete projection in XYZ; N_c is the SQCD color parameter.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: r counts Coulomb-branch generators, whereas r_i denotes a U(1)_r charge.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use exactly the right source's normalization: 2a-c=S(r)/2-r/4 and 1/2<=a/c<=5/4. Image:4, physical page 4, resolves the scrambled extraction: the interacting-theory consequence is 2a-c>r/4, not 2a-c>4r. No central-charge or bulk-frame conversion is needed for the analogy.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The selected left construction has no corresponding anomaly-central-charge input.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: a and c are the central charges appearing in Eqs. (2.1)-(2.4), with a common unspecified function f in the separate formulae for 2a and c.

conventionDictionary.conversion: These are different rings and different uses of ring data. The left BPS classification supplies charge directions; the right generator list supplies the terms of S(r). Free generation is not inferred from the left classification.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The SQCD discussion uses moduli-space expectation values to identify BPS combinations, reporting M^n as BPS and det M as non-BPS; checked in image:2, physical page 22.

limitations: This is a comparison of the supplied source passages and the three listed checked images, not a certification of either complete paper or of the externally imported sum rule.

endpoints.text: The proposed WGCHull framework combines explicit convex-hull construction with a containment test and returns the hull, its contributing vertices and a Yes/No verdict for the supplied extremality sphere and particle set.

Conditional on requiring extremal black holes of every charge direction to decay, the authors derive the generalized condition that conv{±z_i} contain the unit ball. One superextremal state for each Abelian factor is insufficient. For N orthogonal equal-magnitude vectors, one state per factor, they obtain z>√N at fixed physical mPl.

records.exactAssertion: At the level of its advertised geometric task, the left WGCHull framework uses the convex-hull containment criterion formulated at the right endpoint: construct the hull of supplied charge-to-mass vectors and test whether it encloses the extremality ball. This structural method-use relation is restricted to finite, explicitly sign-complete, full-dimensional superextremal inputs, an exact known spherical extremality region, the input prescription S_L=alpha S_R, and cases away from tangency. It includes the right endpoint's orthogonal equal-magnitude example. It excludes historical attribution, identification of the papers' underlying physical charge conventions, equality-case equivalence, solver correctness or runtime certification, spectrum completeness, and any proof of physical decay or ultraviolet consistency.

intersection.statement: The comparison concerns a finite collection of charge-to-mass vectors in an N-dimensional Euclidean charge space, with an exactly supplied spherical extremality region. It invokes the convex-hull WGC as a conditional criterion.

The restricted inputs explicitly include both signs, span the charge space, and have every supplied vector strictly outside the extremality sphere. The right endpoint's orthogonal equal-magnitude family supplies a concrete example satisfying these input requirements when z>1.

required_assumptions.statement: Use an exact, origin-centered extremality ball B_alpha with alpha>0; identify normalized geometric inputs by the explicit prescription S_L=alpha S_R. This prescription defines the comparison and does not identify the papers' physical charge or Planck-mass conventions.

Choose a finite set S_R={plus or minus z_i}, with norms greater than one and linear span R^N. Both signs must be supplied explicitly; the displayed WGCHull setup does not establish automatic antiparticle completion. Sign symmetry and spanning ensure that the hull is full-dimensional and contains the origin in its interior.

Exclude tangency: the normalized hull's minimum facet distance from the origin must differ from one. This avoids identifying the left paper's non-strict acceptance rule with the right paper's strict decay inequalities.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Within the constructed comparison, S_R={plus or minus z e_a : a=1,...,N}, N>=2, z>1, and S_L=alpha S_R satisfy finiteness, sign completeness, spanning, superextremality, and the necessary point-count requirement. These are established for the specified input family, not for an unspecified physical spectrum.
The concrete checks N=2 with z=5/4 and z=2 lie strictly on opposite sides of the containment threshold, so neither check relies on the excluded equality case.

scope_mismatches.statement: At contact, the prescriptions differ: image:2 confirms WGCHull's Yes branch is d_H>=alpha. Images image:4 and image:5 confirm the right paper's strict energy inequality and z>sqrt(N) example. Equality is therefore excluded from the asserted alignment.

WGCHull accepts a supplied set; the right paper formulates its physical condition using the particle spectrum and antiparticles. The chosen relation identifies a geometric decision target and does not turn failure of an incomplete supplied set into failure of the full theory.

An estimated sphere or a hull of isolated black-hole solutions is outside the comparison. Image:3 explicitly describes such approximations as informative preliminary checks; the right endpoint's all-directions criterion requires the actual extremality region.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match only the charge-space dimension N and use a common Euclidean basis. No identification of spacetime dimension or gravitational frame is required for this geometric comparison.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: N counts U(1) factors; charge vectors transform under rotations of the photon basis, after removal of kinetic mixing.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: z_i=q_i m_Pl/m_i is dimensionless. Image:6 resolves the footnote defining m_Pl so that q=m/m_Pl is saturated for an extremal black hole.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The right paper explicitly qualifies its growing bound by fixed physical m_Pl and separately discusses species corrections.

limitations: This is a comparison of source prescriptions with a conditional geometric reconstruction. Node labels, the nomination, and earlier review metadata are not independent verification.

A physical dictionary between the two actions would require the left paper's Section 2.1, especially Eqs. (2.4)-(2.7). Those definitions are not supplied. This is needed only for the explicitly excluded identification of physical conventions, not for the input-defined geometric relation (39acf397002c0348d5a7:p0011s002; d3ba6459ff2ca7a247e8:p0001s002).

No correctness or complexity certification of WGCHull II follows from identifying its target. Image:2 explicitly displays maximization with positive-definite P and a reported polynomial-time claim; those optimization and runtime assertions have not been reproduced (39acf397002c0348d5a7:p0016s001; 39acf397002c0348d5a7:p0016s002).

The right paper's continuous convex-hull argument is reported as its conditional decay criterion. No additional claim is made about exact integer particle multiplicities at finite black-hole charge, decay rates, or dynamical sufficiency (d3ba6459ff2ca7a247e8:p0003s003).
Retaining hull vertices identifies contributors to that hull; it does not by itself establish a smallest particle subset satisfying the WGC (39acf397002c0348d5a7:p0014s001).
Only the supplied spans and six attached page images were checked. No full-paper mathematical coverage is claimed.

endpoints.text: For Δμ_ext<0, the authors find positive entropy corrections at fixed M=Q. For p≥1 the Einstein entropy there vanishes and the leading correction depends on (-Δμ_ext)^(p/(p+1)); for p=0 the baseline entropy is nonzero and the leading correction depends on √(-Δμ_ext).

The paper reproduces the leading fixed-(Q,φ∞) relation δM|_S=−T_BH δS|_M. A nonzero extremal mass shift generally produces a divergent fixed-mass entropy shift near zero temperature, with opposite sign. This does not constrain the finite entropy shift at fixed zero temperature, which is the extremal entropy correction studied here.

records.exactAssertion: Restricted to the shared p=0 electric Einstein–Maxwell sector with q=d−2≥2, controlled leading corrections and positive charge, the right's fixed-(M,Q) entropy–mass identity supports the sign and ensemble interpretation of the left result: a negative extremal mass shift accompanies a positive fixed-mass entropy response. The left's finite square-root endpoint formulas satisfy the corresponding leading differential relation, but their finite entropy difference is not the right's divergent first-order correction. This assertion excludes p≥1 branes, equality of the finite corrections, a numerical cross-paper normalization or Wilson-coefficient match, and any sign constraint on entropy at fixed corrected T=0.

intersection.statement: The comparison is restricted to the common electrically charged Einstein–Maxwell black-hole sector: left p=0 and q=d−2≥2; right one gauge field and no moduli.

Both discuss leading higher-derivative mass shifts and fixed-charge, fixed-mass entropy changes near extremality. The shared comparison concerns the sign and thermodynamic ensemble, with the distinct limiting procedures retained.

required_assumptions.statement: Retain leading derivative corrections in a controlled black-hole background with nonzero uncorrected extremal horizon area.
Use fixed positive rescaled charge and a small, nonzero negative extremal ratio shift. The left endpoint holds the mass at its uncorrected extremal value, Mcal=Qcal.

Interpret the right δ quantities as leading perturbative corrections about a positive-temperature reference before taking its near-extremal limit. Its fixed-mass correction is distinct from its fixed-zero-temperature entropy correction.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The supplied p=0 entropy baseline is nonzero, and the right explicitly includes electric Reissner–Nordström black holes. Selecting this sector satisfies the horizon-area restriction.
The left explicitly selects the real positive-temperature branch when Δμ_ext<0 and reports a positive leading fixed-Mcal=Qcal entropy change.
The right supplies the required fixed-entropy mass correction, its extremal limit, and the fixed-mass entropy identity, including the ensemble distinction.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left also treats p≥1 branes whose uncorrected extremal entropy vanishes. The right's stated nonzero-area black-hole scope does not establish a relation to that branch.

The left gives a finite entropy difference at the uncorrected extremal mass, with a shifted positive temperature. The right's divergent quantity is a first-order fixed-mass correction as the reference temperature approaches zero.
The right's finite entropy correction at fixed T_BH=0 is a separate observable. Its reported independent sign is not constrained by the relation proposed here.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Restrict to p=0, q=d−2≥2 and the electric Einstein–Maxwell sector without moduli. No dimensional reduction or conformal-frame transformation is used.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: p labels the brane case; p=0 is the black-hole case, with q=d−2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Static, spherically symmetric black holes in d dimensions; the supplied electric Reissner–Nordström example provides the selected sector.

conventionDictionary.conversion: At fixed Qcal>0, ΔMcal_ext=Qcal Δμ_ext. Compare its sign with the right δM_ext using positive mass units; do not identify the two papers' raw charge or mass numbers.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: μ=Mcal/Qcal; ΔMcal(Tcal,Qcal) tends to Qcal Δμ_ext near zero temperature.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: δM_ext is the fixed-charge correction to the physical extremal mass. In the electric example M0=e_d|Q|/sqrt(k_N), so physical M=Q is not its general normalization.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use each source's native thermodynamic variables. Positive rescalings preserve the sign comparison; the differential algebra below is performed entirely in left units. Image:4 confirms the right factor g_h/(2π).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Tcal and Scal are rescaled thermodynamic variables; Gibbs derivatives define their conjugacy.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: T_BH=g_h/(2π), with g_h the surface gravity.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: δS|M,Q,φ∞ is the leading entropy correction at fixed physical mass, charge and asymptotic moduli.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: α′ is a formal derivative-expansion parameter; the displayed δ quantities are leading corrections.

endpoints.text: Use the N=1 F-term scalar potential constructed from K and W, solve DIW=0 for supersymmetric minima, and diagonalize the canonically normalized scalar Hessian to obtain moduli masses. Compare their scales with the vacuum potential and KK estimates.

Special geometry, symplectic periods, and the GVW superpotential are used to express the scalar potential and isolate its tadpole-dependent term. SUSY conditions simplify canonically normalized moduli mass matrices, with explicit analytic treatment concentrated on the isotropic background.

records.exactAssertion: Within the displayed isotropic, retained-field SUSY AdS calculations, the right endpoint uses the generic computational core described by the left endpoint: construct the N=1 F-term potential from K,W, impose D_IW=0, and obtain scalar masses from its Hessian with Kähler-metric canonical normalization. This is restricted procedural containment, reconstructed from the two sources; it asserts neither historical borrowing nor use of the left endpoint's additional KK correction. It excludes equivalence of compactifications, a field/flux duality dictionary, equality of spectra, universal mass/AdS ratios, and transfer of either tadpole constraints or ten-dimensional KK conclusions.

intersection.statement: Both calculations use a four-dimensional N=1 F-term potential and impose supersymmetry on all retained chiral fields for the SUSY mass calculation. The intersection is a computational framework, without an identified common compactification.

The comparison concerns the displayed isotropic sectors: three complex fields S,T,U on the left and two complex fields S,τ in the right's explicit isotropic mass matrix. It concerns masses of retained fluctuations only.

required_assumptions.statement: Interpret method use as implementation of the common F-term/SUSY/canonical-Hessian procedure within the displayed effective actions, without asserting historical borrowing or equivalence of the compactifications.
For the restricted AdS comparison, impose D_I W=0 for every retained field and W≠0.
Work on nonsingular positive-metric domains of the displayed Kähler potentials. Canonical normalization must use each theory's own metric and retained field content.
Differentiate with flux parameters fixed. In particular, C_L is constant under moduli differentiation, although it depends on geometric fluxes across different left-hand backgrounds.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The displayed potentials, supersymmetric Hessian construction, and canonical mass calculations establish the required procedural overlap directly.
The left explicitly solves D_I W=0 and reports negative V_0; the right evaluates its SUSY Hessian at D_I W=0 and defines Λ_AdS=−3e^K|W|². Nonzero W follows within the selected AdS sector.

Differentiating the supplied Kähler potentials gives positive metrics for positive left saxions and positive right imaginary parts. The right's resulting metric agrees with its explicitly reported canonical fluctuation factors.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left background is nearly Kähler S³×S³. The right discusses a mirror of a rigid CY and a qualified bulk-sector connection to DGKT. Image:6 confirms that this statement supplies no dictionary to the assigned left background.

The left's KK correction depends on a geometric-flux-dependent internal-volume normalization. The right's tadpole isolation depends on its special-geometry inputs and stated metric assumption. Neither additional operation is transferred by the proposed relation.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the mathematical operations V=e^K(g^{I J̄}D_IW overline(D_JW)−3|W|²) and D_IW=∂_IW+K_IW, using each source's own K,W and index range. Image:1 confirms the left conjugation and −3 term.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The same F-term expression and derivative definition apply to the axio-dilaton and retained complex-structure fields.

conventionDictionary.conversion: There is no asserted field identification. In particular S_L must not be equated to S_R simply because the symbols agree. Their logarithmic weights and saxion conventions differ.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: K_L=−ln(S_L+S̄_L)−3ln(T_L+T̄_L)−3ln(U_L+Ū_L)−3ln C_L. Saxions are Re S_L, Re T_L, Re U_L. Image:3 confirms the logarithms and C_L factors.

Converting a right matrix normalized by signed Λ_AdS to normalization by |Λ_AdS| introduces an overall minus sign. No absolute ten-dimensional scale matching is needed.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The reduced Planck mass is set to one. Λ_AdS=−3e^K|W|²<0, and Eq. (3.16) divides the physical mass matrix by this signed quantity; image:5 confirms the denominator.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use each Kähler metric to normalize fluctuations before comparing mass operators. In Planck units, the real-coordinate Hessian with kinetic metric G=2g has mass operator G^−1H=(1/2)g^−1H; its symmetric canonical representative is G^−1/2 H G^−1/2. Complex and real canonical coordinates differ by the usual √2 convention. This identifies the procedure, not the numerical matrices.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Eq. (3.14) supplies complex Hessian blocks at supersymmetry. For σ=Im S_R and v=Im τ, image:5 gives Ŝ=ΔS_R/σ and τ̂=√3 Δτ/(2v).

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both use a flux-dependent holomorphic W as input to the F-term procedure. No map of flux integers, cycle bases or compactification geometries is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Eq. (2.6) supplies W_L/C_L with RR, NS-NS and geometric-flux terms.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: W_R=∫(F_3−S_RH_3)∧Ω. Image:4 confirms Π=(F_a,u^a), Ω=u^aα_a−F_aβ^a, ∫α_a∧β^b=δ_a^b and reversed wedge order with a minus sign. The tadpole convention is N_flux=∫H_3∧F_3.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: C_R is the reported positive zeroth-order coefficient of Ṽ=e^−K V as a polynomial in Im S_R.

limitations: The relation identifies a common implemented procedure; neither supplied paper explicitly reports this cross-paper relation. Earlier reviewers' assertions provide no premise for it.

No complete Hessian diagonalization, numerical flux search or full-paper mathematical verification was performed. The left spectrum and right physical matrix remain source-reported results (5cd68d47f3a9d593d007:p0007s001; f4a5aa09dcceeb50511f:p0014s001).

The right's further lightest-eigenvalue expression assumes zero phases of x and y. That extra restriction is not needed or imposed for the procedure-use assertion (f4a5aa09dcceeb50511f:p0014s001–p0014s002).

The tadpole-dependent polynomial is reported conditionally on the stated metric assumption; its Appendix B derivation is outside this assertion and was not reproduced (f4a5aa09dcceeb50511f:p0012s001–p0012s002).

The relation establishes no EFT control regime, stability of omitted modes or equality of physical KK scales. The right leaves twisted-modulus stabilization for future work, while the left's corrected KK comparison requires its geometric normalization (f4a5aa09dcceeb50511f:p0010s002; 5cd68d47f3a9d593d007:p0006s002; 5cd68d47f3a9d593d007:p0008s001).

endpoints.text: For the simple flux vector with B=0, the source reviews a supersymmetric stationary point where the six independent shapes coincide. It gives three numerical constants and two equations fixing the dilaton and volume. The eight retained real scalars are stabilized; the twisted sector is not included.

The authors obtain a supersymmetric AdS3 critical point with all eight untwisted dilaton/geometric scalar masses nonzero in the main flux model, and parametric weak coupling, large volume and scale separation. This is a statement about the analyzed closed geometric sector.

records.exactAssertion: Right → left, analogy_only: within their respective classical closed untwisted effective theories, the right main-model critical point parallels the left reviewed B=0/leading-large-f critical point. Both sources report supersymmetric AdS3 stabilization of eight retained real scalars using the real-superpotential framework, with gs∼f^(-3/4), VE∼f^(49/16), VS∼f^(7/4), and characteristic LKK/LAdS∼f^(-1/2) at fixed positive h,m. This is a comparison of source-reported construction patterns and asymptotic powers. Their flux-induced D2 tadpoles differ. The edge excludes equality or specialization of the stationary points, identification of absolute coefficients or spectra, attribution that the right uses the left result as its method, and any transfer of stabilization to the left model's twisted or open sectors.

intersection.statement: Both constructions use massive IIA with F0, F4 and H3 fluxes and O2/O6 sources, reduced on a seven-dimensional G2 space to three-dimensional minimal supergravity with a real superpotential.
The comparison concerns the eight retained real closed untwisted scalars: seven geometric degrees of freedom and the dilaton. Both sources report supersymmetric AdS3 stabilization in that sector.
At fixed positive h and m, each source considers a large positive F4-amplitude parameter f and reports weak coupling, large volume and a decreasing characteristic KK-to-AdS length ratio.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the comparison to the classical effective descriptions with integrated tadpole cancellation. It does not require an exact localized ten-dimensional solution.

Interpret stabilization as the sources' absence of flat directions among the eight retained scalars. Do not extend it to brane-position fields, twisted fields or a requirement that every squared mass be positive.
Compare powers of each source's own f while holding h, m and the displayed flux ratios fixed. No equality of absolute flux units or numerical coefficients is assumed.
Compare the characteristic scale-separation ratios quoted by the sources. The left source explicitly uses volume as a KK-scale proxy; equality of complete KK spectra is excluded.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both sources display the potential form Vpot = inverse-metric contraction of dP with itself minus 4P squared.
The flux choices and stationary-point reports are explicit. Images 1 and 3 confirm the left stationary equations and the right coupling, periods, volumes and squared scale ratio.
The left source reports eight nonzero mass eigenvalues; the right explicitly reports all masses nonzero in its untwisted model. Images 2 and 3 confirm the respective displayed spectra.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left B=0 representative has H3 coefficients all h and F4 coefficients (-f,-f,-f,-f,-f,-f,+6f), with zero flux-induced D2 tadpole. The right has F4 coefficients all -f and H3 coefficients (+h,+h,+h,+h,-h,-h,-h), giving a nonzero pairing and ND2 = hf/(2π)^5 + 2. The left source instead describes an f-independent required D2 count or its replacement by tadpole-completing F4B.

The reported stationary coordinates and spectra differ. The left uses six equal independent shape coordinates and reports dimensions (11.44,4.48,3.84,3.09,3.09,3.09,3.09,3.09); the right gives physical periods in groups of four and three and dimensions (34/25,34/25,34/25,112/25,112/25,2.89,4.15,7.91). These are source reports, not a reconstructed common Hessian.

The left endpoint omits the twisted sector. The right endpoint is its Section 2.3 untwisted result; its subsequent blow-up analysis is a separate contribution. Image 4 explicitly qualifies the F4-only bosonic calculation as insufficient by itself to prove perturbative stability.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the dimensional setting and the algebraic potential form, not the complete potential functions or scalar metrics. Vpot denotes scalar potential, distinguished from internal volume.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Three-dimensional N=1 supergravity; Vpot = g^{ij} ∂iP ∂jP - 4P^2. Supersymmetric AdS3 requires ∂iP=0 and P≠0.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: gs=e^ϕ = [2·14^(3/4)·sqrt(5)/21] h m^(-1/4) f^(-3/4), confirmed in image 3.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare VE with the right Einstein-frame volume and VS with the right string-frame volume at the level of reported f exponents. The right explicitly gives VS=gs^(7/4)VE. Absolute volume coefficients are not equated.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The volume denoted by calligraphic V is Einstein-frame volume; calligraphic VS is string-frame volume. Eq. (2.20) gives V=VS/gs^(7/4); string length is restored explicitly in Eq. (3.33).

endpoints.text: The instability supplies evidence for the AdS swampland conjecture by removing this long-standing candidate counterexample. The conjecture concerns instability of all non-supersymmetric AdS vacua in string theory; this calculation addresses the particular SO(3) × SO(3) vacuum.

Reviewing [12], the SO(3)×SO(3) nonsupersymmetric AdS4 vacuum is stable in the lowest multiplet and at n=1, but has BF-violating scalars at n=2 and higher examined levels. At n=2, a singlet has m²L_AdS²≈−3.117 below −2.25. The authors interpret this instability as evidence for, rather than proof of, the nonsupersymmetric-AdS swampland conjecture.

records.exactAssertion: At the level of reported results, the right endpoint restates the left endpoint's local instability-and-conjecture-evidence result for the SO(3) × SO(3) nonsupersymmetric AdS4 uplift. With μ=m²L²=m²L_AdS² and (d1,d2)=(2j1+1,2j2+1), both report a physical n=2 singlet with μ≈−3.117 below the scalar BF threshold −2.25, despite no BF violation at n=0 or n=1. Both interpret the resulting eleven-dimensional perturbative instability as evidence against this candidate counterexample. The direction runs from the right-hand restatement to the left-hand result. This assertion excludes independent corroboration, equality of unnormalized mass operators or the full KK tower, nonlinear decay conclusions, and proof of the universal swampland conjecture.

Numerical distances, boundary prescriptions, and distance-conjecture parameters have not been reproduced or compared across theories; the right later uses string-frame KK scalings, which cannot silently be combined with the left conventions [43ed00b9bc39e2445e7b:p0028s002; b5f0ec67030dbefac468:p0021s002].

endpoints.text: For the exponential Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton setting, an extremal charged black hole obeys a charge-to-ADM-mass relation with μ = (d−3)/(d−2) + α·α/4. The reviewed Sublattice WGC requires physical states on at least a finite-index charge sublattice to meet or exceed that bound. The source states that this condition implies the Convex Hull Condition and is stable under dimensional reduction.

For a dilaton-dependent coupling, the review gives a dimension- and dilaton-dependent black-hole extremality factor and proposes the corresponding particle bound. Its weak-coupling comparison with the scalar WGC is motivated by an assumed compatible exponential particle-mass dependence, rather than a general discharge proof.

records.exactAssertion: Insufficient evidence establishes a directed relation between the nonzero-dilaton extremality and particle thresholds of these endpoints, even after restriction to d=4 and one U(1). Their Einstein and gauge normalizations can be aligned, but the scalar coordinate in right (3.50)–(3.51) lacks the kinetic dictionary needed to identify its δ²/2 contribution with left (2.5)'s (α·α)/4. The formal condition α·α=2δ² is a conditional reconstruction, not an established physical dictionary. This verdict asserts neither agreement nor disagreement. Equivalence of state-population requirements, arbitrary-dimension normalization, and scalar-force or discharge theorems is excluded.

intersection.statement: Restrict the comparison to d=4, one U(1), and classical Einstein–Maxwell theory with an active, potential-free dilaton and exponential gauge kinetic function. Both displayed extremality formulas include this sector; their scalar normalizations have not yet been identified.
Compare ADM extremality at a fixed asymptotic scalar value and the numerical particle charge-to-mass thresholds at that background. This comparison does not require differentiating the particle mass.

missing_assumptions: The scalar kinetic normalization for precisely the coordinate φ_R appearing in e^(−δ_R φ_R) in right equation (3.50), including any redefinition of δ_R from the preceding example, is not established. Writing its kinetic term as −(M_p²/2) k_R(∂φ_R)², coefficient matching with the left convention would require k_R=1/2 for nonzero δ_R. This requirement is reconstructed, not supplied as a fact [bad4e0dcb505e4ada037:p0006s002; bad4e0dcb505e4ada037:p0006s003; bad4e0dcb505e4ada037:p0007s001; 5355278e70712927024d:p0056s001].

required_assumptions.statement: Use the displayed classical actions with a propagating positive-kinetic-energy scalar and no scalar potential. The left scalar must remain active in the black-hole solution; its stated massive, inactive alternative removes the scalar contribution.

Identify the four-dimensional Einstein coefficients and use the same gauge-field normalization relative to the matter current. A rescaling of charge alone cannot be used to repair the scalar coefficient.

An admissible scalar dictionary must match both the kinetic term and the exponential gauge function. Matching the printed coefficients by setting ||α||²=2δ² without checking the kinetic terms is insufficient.
Evaluate both black-hole quantities using asymptotic scalar data, rather than replacing the asymptotic value by a horizon attractor value.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly fixes a constant scalar metric, dimensionless scalar coordinates, a common exponential gauge kinetic matrix, and the asymptotic evaluation prescription.
The displayed Einstein and gauge terms permit an action-level four-dimensional comparison with M_Pl=M_p and f=g^(−2), keeping the matter-current normalization fixed.
Both formulas explicitly contain the d=4 scalar-free limit, where their particle thresholds reduce to g²q²M_p² ≥ m²/2. This check does not determine the nonzero-dilaton normalization.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left statement requires physical states on a charge sublattice; the right displayed conjecture requires a particle. Equality of numerical thresholds would not equate these population requirements.

The left multi-U(1) formula assumes a common scalar exponential. The right preceding two-charge example has a diamond-shaped extremal charge-to-mass locus and cannot automatically be identified with that multi-U(1) setting.

The review's four-dimensional WGC discussion defines a particle as having m<M_p; the left displayed sublattice statement supplies no corresponding mass cutoff. No equivalence of the allowed state populations is asserted.

conventionDictionary.concept: Dimension, Einstein frame and Planck normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: Restrict to d=4 and identify M_Pl=M_p through the coefficient M²R/2. This removes the separate arbitrary-dimension ambiguity in the printed Planck power.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The Einstein term has coefficient M_Pl^(d−2)/2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The displayed four-dimensional Einstein term has coefficient M_p²/2.

conventionDictionary.concept: Gauge kinetic function and quantized charge
conventionDictionary.conversion: Using F∧*F=(F_μνF^μν/2)*1 gives f=g^(−2) and q_L=q_R in a common current normalization. Thus q_L²/f=g²q_R². Image:2 confirms the left gauge-form coefficient; its relative factor of 1/4 concerns its cited supergravity conventions and is not an additional factor relative to the right action.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Gauge term −fF∧*F/2; charges enter D_μ=∂_μ+iqA_μ. The extremality quadratic form uses f^(−1), not f.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Gauge term −F_μνF^μν/(4g²); the gauge normalization is fixed relative to integer charges in the matter current.

conventionDictionary.concept: Scalar coordinate, exponential sign and kinetic normalization
conventionDictionary.conversion: For a putative right kinetic term −(M_p²/2)k_R(∂φ_R)², set χ_L=√k_R φ_R up to a shift. Exponential matching then gives α_L=−δ_R/√k_R and α_L²=δ_R²/k_R. Equality of the reported scalar contributions requires k_R=1/2 for δ_R≠0; equivalently one possible signed dictionary is φ_R=−√2χ_L and α_L=√2δ_R. The required k_R is not established by the supplied right context.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: In a unit-metric one-scalar coordinate χ_L, the kinetic term is −M_Pl²(∂χ_L)²/2 and f=f_0 exp[α_L(χ_L−χ_L0)]. More generally α·α uses the stated constant scalar metric.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (3.50) describes e^(−δ_Rφ_R)F² and (3.51) states g²=e^(δ_Rφ_R). Their scalar kinetic coefficient is not displayed there. The later canonically normalized KK field ϕ in (3.54) is not explicitly identified with this φ_R.

conventionDictionary.conversion: At d=4, μ_L=1/2+α_L²/4 and C_R=1/2+δ_R²/2. They coincide formally when α_L²=2δ_R². Images:1 and :3 confirm the respective denominators 4 and 2; this difference is present in the supplied PDF images.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: C_R=(d−3)/(d−2)+δ_R²/2, with black-hole equation 𝒬²=2C_R M_ADM².

conventionDictionary.concept: Black-hole charge norm and ADM mass
conventionDictionary.conversion: In common Planck units and the one-active-charge restriction of (3.45), identify q_0=Q_L and g_0²=f^(−1). Then 𝒬²/2=Q_L²/f. Accordingly the explicit factor 2 in right (3.50) does not itself contradict left (2.4).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Q_L is black-hole charge and M_ADM its ADM mass; Q_L²/f=μ_L M_ADM²/M_Pl² in d=4.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The preceding example defines 𝒬²=2(q_0²g_0²+q_1²g_1²); 𝒬 is therefore not simply the integer black-hole charge.

conventionDictionary.conversion: At d=4 the displayed inequalities have identical gauge and mass units after f=g^(−2), and both allow saturation. Matching the coefficient would identify a numerical threshold only; it would not identify the sublattice and existential assertions.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Physical states on at least a charge sublattice satisfy q²/f ≥ μ_L m²/M_Pl².
conventionDictionary.right_definition: A particle should satisfy g²q²M_p² ≥ C_R m².

limitations: Only the supplied spans and four attached images were checked. Earlier extraction and review assertions were not treated as independent evidence or proof.

Neither imported black-hole solution was independently derived. The assessment checks the displayed formulas and the requirements for a physical convention dictionary [bad4e0dcb505e4ada037:p0007s001; 5355278e70712927024d:p0056s001].

An arbitrary-dimension equivalence would additionally require the right Planck and gauge-coupling units: right (3.51) prints M_p², whereas left (2.7) uses M_Pl^(d−2). That extension is explicitly excluded from the chosen four-dimensional comparison [bad4e0dcb505e4ada037:p0007s002; 5355278e70712927024d:p0056s001].

A proof relating particle mass derivatives to black-hole discharge is excluded. The supplied right text describes an expected exponential mass dependence and explicitly leaves strong-coupling or non-dilatonic necessity difficult; its carried anchor fragment must not be read as a completed proof [5355278e70712927024d:p0056s001; 5355278e70712927024d:p0056s002].

The right source cautions that the one-active-charge example is not well understood at the horizon and proceeds by probing from infinity. No additional horizon regularity claim is inferred [5355278e70712927024d:p0056s001].

endpoints.text: Generate charged black branes from the Horowitz–Strominger solutions by lifting and dimensional reduction; rotate scalar combinations into coupled and decoupled fields. Lift charged black holes to strings, boost along the compact direction, and reduce to obtain mixed KK charges and ADM extremality bounds.

Construct charged black holes by boosting a five-dimensional black string, compactifying the boost direction and performing Kaluza-Klein reduction. Take distinct extremal limits to separate the BPS and non-BPS branches.

records.exactAssertion: The right method uses the boost-then-circle-reduction operation expressly contained in the left method: its five-dimensional charged black string is boosted along the longitudinal Killing direction and compactified to produce a four-dimensional black hole with momentum charge carried by the metric KK vector. This relation is restricted to that classical solution-generation stage and its geometric KK connection, with D=5 and d=4. It excludes identity of seeds, actions, scalar normalizations, Horowitz–Strominger derivations, signed flux normalizations, extremality bounds, convex-hull results, BPS classifications and higher-derivative conclusions. It asserts operational use, not historical dependence or citation of the left paper.

intersection.statement: The common operation starts with a charged black string independent of its longitudinal coordinate, boosts along that coordinate, and reduces after imposing a circle identification. The right construction realizes this operation with D=5 and d=4.

The comparison concerns the classical geometric KK connection and generation of momentum charge. It does not require identifying the preexisting charge, the full scalar action, or the extremality surfaces.

required_assumptions.statement: Use a longitudinal Killing direction and the coordinate-independent fields retained by the source reduction ansatz.
Apply the boost before the stated circle identification; compare the resulting reduced solution with the unboosted seed.
Restrict the explicit geometric check to R>0, r>r0>0, and finite real rapidities, so the compact direction remains spacelike and nondegenerate.
Compare the displayed classical construction with its accompanying scalar fields retained. Do not transfer the result to a stabilized-scalar theory or to the corrected extremal geometry.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left prescription makes the lifted solution constant along the extra direction. The right seed and boosted metric depend on r and have no z dependence.
Both sources explicitly order the operations as boost followed by compactification/reduction; the right identification is z~z+2πR.
In the restricted domain, H1=1+(r0/r)sinh²γ1 and Hp=1+(r0/r)sinh²γp are positive. The reconstructed longitudinal metric component is gzz=Hp/H1>0.

The left ansatz retains the radion, and the right construction supplies a nonconstant four-dimensional dilaton. The assertion stops at the classical construction; the right source separately warns that its extremal small holes require significant α' corrections.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left endpoint also includes Horowitz–Strominger seed generation and scalar rotation. The right passage starts from an already charged string; it does not establish use of those earlier stages.

The left distinguishes strings carrying smeared one-form charge from strings charged under two-forms. Its displayed Eqs. (45)–(53) concern the former. No identification of that specific action or seed with the right winding-charged seed is asserted.

The right assigns heterotic BPS and non-BPS interpretations to distinct extremal limits. The shared boost/reduction operation alone supplies neither that classification nor equality with the left convex-hull or extremality results.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Restrict the left prescription to D=5, d=4; identify the longitudinal coordinates y and z and their period 2πR.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: D=d+1; y~y+2πR.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Five-dimensional string reduced to four dimensions with z~z+2πR.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the longitudinal boost and the ratio gμz/gzz. That ratio is invariant under an overall metric Weyl rescaling, so this comparison does not identify the two dilatons or full Einstein-frame metrics.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Mostly-plus signature; Einstein gravitational action and Einstein-frame reduction ansatz.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Mostly-plus displayed metrics; the seed and initial reduced metric are explicitly in string frame, followed by an Einstein-frame expression.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Set u=coshγp and v=-sinhγp. Then u²-v²=1 and the coordinate transformations coincide. The negative sign follows the right Eq. (4.3), checked in image:4.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: t→ut+vy, y→uy+vt, with u²-v²=1.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: t→coshγp t-sinhγp z, z→coshγp z-sinhγp t.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Define R Bμ=gμz/gzz using the left metric decomposition. The right boosted metric gives R Bt=-(r0/r)sinhγp coshγp/Hp. This is a reconstructed geometric connection; no equality of signed flux-normalized charges is assumed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: dsD²=e^{λ/(d-2)}dsd²+e^{-λ}(dy+RB1)²; H2=dB1.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The boost generates gtz in Eq. (4.4); z is subsequently reduced.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match the roles of q and n as integer momentum labels on a circle. Keep w, QL and QR distinct. Their signed flux dictionary and an identification of the preexisting charge are excluded.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: KK charge q is integral and labels momentum q/R. General p-form electric charge Q has the flux definition in Eq. (9).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: n and w are integer momentum and winding charges; QL=n/R-wR/α', QR=n/R+wR/α', as confirmed in image:5.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No scalar-field identification is used. In particular, the left conventionally normalized φ is not silently equated with the right string dilaton.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The scalar has kinetic term -(∇φ)²/2 inside the gravitational prefactor; ρ couples to the form field and the orthogonal σ is set to zero in the seed-generation construction.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The four-dimensional string dilaton satisfies e^{-2φ}=√(H1Hp).

conventionDictionary.conversion: Treat γ1 and γp on the right as rapidities only. The right subscript p labels momentum, not the degree of the left gauge potential.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: p is the degree of Ap; γp;d(α)=[α²/2+p(d-p-2)/(d-2)]^{-1}. Image:1 confirms this definition.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: γ1 and γp are boost parameters entering Hi=1+(r0/r)sinh²γi.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Rename the right M4 as M_ADM to avoid confusing it with the left reduced Planck mass. The displayed formulas consistently use [R]=[r0]=length, [G4]=[α']=length² and [M_ADM]=[QL]=[QR]=length^{-1}; n and w are dimensionless.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: κd²=8πGd and Md^{d-2}=1/κd²; M4 denotes the reduced Planck mass.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: G4 is the four-dimensional Newton constant; M4=r0(2+cosh2γ1+cosh2γp)/(8G4) is the ADM mass.

limitations: Only the packet's supplied passages and six attached images were checked. Upstream node labels and earlier reviews were not used as scientific premises.

A stronger specialization or solution-equivalence claim would require the left section on reduction of two-form-charged black strings and the complete higher-dimensional gauge and dilaton fields of the right seed. Those identifications are excluded here, rather than assumed. Relevant supplied boundaries: c76887d48c011ad5f52e:p0015s002 and 31a83a3f7888e8b785f2:p0009s001.
