No repair of that angular-metric discrepancy or full Einstein-metric comparison is used. The boost and string-frame reduction check uses Eqs. (4.1)–(4.5). Evidence: 31a83a3f7888e8b785f2:p0009s001 and 31a83a3f7888e8b785f2:p0010s001.
The left extracted extremality inequality glyphs are not needed or adjudicated. No equality of ADM extremality bounds is inferred from the shared method. Evidence: c76887d48c011ad5f52e:p0010s001.

The right source's zero-area extremal limits and discussion of α' corrections are separate from the checked construction. Its discussion of negligible loops at small gs, also checked in image:6, supplies no extension of this edge to corrected solutions. Evidence: 31a83a3f7888e8b785f2:p0010s001 and 31a83a3f7888e8b785f2:p0016s002.

endpoints.text: For supersymmetric AdS vacua, the authors conjecture α = 1/2 in the ADC. This supplies an infinite tower at the AdS curvature scale and therefore implies the weaker statement that no parametric gap separates the AdS scale from all massive states.

The ADC conjectures an infinite tower with m ∼ |Λ|^α as Λ → 0 in Planck units, with positive order-one α. Its strong supersymmetric version sets α = 1/2 and excludes scale separation when applied to a KK tower. The review stresses that the strong version lacks a particular argument beyond controlled examples.

records.exactAssertion: The endpoints state the same conjectural strong-ADC law on their shared supersymmetric, fixed-d > 2 AdS near-flat domain: an infinite tower has m/M_p ∼ (|Λ|/M_p²)^(1/2). Their cosmological-constant normalizations differ by a fixed dimension-dependent factor and therefore preserve this exponent and parametric curvature-scale relation. In their explicitly conditional KK application, both state absence of parametric KK scale separation, expressed on the right as L_KK/L_AdS = O(1). The equivalence covers only this shared strong-ADC and conditional KK content. It excludes equivalence of the entire composite right endpoint, proof of the conjecture, universal KK identity of the tower, nonsupersymmetric extensions, exact numerical coefficients and the review's additional assessment of the evidence.

intersection.statement: The shared strong-ADC domain is supersymmetric quantum-gravity AdS vacua approaching Λ = 0 from below. The radius conversion used here is restricted to fixed spacetime dimension d > 2.
Both tower laws use Planck units. Compare masses, cosmological constants and radii consistently in the external d-dimensional theory.
The common conclusion about KK scale separation applies conditionally when the tower realizing the strong ADC is a KK tower.

required_assumptions.statement: For the physical corollary, take the strong ADC as a conjectural premise on the supersymmetric branch; the source comparison itself does not establish its truth.
Keep d > 2 fixed and identify the same geometric AdS radius when converting the two cosmological-constant parameters.

For the no-separation corollary, use the papers' stated parametric proportionality: suppressed factors remain order one along the limit. An exponent alone, without this qualification, would not establish the review's order-one length ratio.
Only in the KK application identify the tower mass with an inverse KK spectral length, up to fixed order-one normalization factors.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both supplied statements explicitly posit an infinite tower and α = 1/2 for supersymmetric AdS. Images image:1 and image:3 confirm the positive one-half exponent. This establishes agreement of conjectural premises, not their physical validity.
The supplied radius formulas permit a fixed-d conversion. The assertion explicitly stays within that domain.

The left source states absence of a parametric gap as a consequence; the right source explicitly gives L_KK = c L_AdS with c an order-one constant. The comparison retains this stated parametric meaning.
Both sources explicitly formulate the KK condition. It is established as the scope of their conditional conclusion, not as a universal identification of every ADC tower.

scope_mismatches.statement: The right endpoint also summarizes the general ADC with positive order-one α. The left assigned claim concerns its supersymmetric strong form; the proposed identity covers that shared component.

An existential light tower and a KK tower are different claims. The shared generic strong ADC obstructs decoupling of all massive towers; the internal-length conclusion requires the stated KK application.

The review's assessment of the evidence, extended-supersymmetry magnetic-WGC discussion and discussion of proposed counterexamples are additional material. They are not identical to the left conjecture or an independent proof of it.

conventionDictionary.concept: Cosmological constant and geometric AdS radius
conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify R = L_AdS for the comparison. Then Λ_L = A_d Λ_R, where A_d = (d−1)(d−2)/2 is fixed at fixed d > 2. This converts the parameters in the scaling laws; it does not assert identical vacuum-energy normalizations.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equations (20)–(21) use geometric radius R = e^τ and Λ_L = −(d−1)(d−2)/(2R²).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Section 5.7 uses Λ_R = −1/L_AdS² and assigns Λ_R mass dimension two. Equation (3.24) also identifies L_AdS through R_μν = −(d−1)g_μν/L_AdS².

conventionDictionary.conversion: Write μ = m/M_p, λ = Λ/M_p² and ℓ = M_p L_AdS in a common external d-dimensional convention. Then μ ∼ |λ|^(1/2). Fixed Planck-normalization factors affect only prefactors. No constancy of M_p in string units across vacua is assumed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Equation (1) is in Planck units; the generalized-distance formulation specifies tower masses in the external Einstein frame.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (5.55) is in Planck units. Section 3.2 explains the dimension-dependent Planck mass; Equation (2.12), checked in image:4, exhibits its dependence on compactification parameters.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Identify the two ADC exponents directly: α_ADC,L = α_ADC,R = 1/2. Images image:1 and image:3 resolve the critical fraction. No identification with the separate distance exponent in Equation (7), checked in image:2, is required.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The strong ADC sets the power of |Λ| to 1/2 for supersymmetric AdS vacua.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The supersymmetric clause following Equation (5.55) sets the same power to 1/2 and names it the strong ADC.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match existential infinite-tower statements and their characteristic mass scales. Neither statement is reduced to a bound on only one massive particle.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: m is the mass scale of an infinite tower; absence of a gap to all massive states is explicitly described as a weaker consequence.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: m in Equation (5.55) is likewise the mass scale of an infinite tower.

conventionDictionary.conversion: In the common KK application, use L_KK ∼ 1/m_KK with fixed normalization factors. Thus m_KK L_AdS = O(1) corresponds to L_KK/L_AdS = O(1). This is a spectral KK scale, without a universal identification with every internal volume or curvature radius.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: When the strong-ADC tower consists of KK states, the source interprets it as absence of separation between external and internal scales.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The strong ADC applied to a KK tower yields Equation (5.56), L_KK = c L_AdS, with c an order-one constant.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare their stated parametric laws with order-one factors suppressed. No universal numerical prefactor, convergence rate or independently derived absence of logarithmic corrections is certified.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The conjecture uses m ∼ |Λ|^(1/2) and states a no-parametric-gap consequence.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The review uses the same scaling and explicitly states an order-one constant in its KK length relation.

limitations: This compares supplied source statements and reproduces their local parametric conversion. It does not establish the conjectured tower in a vacuum family.

The exact coefficient in the radius dictionary uses the supplied text of Equations (20)–(21), physical page 4 of 1906.05225; that page has no attached image. The critical absolute-value bars and positive one-half exponents are visually confirmed in image:1 and image:3.

The generalized-distance argument is not reproduced as a derivation of α = 1/2. Its supplied application gives an order-one exponent under additional kinetic assumptions, whereas the supersymmetric value is separately conjectured (beb0e182182a8a6fc3ae:p0004s003; beb0e182182a8a6fc3ae:p0005s001).

No universal internal-radius identification, numerical value of c, complete KK spectrum or correction analysis is established. The comparison retains the stated conditional KK relation (beb0e182182a8a6fc3ae:p0005s001; 113d16e2ff1f6e908859:p0064s001).

The review's magnetic-WGC route and discussion of proposed IIA counterexamples are excluded from the asserted equivalence (113d16e2ff1f6e908859:p0064s002; 113d16e2ff1f6e908859:p0065s001). Earlier extraction and review verdicts, and their claimed historical coverage, were not inherited as scientific verification.

endpoints.text: An agent reconstruction using the metric weights and Weyl factor gives bulk KK mass n^{-7/4}, AdS inverse radius n^{-9/4}, and hierarchy n^{1/2} in four-dimensional Planck units. If a nonzero AdS potential scales as n^{-9/2}, the bulk KK exponent is 7/18. These exponents are reconstructed from supplied premises rather than quoted from omitted pages.

The introduction reports a relation obtaining the entire spin-2 spectrum of each non-supersymmetric sibling from its supersymmetric partner by a simple mass shift. Universal low-lying spin-2 modes have masses at the cosmological-constant scale, excluding a parametrically larger KK gap for this family. The modes are reported unaffected by orientifold planes. The detailed operator, shift formula, mode functions and normalizability arguments are in Section 7, outside this window.

records.exactAssertion: Left-to-right diagnostic analogy only: the left endpoint's conditional bulk hierarchy Q_bulk = M_KK/sqrt(|Λ_curv|) ~ n^(1/2) and the right endpoint's reported universal spin-2 mode with Q_mode = O(1) use the same KK-to-AdS-curvature comparison. Their evidential roles differ: a bulk hierarchy estimate does not establish a gap in every sector, whereas an admissible nonzero mode at the AdS scale upper-bounds that gap. This assertion compares source-reported diagnostics and conditional scaling bookkeeping. It excludes a shared vacuum or limit, spectral equivalence, method inheritance, support for either family's physical existence, a contradiction between the families, and certification of the complete localized KK gap.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints assess a KK mass relative to the AdS curvature mass. Their intersection is this hierarchy diagnostic, not a common compactification or spectrum.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare dimensionless mass-to-curvature ratios within each lower-dimensional theory; fixed normalization constants may be suppressed, but vacuum-energy density must first be converted to curvature units.
The assertion concerns the diagnostics and scalings reported in the supplied sources. It does not certify their spectral or global existence premises, and it retains each source's family restriction.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly distinguishes M_KK^2/|Λ|, which diagnoses curvature separation, from M_KK^4/|Λ|, which compares with the vacuum-energy scale.

Image:4 confirms m_Λ = sqrt(|Λ|), the one-mode strategy, and the reported universal low-lying spin-2 modes. These establish the right source's intended diagnostic without establishing its omitted spectral calculation.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left concerns Type IIA AdS4 Calabi-Yau orientifolds with O6-planes; the right concerns Type IIB AdS6 uplifts with internal S2 fibred over Σ. Their external dimensions, internal geometries and source configurations differ.

The left estimates a KK scale from cycle volumes and reported parametric scalings. The right reports physical spin-2 modes that obstruct a large KK gap. A bulk scale estimate and an upper bound on the first massive level have different quantifiers.

The left limit varies F4 flux through n. The right compares supersymmetric and non-supersymmetric siblings with identical five-brane charges; the supplied spin-2 summary supplies no corresponding n-limit. No common parameter trajectory is established.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use B_A for the dimensionless curvature magnitude associated with the left vacuum, proportional to |<V_E>| in its displayed Planck convention, and B_B = (m_Λ/m_P,6)^2 on the right. Compare Q_A = (M_KK/m_P,4)/sqrt(B_A) and Q_B = m_mode/m_Λ. Only fixed-factor scaling is identified. In particular, image:3 shows Λ/M_P^d in Eq. (6.10), whereas image:4 defines a mass by sqrt(|Λ|); these dimensionful uses of Λ must not be equated directly.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: S_4 = integral sqrt(-g_E)(R_E - V_E), V_E = V/(2π V_w^2); the on-shell potential determines the AdS curvature.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: m_Λ = sqrt(|Λ|); m_P denotes the reduced lower-dimensional Planck mass.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Take positive masses and the absolute magnitude of the negative AdS cosmological quantity. Parametric separation requires Q_gap to grow without bound. Fixed dimension-dependent curvature normalizations do not change that test.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The relevant separation criterion is M_KK^2/|Λ| >> 1.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The absence-of-separation diagnostic is a KK mode with mass comparable to m_Λ.

endpoints.text: The authors obtain Q²≤e^γM² for Model I and Qext/Mext=e^(γ/2). They interpret γ>0 as satisfying their WGC criterion for all black-hole masses while retaining a horizon.

The adopted black-hole WGC criterion requires an M=Q configuration without a naked singularity. Using the paper's perturbative extremality relation Mext=Q−(2g4+h4)/(5Q), this criterion gives 2g4+h4≥0.

records.exactAssertion: The left Model I result is an algebraic analogy for the right node's adopted extremality diagnostic: on positive electric-charge branches, γ>0 gives Mext,L/Q_L=e^(−γ/2)<1 and a horizon at the RN reference M_L=Q_L; the right's reported linear-order relation gives Mext,R/Q_R=1−C/(5Q_R²)<1 for C=2g4+h4>0, with its adopted nonstrict criterion C≥0. It excludes a derivation of the Wilson-coefficient bound from ModMax, an operator or conserved-charge identification, a controlled EFT horizon calculation at exact M_R=Q_R, transfer of the all-mass claim, and validation of the particle WGC.

endpoints.text: The examples are presented as further evidence for the previously proposed conjecture that every non-supersymmetric AdS vacuum supported by fluxes is unstable. They do not establish that universal conjecture.

The instability supplies evidence for the AdS swampland conjecture by removing this long-standing candidate counterexample. The conjecture concerns instability of all non-supersymmetric AdS vacua in string theory; this calculation addresses the particular SO(3) × SO(3) vacuum.

records.exactAssertion: The packet supports an analogy from the left claim to the right claim in evidentiary role: each paper presents particular non-supersymmetric AdS instabilities as evidence for a broader instability conjecture. The left uses bubble-of-nothing examples in AdS5; the right uses higher-KK BF violations in the SO(3)×SO(3) AdS4 vacuum. This assertion concerns the reported claims and preserves the left conjecture's flux qualification. It excludes implication between the local results, identification of the vacua or mechanisms, method transfer, equivalence of the complete conjecture domains, and proof of a universal conjecture.

endpoints.text: The authors establish absence of scale separation for all supersymmetric AdS7 solutions and their known sisters through universal spin-2 masses M²_susy=8ℓ(2ℓ+3) and M²_non-susy=12ℓ(ℓ+2). At ℓ=1 these are 40 and 36, comparable to |R_AdS7|=42. This is not a classification-wide theorem for non-supersymmetric vacua.

The authors find supersymmetric numerical vacua with six KK scales well above the AdS scale and a seventh tower at or below it, producing an effective AdS3×S1 exterior. Their γ=10⁹, N∼10¹⁹ example has gs∼10−13 and all internal radii large, with finite rather than parametric anisotropy.

records.exactAssertion: At the level of the reported spectra and KK estimates, the left claim provides a qualitative analogy for the right's gamma=10^9, K=-16, M=-1, N approximately 10^19 example: each retains KK excitations without a parametrically large mass relative to its AdS scale, so the nominal AdS dimension alone does not capture all AdS-scale modes. On the right this concerns the seventh tower; the other six towers are heavy, giving the reported effective AdS3 x S1 exterior. This asserts no common spectrum, implication between solution classes, transfer of the AdS7 theorem, method dependence, or tension. It excludes the right's fully scale-separated large-N AdS3 regime and makes no claim about localized string completion or the impossibility of consistent truncations.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints discuss KK decoupling at an AdS scale in supersymmetric type-IIA compactifications. Their intersection is a spectral diagnostic, not an identified common background.
The left's reported universal modes and the right's specified anisotropic example both retain KK excitations whose masses are not parametrically above the respective AdS scale.

The right's finite anisotropic regime must be distinguished from its parametrically large-N regime, where all seven internal directions become scale-separated from AdS3. The latter is outside the chosen analogy.

endpoints.text: The authors calculate positive leading entropy corrections for charged black holes in their two dominant-effect regimes, subject to the D=4 topological qualification. At the uncorrected extremal bound, F(ai)>0 produces two horizons and a positive outer-horizon entropy shift, linking entropy positivity to the favorable extremality shift.

The discussion newly conjectures that the first correction to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy obtained by applying higher-derivative terms to Wald's formula is positive in all cases. The paper reports no known counterexample but supplies neither a general proof nor an explicit entropy calculation in the provided pages.

records.exactAssertion: Defer the candidate left-to-right support relation. The left source calculates a conditional positive total entropy change using its specified comparison with Einstein–Maxwell solutions; the right conjectures positive entropy corrections without identifying the corresponding fixed variables or comparison branch. These missing definitions are decisive because different comparison prescriptions can give different signs, even within a formal quartic-field sector. The packet therefore does not establish support or contradiction between the exact endpoint claims. This abstention excludes universal positivity, equality of the two entropy observables, and any inference of entropy positivity from mass lowering alone.

intersection.statement: A candidate common setting is a static, spherical, electrically charged Einstein–Maxwell black hole with perturbative higher-derivative corrections and entropy evaluated through Wald's formula. This establishes a common subject, but not an identical entropy comparison prescription.

missing_assumptions: The right conjecture must identify the variables held fixed when defining the entropy correction, particularly fixed mass and charge versus fixed charge along the corrected extremal branch.
The right conjecture must specify whether its correction includes the changed horizon area as well as the explicit higher-curvature contribution to Wald's formula.

required_assumptions.statement: A directed support relation requires matching entropy observables, reference solutions and fixed variables. Positivity for a black hole at the uncorrected extremal mass and charge cannot automatically be substituted for positivity along the corrected extremal family.

The left sign argument requires small higher-derivative effects, its specified dominance assumptions, and negligible relevant topological contribution in D=4. Away from extremality, the actual ξ-weighted quartic-field contribution must dominate the remaining terms.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly defines the total entropy correction as ΔS=ΔS_horizon+ΔS_Wald, with the outer event horizon used.

The left calculation supplies a comparison at the same mass and charge: it perturbs the metric and horizon while retaining the Einstein–Maxwell parameters m and q. Its ξ=0 reference saturates the uncorrected extremality bound.
The right source explicitly labels entropy positivity a conjecture and requests checks or a proof. The conjecture paragraph does not define its fixed-variable prescription.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left result is conditional on two dominant-effect regimes and a D=4 topological qualification; the right proposes positivity 'in all cases' without a corresponding precise domain.

The left ξ=0 entropy shift compares solutions at the classical extremal mass and charge and starts at square-root order in the higher-derivative coefficients. The right does not specify whether this is its intended 'first correction'. Image:2 confirms the square root in S54.

The displayed hierarchy alone does not demonstrate uniform positivity arbitrarily near ξ=1: the quartic-field term in G is proportional to (1−ξ)^2, whereas the a4 contribution survives at ξ=1. S40 also explicitly excludes the ξ≈0 limit.

endpoints.text: The authors find a supersymmetric AdS5 → AdS3 × R2 example when the nonzero charges obey q1+q2+q3=0 and the background D field balances B. The IR solution satisfies the supersymmetry conditions and degenerates if any charge vanishes.

Flipping the F₄ sign in the F₄B=0 example produces a nonsupersymmetric AdS₃ solution with the same bosonic potential and positive Hessian in the eight-scalar sector. At the reported extremum V≠−4P², identifying supersymmetry breaking.

records.exactAssertion: Left→right is an algebraic analogy only: the left fixed-point metric and scalar expressions are insensitive to individual charge signs, while supersymmetry is checked separately using signed BPS conditions; the right Appendix C potential is even in its F4 coefficient f, while its sign-sensitive superpotential is checked separately and the flipped vacuum is reported nonsupersymmetric. The arrow orders the comparison and asserts no implication, specialization or method dependence. This does not identify the backgrounds, fluxes, superpotentials or stability spectra; does not claim that a left charge-sign reversal necessarily breaks supersymmetry or that both D signs have the same AdS dual. The assertion uses Appendix C's displayed reversal without establishing the node's F4B=0 decomposition, a complete ten-dimensional solution, or stability outside its reported eight-scalar sector.

intersection.statement: Both endpoints concern AdS3 sectors described by supergravity, with bosonic expressions and separate supersymmetry checks. Their intersection supports an algebraic comparison, without establishing a common compactification or parameter regime.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the left comparison to the displayed nondegenerate fixed-point expressions, with B>0, finite nonzero g and all qI nonzero. Their algebraic sign invariance is not a claim that every sign change preserves the chosen Killing spinor.

Restrict the right comparison to Appendix C's displayed potential and its reported F4 reversal. In checking dependence on f, hold the other coefficients and scalar arguments fixed; do not extend the result to additional flux sectors.

Keep bosonic sign dependence, preserved supersymmetry and scalar stability as separate questions. Supersymmetry conclusions use the sources' model-specific tests, rather than sign invariance or Hessian positivity alone.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly supplies B>0, the nonzero-charge restriction, the conventional signs q1,q2>0 and q3<0, the fixed-point formulas, and their separate supersymmetry condition.

Appendix C displays f only through f² in its scalar potential, while its displayed superpotential contains a term linear in f. It separately reports the supersymmetry-breaking diagnostic at the extremum.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left construction uses the five-dimensional U(1)³ truncation of IIB on S5 and a magnetic plane; the right uses IIA compactification on a seven-dimensional G2 orientifold to three dimensions. The right abstract qualifies its AdS description as a smeared-orientifold effective description.

The left auxiliary-field choices D=±2B both preserve field-theory supersymmetry; for the stated charge convention the AdS dual is associated with D<0. The right operation reverses F4 and is reported to break supersymmetry. These operations are not interchangeable.

The left endpoint concerns a BPS fixed point and degeneration at vanishing charge. The right endpoint additionally reports positive eigenvalues in an eight-scalar sector. Neither statement transfers a stability spectrum to the other model.

endpoints.text: The proposed vacua are potential counterexamples to the strong AdS distance conjecture when the relevant tower is the KK tower. The authors state compatibility with its discrete-gauge-symmetry refinement; unexamined towers prevent an unrestricted conclusion about the strong conjecture.

Conditional WGC arguments obstruct scale separation for 4d N≥2 AdS vacua with unbroken U(1), identifying the EFT cutoff with M_KK. The strong AdS distance conjecture likewise forbids supersymmetric separation if its tower is KK: α=1/2 in m/M_p ∼ |Λ|^α. Weaker α<1/2 permits separation; DGKT gives α=7/18.

records.exactAssertion: Restricted to its strong-ADC/KK component, the right endpoint supports the left endpoint's classification of the reported supersymmetric, parametrically KK-separated DGKT-dual proposals as potential counterexamples under the KK-tower identification: alpha=1/2 requires M_KK times the AdS radius to remain of fixed parametric order, whereas the reported separation requires that product to grow without bound. This edge concerns interpretation of the reported construction. It excludes proof of a completed vacuum or unrestricted ADC violation, application of the N>=2 WGC obstruction, transfer of alpha=7/18 to the left families, and verification of the discrete-symmetry refinement.

intersection.statement: The common domain is the supersymmetric AdS4 branch, evaluated under the explicit identification of the ADC tower with KK modes. Both sources state the same alpha=1/2 obstruction in this domain.
The compared hierarchy is between the KK mass and inverse AdS curvature radius along a parametric family. Separation from the vacuum-energy length L_rho is a distinct, stronger requirement.

required_assumptions.statement: Use the supersymmetric strong-ADC hypothesis alpha=1/2 and stipulate m=M_KK. These are the hypotheses of the comparison, not independently established facts about a completed compactification.

Evaluate masses and radii consistently in the external four-dimensional Einstein description, normalizing masses by the corresponding vacuum Planck scale. Compare parametric behavior, retaining only parameter-independent convention factors.
Interpret the displayed power laws as leading asymptotic scalings with nonzero, parameter-independent prefactors as the dimensionless negative cosmological constant approaches zero.

Treat the left hierarchy as the authors' reported result for their proposed construction. The asserted edge concerns its conditional interpretation; it does not require establishing an exact localized string or M-theory vacuum.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both sources explicitly formulate the supersymmetric alpha=1/2 condition and the KK-tower identification, so the conditional diagnostic is supplied directly.
Both definitions give inverse AdS radius proportional to M_p times the square root of the absolute dimensionless vacuum potential. Their fixed normalization difference does not change the diagnostic.

The left authors explicitly report parametric AdS/KK separation, identify the proposals as potential strong-ADC counterexamples, and report verification of the hierarchy in their lifted approximation.

scope_mismatches.statement: The right WGC argument assumes four-dimensional N>=2 supersymmetry, an unbroken U(1), and identification of the EFT cutoff with M_KK. The left investigation targets N<=1. That WGC argument is not applied to the left proposals.

The left focuses on KK modes and explicitly leaves other possible light towers unexamined. The right definition also requires a winding hierarchy. The selected edge establishes neither a complete finite-field EFT nor a violation of the existential ADC over all towers.

The alpha=1/2 diagnostic applies to the reported supersymmetric branch. The left also discusses nonsupersymmetric solutions and leaves near-source completion unresolved; supersymmetry after full localization is not established by this edge.

endpoints.text: A charged black hole can discharge by thermally producing sufficiently light charged particles or by Schwinger pair production in its electric field. The dominant regime depends on black-hole mass and charge and on the emitted particle mass; the subsection absorbs its unit charge into g.
Combine discrete-charge black-hole discharge with WGC/BPS bounds and a species-type mass bound. The extremal Reissner–Nordström appendix substitutes Schwinger emission for Hawking evaporation.

records.exactAssertion: As a comparison of reported operations, the right endpoint's Appendix A uses the left endpoint's cold/extremal Schwinger-discharge prescription: it selects electric-field pair production for a massive charged particle at T_H=0. It then adds its own BPS assumption and discrete-charge energy budget to obtain a parametric mass bound. This edge is conditional on the right calculation's stated approximations. It excludes equality of the printed efficiency thresholds, validation of the curved-space rate or complete discharge dynamics, a universal species/WGC theorem, and any claim of bibliographic dependence on the left paper.

intersection.statement: The common domain is the reported semiclassical treatment of electrically charged four-dimensional black holes emitting massive charged particles in the cold or extremal regime. The right calculation selects extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes with vanishing Hawking temperature.

required_assumptions.statement: The comparison concerns the sources' stated operations. For a positive emitted-particle mass, the right endpoint's T_H=0 belongs to the left endpoint's T_H much smaller than m branch.

The right calculation conditionally uses the flat-space Schwinger exponential when the electric field dominates background curvature, and approximates emission by the near-horizon contribution. These are its declared approximations, not independently established properties of a supplied model.
The right Appendix A assumes an emitted particle carrying both continuous and discrete charge, with BPS mass m=gqM_p; its O(k) counting additionally assumes unit discrete charge.

Reproducing the right endpoint's auxiliary mass bound uses its order-of-magnitude identification of small exponential suppression with efficient discharge and its requirement that sufficient mass remain to emit O(k) particles. The resulting inequalities are parametric large-k statements.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Both source passages explicitly identify electric-field Schwinger production as the relevant cold/extremal discharge operation; the right passage explicitly states T_H=0.

Appendix A explicitly declares the BPS assumption, near-horizon approximation, efficiency estimate and unit-discrete-charge counting. Their presence in the reported prescription is established; their realization in a complete physical model is not asserted.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left endpoint also treats hot thermal discharge. That branch does not participate in the right endpoint's extremal Appendix A calculation.
The discrete-charge energy budget and BPS assumption are additional right-hand inputs. They do not follow from the left endpoint's discharge-regime classification.

The printed extremality coefficients and Schwinger efficiency formulas do not have an established numerical convention dictionary. The relation therefore identifies the operation used, without identifying the printed thresholds.

The left source leaves universal discharge necessity open. The right source acknowledges alternative emission sequences involving discrete-neutral, strictly superextremal particles and restricts its strongest carrier-identification argument to the supersymmetric setup.

endpoints.text: For a four-dimensional cutoff excluding internal KK modes, the author concludes that the proposed uplift leaves the EFT of the supersymmetric AdS starting point. Whether uplift actually reaches positive curvature remains unanswered. The discussion relates EFT validity to KPV and Klebanov–Strassler descriptions and conjectures a connection to constrained-superfield de Sitter supergravity.

With nonzero uplift, varying one parameter while holding the other fixed permits a smooth AdS–Minkowski–dS passage. The KK scale remains nonzero at the Minkowski point while H vanishes, allowing separation from the curvature scale rather than an obligatory light KK tower.

endpoints.text: The authors obtain |⟨V⟩|/mKK²∼gsρ^((p−7)/2) when a fixed orientifold contribution sets the nonzero vacuum scale. For p<7, weak coupling or large volume therefore produces separation from the overall KK tower, independently of D; numerically controlled vacua need not possess an unbounded parameter.

The authors construct weakly coupled, quantised-flux examples with volume-based scale separation for inherited vac 10,11, nonabelian vac 32,33, and magnetised vac 35–40. These statements do not establish physical separation of the full KK spectrum.

records.exactAssertion: Right→left, analogy_only: the right's reported weakly coupled AdS3 families exhibit the overall-volume hierarchy ε_vol=(vol7)^(2/7)/(τ0^(-1)L)²≪1, which matches the diagnostic underlying the left endpoint. The numerical comparison below checks the inherited vac 10,11 subfamily; the other named families are compared at the level of their reported diagnostic. Excluded are an application or specialization of the left's fixed-coefficient leading-O5 formula, a demonstrated common dynamical mechanism, physical separation of the full KK spectrum, and conclusions about fully localized solutions or stability beyond the analyzed effective theory.

intersection.statement: The dimensional overlap is type IIB compactification to D=3 with O5/D5 sources, hence p=5<7.
Both endpoints compare the external curvature length with an internal scale inferred from the overall string-frame volume. This common diagnostic does not determine the lightest physical KK mass.
The comparison concerns the papers' smeared-source effective descriptions.

required_assumptions.statement: Compare dimensionless geometric ratios at scaling order, using the external and internal lengths in the same string frame. Numerical potential normalizations and raw modulus symbols need not be identified.
Interpret the volume estimate as a proxy throughout; do not replace it with a statement about the complete KK spectrum.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left defines its internal volume in string frame; the right identifies its volume as string-frame volume and explicitly identifies τ0^(-1)L as the external length in the ten-dimensional metric.
Both sources expressly qualify the connection between their overall-volume estimate and the physical KK spectrum.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left's sufficient mechanism requires a leading orientifold contribution and control of its effective coefficient. The right establishes a fixed net source tadpole and parametrically changing internal shape. A fixed tadpole does not establish a fixed shape-dependent source coefficient or its order relative to the vacuum potential.

The left isolates an isotropic breathing modulus and acknowledges other-modulus dependence in prefactors. The right's examples have anisotropies that scale with the flux parameter, so the fixed-prefactor formula cannot be transferred silently.
The left explicitly allows anisotropic exceptions to its isotropic curvature obstruction. The right's anisotropy therefore does not establish a tension with that obstruction.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Restrict the left's dimensional labels to D=3 and p=5 for comparison with the right.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: D is the external spacetime dimension; p labels an Op/Dp source.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The examples are type IIB AdS3 reductions with O5/D5 sources.

conventionDictionary.concept: Overall volume and the symbol ρ
conventionDictionary.conversion: Define r_vol=(vol7)^(1/7). On the left r_vol=√ρ_L, hence ρ_L=(vol7)^(2/7). No equality between the papers' raw ρ symbols is asserted. Image:1 confirms the exponent (10−D)/2.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The string-frame metric contains ρ_L times a unit-volume internal metric; vol7=ρ_L^(7/2) at D=3.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: vol7 is the overall internal volume; individual characteristic lengths are written L_s^a=ρℓ_a, L_s^i=ρℓ_i and L_s^7=ρℓ_7.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Writing L_s=L_E/τ_L on the left and L_s=τ0^(-1)L on the right gives ε_vol=(r_vol/L_s)^2. Thus the left's curvature-to-volume-KK ratio is proportional at scaling order to the square of the inverse hierarchy used on the right.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: ds10²=τ_L^(-2)ds_D²+ρ_L ds̃_internal² and m_KK,vol²∼ρ_L^(-1)τ_L^(-2).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: L_s=τ0^(-1)L is the external ten-dimensional length; restricted separation means L_s≫(vol7)^(1/7).

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use positive curvature magnitudes and dimensionless length ratios. Match |V|∼L_E^(-2) only at scaling order; no numerical equality of the two potential conventions is required.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The Einstein-frame action contains R_D−V and sets M_Pl=1. Equation (3.4) retains the signed source coefficient; the separation criterion uses its magnitude.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: For the inherited AdS3 pair, equation (4.7) gives L²=−2/V0 with V0<0.

conventionDictionary.conversion: For p=5, the left's expression becomes |T5,eff|g_s/ρ_L. Applying it to the right would require evaluating the shape-dependent source contribution and establishing |V0|∼|V_O5|. Fixed net charge alone supplies neither check. This conversion is not invoked by the chosen analogy.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Orientifold multiplicities do not scale in the stated ansatz, but other moduli turn the potential prefactors into functions.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (4.10) fixes (2πℓ_s)²(2N_O5−N_D5)=3a³ while equation (4.11) exhibits parametrically changing shape.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Do not identify the tilded fluxes across papers or equate exterior closedness with an open-string correction. Images:3 and :6 verify these distinct definitions.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Tildes factor out breathing-modulus dependence using the unit-volume metric. The closed/non-closed superscripts in equation (4.10) instead distinguish exterior derivatives.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Tilded RR strengths include open-string corrections needed by the modified Bianchi identities; for example f̃1=gψ³.

limitations: A stronger theorem-application relation would require the right's evaluated O5/D5 potential, its shape dependence, and its asymptotic ratio to V0. The supplied fixed tadpole does not provide that information; this stronger claim is excluded. Evidence: eda53411e0702e9a08c8:p0008s001, eda53411e0702e9a08c8:p0013s001, eb14a666a2878613c181:p0035s001.

The right explicitly leaves physical KK decoupling and higher-dimensional stability to a future spectrum calculation; the seventh characteristic direction being comparable to the external scale does not by itself establish an allowed light KK eigenmode. Evidence: eb14a666a2878613c181:p0038s002; image:5.

The comparison accepts the reported vacuum families and their flux scalings as source inputs. It does not reproduce their complete critical-point equations, mass spectra, global flux quantization, or localization. Evidence: eb14a666a2878613c181:p0035s001, eb14a666a2878613c181:p0036s002, eb14a666a2878613c181:p0038s003.
Only the supplied page subset and six attached images were checked. Earlier record-validation and coverage labels were not treated as scientific certification.

endpoints.text: At U=V=ξ=χ=0, arbitrary constant axion and dilaton and otherwise trivial fields give a unit-radius AdS5 vacuum. Its uplift is supersymmetric AdS5 × SE5, preserving eight supercharges and spontaneously breaking the five-dimensional N=4 supersymmetry to N=2.

M5 twists on negatively curved surfaces yield smooth eleven-dimensional warped AdS5 solutions preserving N=2 or N=1 supersymmetry. The N=2 solution includes an explicit AdS7-to-AdS5×Σ flow at C₁=0; reported holographic central charges scale as N³(g−1).

records.exactAssertion: The left vacuum is an analogous example to the right AdS5 fixed points: each is reported as a supersymmetric AdS5 solution described through gauged supergravity and uplifted to higher-dimensional supergravity. The left-to-right relation is restricted to this construction pattern. It asserts no equivalence, specialization, use of the other endpoint's method, shared truncation or supersymmetry-breaking mechanism, and no transfer of the right AdS7 flow or N³(g−1) central-charge scaling.

intersection.statement: The common descriptive regime is supersymmetric AdS5 solutions represented in gauged supergravity and uplifted to higher-dimensional supergravity. This establishes a common construction pattern, not a shared solution or effective theory.
Both constructions admit four-dimensional SCFT interpretations. The left SE5 family is described as dual to four-dimensional N=1 SCFTs; the right includes four-dimensional N=1 and N=2 branches.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the comparison to the specified left supersymmetric vacuum and the right negatively curved M5 branches at their AdS5 fixed points.
Interpret each supersymmetry label in its stated spacetime dimension; do not identify the two occurrences of N=2.
Use the reported supergravity regime. Treat the right central charges as supergravity, large-N results, without asserting quantum-exact conformality.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left passage explicitly specifies U=V=ξ=χ=0, constant axion and dilaton, otherwise trivial retained fields, and a supersymmetric unit-radius AdS5 vacuum; image:1 confirms these statements.
The right passages specify κ=1 for H2, the N=2 fixed point and C1=0 flow, and the N=1 fixed point. Image:3 confirms the N=2 equations and image:4 confirms the distinct twist assignments.
The supplied text distinguishes left five-dimensional supersymmetry from right four-dimensional supersymmetry, allowing the analogy without assuming equal supercharge counts.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left uses five-dimensional gauged supergravity and a ten-dimensional type IIB AdS5×SE5 uplift. The right uses seven-dimensional SO(5) gauged supergravity and an eleven-dimensional warped AdS5 compactification with six internal dimensions.

The left reports spontaneous partial breaking of five-dimensional N=4 to N=2. The right selects different M5 twists preserving four-dimensional N=2 or N=1; the supplied evidence does not identify these mechanisms.
The assigned left assertion is a vacuum statement. The AdS7-to-AdS5×Σ flow and N³(g−1) central-charge scaling belong to the right construction and cannot be transferred through this analogy.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Match only the presence of a supersymmetric AdS5 factor and a lower-dimensional gauged-supergravity description. No identification of the internal manifolds or higher-dimensional theories is made.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: A D=5 gauged-supergravity vacuum uplifts to type IIB in D=10 on AdS5×SE5.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: A D=7 SO(5) gauged-supergravity construction uplifts to D=11; the AdS5 warp factor depends on a six-dimensional internal space.

conventionDictionary.conversion: The left five-dimensional N=2 label is not the right four-dimensional N=2 label. The supplied left SCFT interpretation has four-dimensional N=1, matching only the boundary supersymmetry label of the right N=1 branch.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The source reports eight preserved supercharges and spontaneous D=5 N=4→N=2 breaking; image:1 confirms the wording.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: N=2 and N=1 denote supersymmetry in four-dimensional notation. The N=1 field theory has four supercharges.

conventionDictionary.conversion: No scalar-field map is asserted. In particular, the left axion a is not a right twist coefficient, and the two fields denoted φ are not identified.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: a=C(0) and φ=Φ are the IIB axion and dilaton. U,V,ξ,χ vanish at the chosen vacuum. Σ=e^{−2(U+V)/3} is a scalar redefinition, confirmed in image:2.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: λ=λ2 with 3λ2+2λ1=0 in the N=2 branch; λ1=λ2=−φ/2 in the N=1 branch. These are seven-dimensional scalar combinations. Σg denotes a Riemann surface.

conventionDictionary.concept: Curvature sign, twist coefficients, and trivial fields
conventionDictionary.conversion: Keep the curvature sign and twist weights specific to the right construction. Vanishing left retained fluctuations does not mean vanishing higher-dimensional supporting flux.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Other retained fields are trivial at the vacuum; background five-form flux is part of the SE5 gauging construction.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: κ=+1 means H2 and κ=−1 means S2. The twist potentials have A_x^(1)=a/y and A_x^(2)=b/y, with a+b=1/4. N=2 uses (a,b)=(1/4,0); N=1 uses (1/8,1/8), as confirmed by image:4.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Unit-radius metric conventions do not establish equality of physical radii, Newton constants, or actions across the constructions. No cross-theory Weyl rescaling or unit conversion is needed for the restricted analogy.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The displayed D=5 action has an Einstein gravitational term. The chosen AdS5 radius is one; the gauge-coupling convention g=1 is stated on physical page 17.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Section 4 sets the AdS7 radius to one. Equation (26) uses a unit-radius AdS5 reference metric inside the eleven-dimensional warped metric. Equation (101) keeps R_AdS5 and G_N^5 explicit.

conventionDictionary.conversion: For clarity, denote the right genus by h and its radial metric function by γ(r), both called g in the source. Then c=(8/3)(h−1)e^{2γ+3f0}N_M5³. This is a notation change within the right construction, not a map to the left.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: N in the assigned vacuum assertion labels supersymmetry; that assertion supplies no central charge or M5-brane number.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: N in equation (102) counts M5 branes; g−1 uses the surface genus, whereas g in e^{2g+3f0} is the metric function. f=f0−log r and c=πR_AdS5³/(8G_N^5), normalized to c=N²/4 for N=4 U(N) SYM. Image:4 resolves the N=1 prefactor as 27/2^8.

limitations: The relation is a reconstructed comparison of source-reported constructions, not a relation asserted by either paper. Upstream node labels and earlier reviewers' assertions were not used as scientific premises.

The left vacuum's full field equations, ten-dimensional uplift substitution, and Killing-spinor equations were not independently reproduced. Its specified values and supersymmetry are directly reported on physical page 17, confirmed by image:1. The omitted SE5 formulas (3.1), (3.4), and (3.12) would be relevant to that excluded stronger verification.

The right fixed-point algebra and central-charge prefactors were checked, but the full interpolating solution, global smoothness, complete eleven-dimensional fluxes, and full Killing-spinor calculation were not reproduced; their reported scope is supplied in 5f1a711a8f88239ec4a3:p0018s001, p0019s001, and p0020s001.

No duality, action map, flux-normalization map, or Newton-constant matching between these IIB and M-theory constructions is established. Such data would be needed for the explicitly excluded equivalence or quantitative-support claims.
The right paper leaves quantum corrections to conformality open (5f1a711a8f88239ec4a3:p0020s002). The central-charge check does not establish finite-N exactness.

Image:2 concerns the HK4×S1 scalar parametrization; its use is limited to notation, also supplied for the SE5 action in e024273dd196411df131:p0016s001. Image:5 equation (1) belongs to a D3 twisting example (5f1a711a8f88239ec4a3:p0007s001), so it was not used to set the M5 twist coefficients.

endpoints.text: For 3D forward scattering, the paper uses M(s)=16A3s², a Cauchy contour integral of M(s)/s³, crossing symmetry and the optical theorem. With the boundary contribution absent, the resulting cross-section integral is nonnegative.

Use crossing-symmetric forward amplitudes, a contour integral of M(s)/s³, Schwarz reflection, a Froissart-bound assumption, and the optical theorem to relate four-derivative coefficients to nonnegative spectral integrals.

records.exactAssertion: The right method uses the left method's single-amplitude forward-dispersion construction at the level of its displayed analytic argument: extract the s² coefficient with ∮ds M/(2πi s³), deform to real-axis cuts with no boundary term, use Schwarz reflection and crossing, and obtain positivity from the optical theorem. For the right projection Q(u,v)=Σu_i v_j u_k v_l C_(ij)(kl), defining a′_eff=Q/4 gives 16a′_eff=4Q=(2/π)∫_{s₀}^∞ds Im M_uv(s)/s³≥0, which has precisely the left construction's form before substituting Im M_L=sσ_L. This is a reconstructed method-use relation under the passages' stated analytic and boundedness hypotheses. It excludes a claim of documented historical dependence, equality of physical Wilson coefficients or theories, equality of spectral functions, validation of an unregulated massless limit, 4D applicability, and any charge-to-mass or WGC implication.

intersection.statement: Both constructions concern 3D forward amplitudes and extract their low-energy s² coefficient using the same contour kernel ds/(2πi s³). The right construction first projects the species amplitude onto real product states specified by u and v.

The shared domain is conditional on an analytic coefficient-extraction contour, real-axis discontinuities, crossing, Schwarz reflection, a vanishing contribution at infinity and optical-theorem positivity. The comparison establishes reuse of this construction, without establishing these hypotheses for an arbitrary physical UV completion.

required_assumptions.statement: To apply either dispersion argument, the amplitude must admit the stated low-energy coefficient extraction and contour deformation without an unresolved singularity at the origin. The left supplies a photon-mass regulator prescription; the right uses a Taylor expansion and separated thresholds. Their physical regulator limits are not equated.

The large-circle integral of M(s)/s³ must vanish. Both passages invoke Froissart behavior for this purpose; the relation retains this as a hypothesis rather than independently deriving UV boundedness.
The selected amplitude must obey Schwarz reflection and forward crossing, so that its negative-cut contribution equals its positive-cut contribution.

Optical-theorem intermediate-state weights must be nonnegative. On the right, u and v are real unit vectors, so contraction of the optical theorem produces an absolute square for each intermediate state.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The displayed equations establish that both sources actually choose forward amplitudes, the s⁻³ contour kernel and an s² residue. Images image:1 and image:4 confirm the respective factors 16 and 4.

Both passages explicitly perform the same crossing reduction and invoke optical-theorem positivity. Images image:2 and image:5 confirm the common factor 2/π and the right-hand spectral denominator s³. This establishes the method comparison, not physical verification of the assumed amplitude properties.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left treats one photon, represented by a scalar dual; the right treats N photons and an entire family of species projections. Image image:3 confirms that multiple photons are future work in the left paper. The left inequality alone therefore does not establish the full right family.

The left expresses its spectral weight through a total cross-section, whereas the right keeps an imaginary amplitude and intermediate-state products. Their positivity mechanisms coincide without identifying numerical cross-sections between different theories.

conventionDictionary.concept: Printed left coefficient and endpoint alias
conventionDictionary.conversion: Use a′ for the printed source coefficient. A3 in the node is an endpoint label; the extracted a0 glyph is not a distinct coefficient. Image image:1, Eq. (2.15), and image:2, Eq. (2.18), resolve the prime.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: No original a′ symbol is required on the right.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Q(u,v)=Σ_ijkl u_i v_j u_k v_l C_(ij)(kl); the residue is 4Q, as printed in image:4, Eq. (2.31).

The right definition compensates its mostly-plus signature with the explicit minus sign. No curvature-sign or gravitational-coupling identification is needed for the contour comparison.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Three spacetime dimensions, mostly-plus signature and s=−(k₁+k₂)². The vectors u and v carry species indices and are unrelated to the Mandelstam variable u.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both use I[M]=∮ds M(s)/(2πi s³) and Disc M=M(s+iε)−M(s−iε)=2i Im M. Their s₀ values have corresponding threshold roles but need not be numerically equal.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: s₀ is the squared lowest energy at which nonanalyticity appears; the contour and IR expansion presume the stated separation from the origin.

(2.35); image:5 confirms the absolute-square glyph in Eq. (2.36), whose displayed formula does not repeat that sum.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: 2 Im M_ij,kl=Σ_n M_ij→n M*_kl→n; real product-state contraction supplies positivity.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Dimensional reconstruction from the canonical Maxwell actions and displayed amplitudes gives [s]=[s₀]=2, [a′]=[Q]=[C]=−3, [M]=1 and [σ_L]=−1. Thus both dispersion integrals have dimension −3. No numerical conversion between Planck conventions or charge-to-mass ratios is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Natural units include 4πG=ε₀=1. The source explicitly gives [M]=1 and [σ]=−1 in 3D.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M₃ is retained explicitly, the Maxwell kinetic term is canonically normalized, and C multiplies four field strengths. Image:6 confirms the action normalization.

limitations: This comparison checks the supplied contour identities and their algebraic composition. It does not establish full-paper mathematical correctness or the existence of a UV completion satisfying the dispersion hypotheses.

The asserted relation is mathematical method reuse, not a claim that the right paper explicitly attributes this particular contour argument to the left paper. No bibliography identification is inferred.

The comparison uses Q exactly as displayed in Eq. (2.31). A componentwise Wilson-coefficient identification would additionally require the explicit pair-symmetrization convention and the dual-action normalization referenced by right Eq. (2.15); that stronger identification is excluded.

The left reports a photon-mass regulator prescription, while the supplied right analyticity passage does not establish a corresponding regulator-removal argument. Equality or validity of unregulated massless amplitudes is excluded.

No loop matching, charge normalization, gravitational normalization, spectrum bound, tower claim, or 4D argument is reproduced. Earlier reviews and node labels supply no independent scientific premises.

endpoints.text: For α<1, the authors infer that the dilatonic weak gravity threshold is also necessary: below it, condensed branches encounter singularities, and the numerical singular curves approach q/q_W=1. Explicit examples use α=1/√3 and α=0.9; necessity for α>1 is not established.

Using the horizon-complement prescription, the authors propose the usual dilatonic inequality q²e^(2αφ₀)>(1+α²)m² for α>1/√3, with curvature-dependent replacements at the critical coupling and in small-α AdS. For 0<α<1/√3 in dS they tentatively suggest the complex-metric threshold q²e^(2αφ₀)>m²/(1−α²), explicitly requiring further investigation.

records.exactAssertion: At the explicitly sampled α=0.9, the left numerical necessity inference provides an analogy to the right AdS horizon-complement WGC proposal: each singles out the factor √(1+α²), and each relates its threshold to a boundary involving singular solutions. Their respective squared boundary coefficients are q_W²/Δ_L²=1.81 and (q_R²e^(2αφ₀)/m_R²)_boundary=1.81. The analogy concerns coupling dependence and boundary reasoning only. It excludes equivalence or mutual validation of physical bounds, identification of Δ_L with m_R or of individual charges, a common dynamical solution family, and the right critical-coupling, small-α and dS extensions.

intersection.statement: Both discuss four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity in AdS. The reported coupling ranges overlap for 1/√3<α<1; the concrete numerical example used here is α=0.9. This is an intersection of settings and parameter labels, not an established common solution family.

required_assumptions.statement: Restrict the comparison to α=0.9 and the right AdS branch above 1/√3. Compare the coefficient of each source's own energy or mass denominator, without identifying those denominators or the individual charges.

Retain the epistemic distinction: the left is a numerical necessity inference for a boundary-driven construction; the right is a conjectured assignment of WGC states to the complement of a black-hole region.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: Figure 5 explicitly includes α=0.9 and Δ=2. Since 0.9²=0.81>1/3, this example falls within the right AdS regime whose horizon boundary is Eq. (96).

The displayed left threshold has q_W²=(1+α²)Δ². The right horizon boundary has Q²e^(2αφ₀)=(1+α²)M², and its WGC prescription reverses the black-hole inequality. These establish the common coefficient without a physical charge/mass dictionary.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left action has a constant cosmological term +6 and no nonconstant neutral-dilaton potential. The right studies a nontrivial V(φ). Matching the Maxwell-dilaton kinetic terms does not establish the same theory.

The left denominator Δ is an AdS scalar normal-mode energy/conformal dimension; its sampled Δ=2 has scalar mass parameter m²=-2. The right horizon-complement inequality uses mass, while its auxiliary particle analysis permits a field-dependent m(φ). No identification Δ=m is made.

The left studies boundary-driven condensate branches and explicitly says its examples contain no black holes. The right classifies horizons of spherical black-hole solutions. Their regularity boundaries have different physical meanings.

The left uses an inclusive q≥q_W threshold. The right proposes a strict superextremal inequality and changes its horizon criterion at and below α=1/√3. Its small-α dS suggestion is explicitly tentative. Only boundary coefficients at α=0.9 are compared.

conventionDictionary.concept: Dimension, gravitational normalization and dilaton coupling
conventionDictionary.conversion: The displayed normalizations match through κ²=8πG, so 1/(2κ²)=1/(16πG). The shared kinetic convention permits comparing the numerical α label; it does not match scalar potentials. Image:3 confirms the left kinetic coefficients and +6 term.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Four-dimensional action with prefactor 1/(16πG), terms R+6-2(∂φ)²-e^(-2αφ)F²; α≥0 can be selected by the stated symmetry.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Four-dimensional action with prefactor 1/(2κ²), terms R-2(∂φ)²-e^(-2αφ)F²-V(φ).

conventionDictionary.conversion: No physical conversion Δ_L=m_R is asserted. Rearranging the left relation gives m_L²=Δ_L(Δ_L-3), hence Δ_L=2 gives m_L²=-2 in its displayed AdS units. The analogy compares coefficients multiplying Δ_L² and m_R² separately.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: Δ_L=3/2+√(9/4+m_L²) is the minimum scalar frequency in the displayed AdS convention and the dual operator dimension.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: m_R is the particle mass used in the WGC inequality; the worldline discussion allows m_R(φ), with mass and charge in geometrized units.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Image:6 resolves the worldline coefficient as √(4πG)gq_R and confirms g=e^(αφ₀). A physical identification q_L=q_R is not established. Signs of A_t and charge need not be matched for this comparison of squared thresholds.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: q_L enters D_a=∇_a-iq_LA_a. The asymptotically flat motivating solution uses A_t=Q_L/r.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The worldline charge couples through √(4πG)gq_RA_μẋ^μ, with A_t=-gQ_R/(√(4πG)r); its Coulomb term is -e^(2αφ₀)q_RQ_R/r.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare dimensionless threshold coefficients in each source's own units. Image:6 confirms that the upper minus sign is dS and the lower plus sign is AdS. No conversion between individual dimensionful particle parameters is used.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The action R+6 and frequency formula are written in fixed AdS-radius units.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: H=1/L is the inverse AdS scale; Eq. (61) uses ∓H²r² times the dilatonic factor for dS/AdS respectively.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare the squared boundary coefficients K_L²=q_W²/Δ_L² and K_R²=(q_R²e^(2αφ₀)/m_R²)_boundary, with nonzero denominators. At α=0.9 both coefficients are 1+0.9²=1.81. This is a formal coefficient comparison, not a state or theory identification.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: q_W=Δ_L√(1+α²), with reported censorship preservation at q_L≥q_W. Figure 5 plots q_L/q_W.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: For AdS α>1/√3, the black-hole boundary is Q_R²e^(2αφ₀)=(1+α²)M_R²; the particle WGC prescription selects the strict opposite side.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Only the role of a singular/regular solution boundary in motivating a charge threshold is analogous. A disappearing black-hole horizon is not identified with the obstruction to continuing the left condensate branch.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: A singular obstruction to smooth condensed solutions as the boundary amplitude a is increased.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: A boundary in black-hole parameter space where the event horizon meets the singular surface, used to motivate a complementary WGC region.

limitations: The left necessity statement is the authors' inference from numerical branches and an apparent approach toward q/q_W=1. The supplied finite plots do not prove the infinite-amplitude limit or exhaust all possible evolutions (81e90d90727ad688e2db:p0011s001; 81e90d90727ad688e2db:p0011s002; 81e90d90727ad688e2db:p0012s001).

Equivalence or physical support would require a compatible potential, matter coupling, boundary conditions and charge/energy dictionary. The right Section 2 potential Eq. (4) and full solution Eq. (8), together with the left Sections 3.2–3.3 boundary data, would be relevant to that excluded stronger comparison. endpoints.text: The controlled highly charged limit yields d₀>0. The extremality calculation gives Δz=2d₀/(5m²)>0, so extremal charge-to-mass ratios approach unity from above with increasing mass. The authors infer superextremal smaller black-hole states and kinematically allowed decays satisfying the WGC under their assumptions.

The authors claim that electrically charged BPS states become extremal at infinite-distance limits of the complex-structure moduli space. For single-charge states, the displayed large-complex-structure relation is between inverse gauge kinetic entries and mass squared, leading to equality of dilatonic and BPS charge-to-mass factors. Multicharge states require the full BPS flow. The general Hodge-theoretic proof is announced but not supplied in this window.

records.exactAssertion: The left-to-right relation is analogy_only at the level of the displayed, source-reported arguments: both use black-hole extremality to interpret WGC-compatible charge-to-mass data. The left reports an outward finite-mass correction relative to the Einstein-Maxwell RN benchmark; the right reports BPS saturation of a scalar-dependent extremality threshold. This assertion excludes a derivation of either endpoint from the other, transfer of the entropy method, numerical equivalence, a shared controlled solution, physical state-population claims and a contradiction between the positive shift and BPS saturation.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use separate labels c_iᴸ and c_iᴿ. No coefficient identification or field-redefinition map is established. conventionDictionary.right_definition: Equation (B.14) has R/(2κ²)−F²/4 plus nine operators: three curvature-squared terms, RF², Ricci-FF, Riemann-FF, (F²)² and two derivative-of-F contractions. In particular c₂ᴿ multiplies R_{μν}R^{μν}.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both displayed metric conventions have negative time component, but a common higher-derivative field frame, time normalization and gauge normalization have not been matched. Removing the cosmological term from a metric does not by itself establish a limit of the AdS orbit/CFT calculation.

records.exactAssertion: Restricted to its unwarped, untwisted DGKT baseline in Section 2, the left endpoint implements the direct-reduction and kinetic-normalized fluctuation method exhibited by the right endpoint's bulk calculation: reduce the massive IIA flux/O6 action, obtain the scalar potential and kinetic terms, impose a critical point, and extract scalar masses using those kinetic terms. This uses_method edge concerns that shared procedure only. It excludes numerical equality of the actions or spectra, the blow-up sector, the warped extensions, and any assertion that left repeats right's particular external-four-form elimination.

The comparison uses the left paper's unwarped, smeared DGKT baseline and the right paper's bulk zero-mode approximation. It does not extend to localized warped profiles.

endpoints.text: The imported WGC asserts that a consistent gravitational theory with an Abelian force contains a state satisfying q>m/mPl. Extremal-black-hole discharge motivates this requirement; it is an assumed conjecture underlying the paper's naturalness conclusions.

ModMax coupled to Einstein gravity has mass-independent extremal Z̄. It therefore lacks any strictly decreasing discrete subset and fails the necessary decay condition, leading to conditional incompatibility with the black-hole WGC despite its shifted charge-to-mass normalization.

records.exactAssertion: The right endpoint is a kinematic analogue of the extremal-black-hole discharge motivation underlying the left endpoint: additive charge conservation and a strict final-rest-mass deficit require at least one charged product with charge-to-mass ratio, or norm, greater than the parent's. In the reported fixed-γ ModMax black-hole family, all offspring black holes have norm at most the parent's constant exp(γ), obstructing such decay. In the left argument, decay of the reference extremal black hole into particles instead requires a particle with z_i > 1. The right-to-left direction identifies this comparison, not a logical implication. This assertion excludes equivalence of the two WGC statements, proof or specialization of the particle conjecture, a contradiction between the endpoints, added charged matter, and marginal fragmentation without mass dissipation.

intersection.statement: Both arguments impose additive conserved charge and a strict deficit between total daughter rest mass and parent mass. They therefore compare the parent's charge-to-mass ratio with a weighted sum of daughter ratios whose nonnegative weights sum to less than one.

The intersection is a kinematic requirement for extremal-black-hole discharge: at least one charged product must exceed the parent's charge-to-mass ratio, or its norm. The comparison does not require a common absolute charge normalization.

required_assumptions.statement: Use the respective source conservation equations, positive daughter masses, nonnegative mass fractions, and strict total daughter mass below the parent mass.
Use the right paper's definition of decay, which excludes the marginal configuration with no mass dissipation.
Hold the ModMax parameter γ fixed within one theory and use the reported extremality surface, whose charge-to-mass norm is the positive constant C = exp(γ).

Restrict the right-hand decay comparison to charge-bearing offspring black holes bounded by that same extremality surface. Additional charged elementary matter is not included in this restricted assertion.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left source explicitly derives its particle bound from charge conservation and a strict final-rest-mass inequality. Image:2 confirms the single-species argument; image:3 confirms the mass-fraction formulation.

The supplied appendix explicitly supplies the strict mass-fraction condition, the exclusion of zero-dissipation fragmentation, and the vector charge-conservation equation. Image:5 confirms the vector equation.
The model definition specifies γ > 0. Image:4 confirms both the reported constant extremal ratio exp(γ) and its zero mass derivative.

The right source explicitly discusses the photon-and-graviton setting with black-hole offspring, bounds offspring ratios by their extremality values, and includes electric and magnetic charges in the charge vector.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left endpoint is a conjectural existence requirement for a charged state, motivated through decay into particles. The right endpoint is a model-specific obstruction to decay into black holes under the black-hole WGC hypothesis. Their conclusions have different quantifiers and different final-state spectra.

ModMax at fixed nonzero γ does not approach Maxwell by reducing field strength. The right paper expressly rejects applying the absolute EFT criterion Z̄ > 1 to this model. Its reported Z̄ = exp(γ) > 1 therefore does not supply the particle state required by the left endpoint.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Keep the two definitions separate. For the algebraic comparison, divide each ratio by its own parent extremality value: C_L = 1 and C_R = exp(γ). Both extremal parents then have normalized ratio one. This positive, fixed rescaling preserves the relevant inequalities.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: z_i = q_i mPl/m_i for particles and Z_L = Q_L mPl/M for a black hole. The Planck mass is defined so that the reference extremal black hole has Z_L = 1; image:1 resolves the footnote.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Z_R = √2 Q°/(κ M°), with bars denoting extremality. In ModMax the extremal norm is C_R = exp(γ).

conventionDictionary.conversion: No numerical identification of q_i with Q_e or Q_m, or of mPl with √2/κ, is established or required for this analogy. No SI or Newton-constant conversion is used.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The displayed scalar-QED kinetic term is −F²/4 and Dμ = ∂μ + iqAμ. mPl is specified by extremal saturation rather than by an explicit supplied formula in Newton's constant.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: The ModMax Lagrangian contains a factor 1/e², while its physical black-hole ratio is defined using κ and charges at infinity.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use each source's masses in its own conservation equation. No frame transformation or identification of the two black-hole solution families is performed.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: m_i is the physical particle mass; the source evaluates the running particle ratio at that mass. M is the parent black-hole mass in the discharge argument.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: M° and Q° are physical mass and charge computed at spatial infinity in asymptotically flat spacetime.

conventionDictionary.conversion: For the left single-species calculation choose particle charge with the parent's sign. For the right calculation use the vector norm and triangle inequality; daughter charge directions need not align.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: The charge vector includes electric and magnetic components, Q = (Q_e, Q_m), and extremality is |Z| = Z̄; image:5 confirms these definitions.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Both sets of weights are nonnegative rest-mass fractions. Their sum is strictly below one in the decay problem being compared.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: σ_i = M_i/M_0, with Z_0 = Σ_i σ_i Z_i and Σ_i σ_i < 1. Zero-dissipation marginal fragmentation is excluded.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Compare a daughter with its parent, rather than treating the number one as a universal threshold across the two theories.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: The required particle has z_i > 1 relative to the reference extremal black hole.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: Offspring black holes are bounded by their own extremality surface. In fixed-γ ModMax their norm is at most exp(γ), equal to the extremal parent's norm.

endpoints.text: Analyze closure of the discrete orientifold/orbifold group. Separately, contract the smeared Einstein equations along parallel and transverse directions and combine them with flux index restrictions from form equations and Bianchi identities.

Build larger finite orbifold groups preserving the lattice, metric, and Maurer–Cartan equations. Their invariant forms determine scalar projections; analyze orientifold conjugacy classes, fixed loci, and a local A₁ blow-up to interpret the altered O-plane geometry.

records.exactAssertion: Restricted to discrete geometric compatibility, the right endpoint uses the normalizer/closure submethod implemented by the left endpoint: an involution must normalize the chosen orbifold group modulo lattice identifications. Right Eq. (4.22) states this test, and Eq. (4.23) applies its coset-conjugation form; left Eqs. (4.18)–(4.22) implement it for <Q>. This reconstructed method-use relation excludes bibliographic attribution, equivalence of the complete methods or compactifications, use of the left Einstein-equation obstruction, and transfer of blow-up smoothness, holographic or full string-consistency conclusions.

intersection.statement: Both methods test compatibility of an involution with a finite geometric orbifold action, with equalities understood modulo the compactification lattice. The common test is preservation of the orbifold subgroup under conjugation.

required_assumptions.statement: Perform group manipulations on the induced transformations of the compact covering space, after imposing its lattice identifications; sigma is an involution there.
Keep the chosen orbifold subgroup fixed when testing compatibility. Closure after enlarging that subgroup is a different quotient construction.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The left supplies the lattice-dependent relations, sigma squared equal to identity, and independent commuting order-three generators S and Qtilde. It explicitly suppresses the other generator T in this calculation.

The right specifies finite lattice actions, records the extra x7 shifts required by its nilmanifold lattice, calls sigma an orientifold involution, and requires g and g-prime in Eq. (4.22) to belong to the orbifold group.

scope_mismatches.statement: The concrete groups and spaces differ: the left tests an order-three subgroup on a six-torus, whereas the right constructs a group containing an order-eight dihedral subgroup on a seven-dimensional nilmanifold compactification. No isomorphism of their complete constructions is asserted.

The left's separate smeared Einstein-equation obstruction assumes an O6 configuration, Ricci-flatness, transverse H3 and a global parallel/transverse split. The right's displayed example is an AdS3 type-IIB construction with O5 sources and F3/F7 flux. Transfer of that obstruction is excluded.

The blow-up conclusions concern different local geometries. The right reports overlap on the A1 exceptional divisor; the left reports a smooth local O6 locus after correcting its involution. These are not identified as the same geometric result.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Use a common abstract compact covering space X and its finite transformation group Gamma. Equality means equality of induced maps on X, including all lattice identifications; no coordinate or length conversion between the examples is asserted.
conventionDictionary.left_definition: X is T6 with complex coordinates Zm identified under shifts by 1 and alpha, alpha = exp(i*pi/3).
conventionDictionary.right_definition: X is a lattice quotient of a group manifold; the displayed AdS3 example uses Nil3 times T4. Its coordinates have period 2, with additional x7 shifts accompanying certain shifts in x1 and x2.

conventionDictionary.left_definition: alpha = exp(i*pi/3) is a complex phase entering Qtilde and the lattice.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: alpha is an order-two affine orbifold generator that does not commute with tau.

conventionDictionary.conversion: Represent both by an involutive map sigma on X. The left signs label the geometric maps, with no corresponding sign choice assigned to the right. Image:1 confirms the signs and Eq. (4.18).
conventionDictionary.left_definition: sigma-minus(Zm) = -conjugate(Zm), sigma-plus(Zm) = conjugate(Zm), and sigma squared is identity modulo the lattice.
conventionDictionary.right_definition: sigma is the orientifold involution in Eq. (4.22); sigma times an orbifold element belongs to its orientifold coset.

conventionDictionary.conversion: On X, right Eq. (4.22), g^-1 sigma g = sigma h with h in Gamma for every g in Gamma, is equivalent to sigma Gamma sigma^-1 = Gamma. This is the criterion implemented by the left's closure calculation.

conventionDictionary.right_definition: Eq. (4.22) requires conjugating an orientifold element by an orbifold element to remain in the orientifold coset, modulo the lattice.
